artigos.titulo: Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain
artigos.destaque: A surprising discovery suggests that some early signs of Alzheimer’s disease may begin outside the brain. Using miniature laboratory systems made from human cells, scientists found that genetic mutations associated with inherited Alzheimer’s can disrupt nerve-to-muscle connections without any involvement from the brain or spinal cord. This could help explain why some patients experience changes in balance, walking, and coordination long before memory problems develop.

artigos.titulo: Common osteoporosis drugs linked to 24% lower dementia risk in major study
artigos.destaque: A massive study of more than 120,000 older adults suggests that common osteoporosis drugs may reduce the risk of Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias by up to 24%. The surprising findings raise the possibility that medications already used to strengthen bones could also help protect the aging brain.

artigos.titulo: "I Was Blamed for My Condition-Now I Am Blamed for Its Treatment": The Migration of Obesity Stigma
artigos.autores: Koufakis T, Patoulias D, Conte C et al.
artigos.destaque: Addressing treatment stigma does not require indiscriminate medicalization but rather individualized, evidence-based treatment free from moral judgment. Obesity destigmatization must therefore extend beyond recognition of the disease to acceptance of its treatment.

resumo.texto: Obesity stigma remains a pervasive yet insufficiently recognized social and clinical problem that can compromise healthcare engagement and health outcomes. Over the past decade, substantial efforts have promoted person-first language, respectful representation, and recognition of obesity as a chronic, biologically regulated disease. However, the advent of highly effective obesity pharmacotherapy has made treatment an increasingly prominent target of obesity stigma: People are now blamed not only for having obesity but also for treating it. Although the immediate focus of judgment has evolved, the underlying willpower-based model persists: Weight loss is often considered legitimate only when achieved through unaided personal effort. Emerging evidence indicates that users of obesity medications may be evaluated less favorably than individuals losing weight through lifestyle intervention, while metabolic-bariatric surgery has long been associated with the "easy way out" narrative. Treatment-related stigma may also be present among people living with obesity. It could discourage treatment-seeking and disclosure, influence clinical decision-making, undermine long-term treatment persistence, and reinforce therapeutic inertia and inequalities in care. Addressing treatment stigma does not require indiscriminate medicalization but rather individualized, evidence-based treatment free from moral judgment. Obesity destigmatization must therefore extend beyond recognition of the disease to acceptance of its treatment.

artigos.titulo: Screening for Nutritional Risk in Adults Receiving Obesity Treatment: A Systematic Literature Review of Available Tools and Identification of Conceptual Gaps
artigos.autores: de van der Schueren MAE, Prado CM, Stanford FC et al.
artigos.destaque: Identified tools did not capture key concepts for assessing nutritional risk in adults receiving obesity treatment. Thus, development of new nutrition screening tools is needed to capture these concepts in ways that are actionable for clinicians in general outpatient settings.

resumo.texto: Identify nutrition screening tools used in obesity research and qualitatively assess their appropriateness for evaluating nutritional risk in adults receiving obesity treatment, including with obesity management medications (OMMs) in outpatient clinical settings.

A systematic review of MEDLINE and Embase (29-January-2026) along with relevant conference websites (22-March-2026) targeted published studies in English of non-hospitalized adults with obesity or overweight that used a screening tool for nutritional risk (inadequate dietary intake and/or undernutrition). Studies were manually reviewed and summarized to identify tools. Identified tools were obtained and considered for practical use in outpatient settings (e.g., length, complexity). Practical tools were qualitatively assessed for capture of clinically-informed nutritional risk concepts in obesity treatment (e.g., weight loss, energy intake and gastrointestinal symptoms).

Sixteen studies met inclusion criteria and were summarized. Semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaires (n = 11) and an unavailable nutrition performance questionnaire (n = 1) did not meet practical considerations. Three tools were qualitatively assessed: International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) Nutrition Checklist, Simplified Nutritional Appetite Questionnaire (SNAQ) and Rapid Eating Assessment for Participants-Short Form (REAP-S). Concepts relevant to nutritional risk with obesity treatment were not adequately captured by these identified tools. Notable missing concepts included weight loss, fluid intake, gastrointestinal symptoms, history of bariatric surgery and comorbid conditions.

Identified tools did not capture key concepts for assessing nutritional risk in adults receiving obesity treatment. Thus, development of new nutrition screening tools is needed to capture these concepts in ways that are actionable for clinicians in general outpatient settings.

artigos.titulo: Developing Robust Antiobesity Medication Implementation Approaches to Maximize Population Health: Protocol for the DOMINO Study
artigos.autores: Marks BA, Sales AE, Hsu C et al.
artigos.destaque: This study will generate an empirically derived, partner-driven road map for implementing AOM use. By addressing operational barriers, workflow integration, and patient affordability, DOMINO will produce scalable tools and processes for health systems to optimize obesity care and advance equity in obesity management.

resumo.texto: Despite robust evidence supporting the efficacy of antiobesity medications (AOMs), their use remains limited and inequitable across populations. Patient, provider, and system-level barriers constrain equitable AOM use in eligible persons, limiting the cumulative health benefits realized by eligible patients.

Guided by the tailored implementation for chronic diseases (TICD) framework and implementation mapping (IM), the DOMINO (Developing Robust Antiobesity Medication Implementation Approaches to Maximize Population Health) study aims to identify determinants of AOM use, obtain stakeholder input, and develop an implementation road map to guide payers, health systems, and prescribers in supporting equitable and appropriate clinical use of AOMs.

The DOMINO study begins with a data-driven needs assessment, followed by qualitative interviews to assess contextual factors, and then stakeholder-guided selection of strategies to address barriers and contextual factors, resulting in an IM approach. Aim 1 evaluates AOM prescribing patterns and determinants of use using electronic health record data from 3 southeastern US health systems. Demographic, clinical, and provider characteristics of AOM users and nonusers will be compared. Cox regression will estimate time from first eligible BMI to AOM initiation, incorporating time-varying covariates and calendar-year fixed effects; secondary analyses will assess repeated use, duration, and medication switching. Aim 2 uses the TICD framework to guide approximately 90 semistructured interviews with patients, providers, health system leaders, and payers to identify multilevel barriers and facilitators to AOM adoption. Our analytic approaches will allow for both deductive and inductive insights to identify salient determinants. Aim 3 will use findings from aims 1 and 2 to develop an AOM implementation road map. Determinants will be prioritized by importance and feasibility, mapped to implementation strategies, and refined through advisory panels using acceptability, feasibility, effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, side effects or unintended consequences, safety, and equity criteria to enable future hybrid trial testing.

The DOMINO study was funded in April 2024. Preliminary data obtained prior to submitting the grant application indicated significant variability in the number of AOM users, the number with a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) prescription, and race/ethnicity demographics. Electronic health record (EHR) data extraction from the 3 health systems was completed in April 2026; data cleaning and preparation of analytic datasets are underway. As of August 2026, aim 2 included 40 patient interviews, 5 payer interviews, and 14 provider interviews. Aim 3, including advisory board panels, is anticipated to begin in late 2026. Publication of results is expected by June 2028.

This study will generate an empirically derived, partner-driven road map for implementing AOM use. By addressing operational barriers, workflow integration, and patient affordability, DOMINO will produce scalable tools and processes for health systems to optimize obesity care and advance equity in obesity management.

artigos.titulo: A weight loss fibrotic response in visceral fat is driven by defective lysosome-dependent collagenolysis
artigos.autores: Rebière C, Oliveira A, Dussaud S et al.
artigos.destaque: This suggests that defective ECM degradation, rather than continued ECM production, underlies fibrosis persistence and aggravation during WL. Together, these findings identify impaired collagenolysis as a critical barrier to adipose tissue recovery after WL and suggest that enhancing ECM clearance, rather than inhibiting ECM synthesis, may represent a more effective therapeutic strategy to restore adipose tissue function.

resumo.texto: Obesity induces pathological remodeling of white adipose tissue (WAT), including chronic inflammation and fibrosis, which drive metabolic dysfunction. Although weight loss (WL) is the cornerstone of obesity treatment and improves systemic metabolic health, its effect on WAT remodeling remains incompletely understood. Using a mouse model of diet-induced obesity followed by nutritional WL, we show that visceral WAT (vWAT) failed to fully recover despite normalization of body weight and marked metabolic improvement. Notably, vWAT fibrosis persisted and continued to progress after WL. This occurred while extracellular matrix (ECM) production by adipose progenitor cells was markedly reduced following WL, explaining why pharmacological inhibition of ECM synthesis fails to prevent fibrosis during WL. Instead, we observed impaired collagen degradation by both progenitor cells and macrophages, along with lysosomal dysfunction, during WL. This suggests that defective ECM degradation, rather than continued ECM production, underlies fibrosis persistence and aggravation during WL. Together, these findings identify impaired collagenolysis as a critical barrier to adipose tissue recovery after WL and suggest that enhancing ECM clearance, rather than inhibiting ECM synthesis, may represent a more effective therapeutic strategy to restore adipose tissue function.

artigos.autores: Baidoe-Ansah D, Mayer A, Mattern J et al.
artigos.destaque: Unhealthy nutrition in early life can reduce response to a weight loss drug in adult obesity.

artigos.titulo: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity
artigos.autores: Schnitzer TJ, Hunter DJ, Conaghan PG et al.
artigos.destaque: In participants with painful knee osteoarthritis and obesity, treatment with retatrutide resulted in significantly greater reductions in both the WOMAC pain score and body weight than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-4 and -1 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05931367 and NCT05929066.).

resumo.texto: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for the treatment of painful knee osteoarthritis in persons with obesity.

In two phase 3 trials, adults without diabetes who had painful knee osteoarthritis and a body-mass index of at least 27 were randomly assigned to receive once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide (9 or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-4 and 4, 9, or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-1-OA) or placebo. In TRIUMPH-4, the primary end points were the change in the WOMAC pain score (range, 0 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) and the percent change in body weight at week 68. In TRIUMPH-1-OA, the primary end point was the change in the WOMAC pain score at week 80. For non-pain-related end points, intercurrent events were handled with a treatment-policy strategy. For pain-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events that suggested treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy elsewhere. We also report results for an intention-to-treat (ITT) estimand.

A total of 445 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-4 and 574 in TRIUMPH-1-OA. At 68 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-4 were -3.96 (9 mg) and -3.74 (12 mg), versus -2.12 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.83 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -2.37 to -1.30] and -1.61 [95% CI, -2.16 to -1.07], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -1.70 (95% CI, -2.19 to -1.22) and -1.38 (95% CI, -1.91 to -0.85) (P<0.001 for all comparisons). The mean percent changes in body weight with retatrutide were -20.0% (9 mg) and -23.7% (12 mg), versus -4.6% with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -15.4 percentage points [95% CI, -18.7 to -12.1] and -19.2 percentage points [95% CI, -22.4 to -15.9]; P<0.001 for both comparisons). At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OA were -3.22 (4 mg), -3.48 (9 mg), and -3.64 (12 mg), versus -1.87 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.35 [95% CI, -1.92 to -0.78], -1.61 [95% CI, -2.20 to -1.02], and -1.77 [95% CI, -2.34 to -1.20], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -0.96 (95% CI, -1.61 to -0.30), -1.41 (95% CI, -2.07 to -0.75), and -1.64 (95% CI, -2.26 to -1.02) (P≤0.005 for all comparisons). In both trials, serious adverse events were more common with retatrutide than with placebo, and the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.

In participants with painful knee osteoarthritis and obesity, treatment with retatrutide resulted in significantly greater reductions in both the WOMAC pain score and body weight than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-4 and -1 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05931367 and NCT05929066.).

artigos.titulo: Hemodynamic effects of semaglutide in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial
artigos.autores: Borlaug BA, Jensen MD, Packer M et al.
artigos.destaque: The results from this trial indicate that, in patients with HFpEF and obesity, treatment with semaglutide reduced left heart filling pressures during exercise and at rest and was associated with hemodynamic HFpEF remission in over half of treated patients. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05371496 .

resumo.texto: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide improves symptoms in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) through unclear mechanisms. Here, in this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 81 patients (47 women) with HFpEF and obesity to semaglutide (2.4 mg weekly) or placebo for 52 weeks. The primary outcome was the change in invasively measured pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP), a direct measure of cardiac congestion, during low-intensity exercise. Additional mechanistic outcomes included other hemodynamic measures and hemodynamic HFpEF remission (defined as normal PAWP under conditions of both rest and exercise at 52 weeks). At baseline, PAWP was 17.5 ± 4.3 mmHg at rest and 31.7 ± 5.2 mmHg during exercise. After 52 weeks, the mean change in PAWP during exercise was -9.8 (95% confidence interval (CI): -11.3 to -8.2) mmHg with semaglutide and +0.9 (95% CI: -1.3 to 3.0) mmHg with placebo (estimated difference, -10.6 mmHg; 95% CI: -13.3 to -8.0; P < 0.0001). As compared to placebo, semaglutide also decreased resting PAWP (estimated difference, -7.1 mmHg; 95% CI: -9.8 to -4.4; P < 0.0001), and semaglutide-treated patients were more likely to experience hemodynamic remission (53.7% versus 7.4%, odds ratio = 14.1, 95% CI: 3.0-134.6, P < 0.001). The results from this trial indicate that, in patients with HFpEF and obesity, treatment with semaglutide reduced left heart filling pressures during exercise and at rest and was associated with hemodynamic HFpEF remission in over half of treated patients. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05371496 .

artigos.titulo: Effectiveness and Safety of Once-Weekly Semaglutide 2.4 mg in Korean Adults With Obesity or Overweight: A Multicenter Retrospective Real-World Study (RE-SEMA-K Study)
artigos.autores: Kwon YJ, Kim YS, Ko HJ et al.
artigos.destaque: Semaglutide 2.4 mg achieved substantial weight loss in South Korean adults with overweight or obesity. Weight reduction was comparable to the STEP 6 trial despite shorter follow-up (4.9 months), substantial prior obesity medication exposure, and accelerated dose escalation, supporting robust real-world effectiveness.

resumo.texto: To evaluate the effectiveness and treatment patterns of once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg in South Korean adults with overweight or obesity in real-world practice.

This multicenter retrospective study analysed electronic medical records from 17 centres in South Korea. Included were adults (≥ 19 years) with BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2, or ≥ 23 kg/m2 with obesity-related comorbidities. Primary endpoints were changes in body weight at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. Secondary outcomes included body composition, categorical weight loss, cardiometabolic changes, treatment persistence, safety, and changes in liver function.

Among 1160 patients (40.9% with prior obesity medications), semaglutide treatment induced progressive weight reduction (-5.85%, -9.55%, -11.43%, and -13.16% at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months). Greater reduction occurred in women, younger patients, and those without T2D or prior obesity medication. By 6 months, cardiometabolic, liver function, and body composition parameters improved, with preferential loss of fat over lean mass (all p < 0.001). Starting doses varied across patients (0.25 mg, 55.9%; 0.5 mg, 30.4%; 1.0 mg, 11.9%), with rapid dose escalation reaching the maintenance dose (2.4 mg) in a mean of 3.52 months, reflecting individualised real-world dosing. Mean treatment duration was 4.9 months. Adverse events, predominantly transient gastrointestinal symptoms, occurred in approximately 22% of patients.

Semaglutide 2.4 mg achieved substantial weight loss in South Korean adults with overweight or obesity. Weight reduction was comparable to the STEP 6 trial despite shorter follow-up (4.9 months), substantial prior obesity medication exposure, and accelerated dose escalation, supporting robust real-world effectiveness.

artigos.titulo: GLP-1-Based Therapies Across the Menopausal Transition: Dermatologic Considerations and Practical Management
artigos.autores: Sanchez-Melendez S, Linkner R
artigos.destaque: Dermatologic care should anticipate the overlapping effects of menopause and substantial weight loss. A longitudinal, tissue-preservation approach may shift care from reactive correction toward proactive management.

resumo.texto: Glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies have transformed obesity management. Their growing use among perimenopausal and menopausal women introduces new dermatologic considerations, particularly when weight loss occurs alongside menopause-associated changes in skin, adipose tissue, muscle, bone, and hair.
To provide a practical framework for dermatologic management of perimenopausal and menopausal women receiving glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies.

PubMed was searched from inception through September 2026 for literature on Glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies, menopause, skin aging, lean mass, alopecia, and aesthetic procedures. Reference lists of relevant reviews and consensus statements were also hand-searched. The senior author, a dermatologist and obesity medicine specialist, provides a practice-based perspective.

Key considerations include weight-loss trajectory, lean mass and bone preservation, nutrition, hair changes, procedural timing, and multidisciplinary comanagement. A staged aesthetic approach prioritizes skin quality during active weight loss, with structural correction as weight stabilizes.

Dermatologic care should anticipate the overlapping effects of menopause and substantial weight loss. A longitudinal, tissue-preservation approach may shift care from reactive correction toward proactive management.

artigos.titulo: Physical Performance After Acute Myocardial Infarction: Gait, Frailty, and Cardiovascular Prognosis
artigos.autores: da Luz Goulart C, Franzoni L, Correale L et al.
artigos.destaque: Incorporating gait speed, SPPB, and frailty assessment into conventional risk stratification may improve patient phenotyping and identify individuals requiring more intensive rehabilitation and follow-up. Further prospective studies are needed to standardize assessment strategies and determine whether improving physical performance translates into better cardiovascular outcomes.

resumo.texto: Physical performance and frailty have emerged as potential markers of physiological reserve and cardiovascular vulnerability after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). This review examines the prognostic significance of gait speed, lower-extremity physical performance, frailty, and sarcopenia after AMI and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and discusses their underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical implications.

Slow gait speed, impaired Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores, and frailty are associated with mortality, rehospitalization, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular events after AMI or ACS. Gait speed and SPPB may provide incremental prognostic information beyond conventional cardiovascular risk assessment and established risk scores. These associations may reflect an interconnected cardiac-vascular-muscle axis involving reduced cardiac reserve, vascular dysfunction, impaired skeletal muscle perfusion, sarcopenia, and physical deconditioning. Importantly, emerging evidence suggests that targeted cardiac rehabilitation may improve gait speed, muscle strength, and overall physical performance in vulnerable patients. Physical performance represents a clinically relevant and potentially modifiable dimension of post-AMI cardiovascular vulnerability. Incorporating gait speed, SPPB, and frailty assessment into conventional risk stratification may improve patient phenotyping and identify individuals requiring more intensive rehabilitation and follow-up. Further prospective studies are needed to standardize assessment strategies and determine whether improving physical performance translates into better cardiovascular outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Cytokines and hematological indices as potential markers of low cardiorespiratory fitness and sarcopenia in hemodialysis patients
artigos.autores: Kuo CH, Fang JT, Hsiao CC et al.
artigos.destaque: Elevated IL-10 was independently associated with low HGS - a novel finding - while IL-6 was associated with sarcopenia. RDW emerged as a potential CRF marker. These findings suggest that cytokine and hematological profiling may hold future value for early screening of physical fitness decline in HD patients, pending external validation.

resumo.texto: Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (HD) are prone to low cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), reduced muscle strength, and sarcopenia - conditions that predict poor outcomes but are challenging to assess routinely. This study aimed to identify plasma inflammatory cytokines and hematological parameters associated with physical fitness impairments.

In this cross-sectional study, 61 HD patients and 20 healthy controls underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing, handgrip strength (HGS) measurement, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, cytokine quantification, and blood counts. Low peak oxygen uptake (V̇O2) was defined as < 14 mL/kg/min; low HGS, low appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI), and sarcopenia were defined per Asian Working Group criteria. Associations were analyzed using multivariate binary logistic regression and decision trees.

Compared with controls, HD patients demonstrated impaired physical fitness (56% low peak V̇O2, 36% low HGS, 44% low ASMI, and 21% sarcopenia), anemia, and elevated IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10. Multivariate analysis identified that older age was associated with low peak V̇O2; elevated IL-10 (OR 7.39, p = 0.019) and lower hemoglobin with low HGS; lower BMI with low ASMI; and elevated IL-6 (OR 1.17, p = 0.005) with sarcopenia. Elevated red cell distribution width (RDW) correlated with low peak V̇O2. Decision trees combining cytokines with hematological and demographic parameters showed strong discrimination for low peak V̇O2 (AUC = 0.803) and sarcopenia (AUC = 0.918).

Elevated IL-10 was independently associated with low HGS - a novel finding - while IL-6 was associated with sarcopenia. RDW emerged as a potential CRF marker. These findings suggest that cytokine and hematological profiling may hold future value for early screening of physical fitness decline in HD patients, pending external validation.

artigos.titulo: Knowledge, Perspectives, and Experiences of Women in Kuwait Regarding GLP-1/GIP-Based Medications for Weight Management: A Cross-Sectional Study
artigos.autores: Alharbi M, Alshammari M, Alkazemi A
artigos.destaque: Despite high awareness of GLP-1/GIP-based medications among women in Kuwait, understanding, information sources, and perceptions varied according to medication-use status. Differences in information sources and safety perceptions highlight an opportunity for healthcare professionals to provide accessible, evidence-based medication information and support informed treatment decisions.

resumo.texto: GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists are increasingly used for obesity and type 2 diabetes, alongside growing public and social-media attention. Understanding how women perceive these medications and obtain medication-related information may help healthcare professionals support informed and appropriate use.

A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among women aged ≥18 years living in Kuwait from March to June 2026. The questionnaire assessed medication awareness and knowledge, information sources, attitudes, medication-use experiences, and factors influencing treatment decisions. Previous/current users were compared with participants who had never used the medications or were considering future use using appropriate bivariate statistical tests. Multivariable logistic regression was used for selected information-source and perception outcomes, adjusting for age, BMI, and weight-management intention. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.

Among 445 participants, 132 (29.7%) reported previous/current GLP-1/GIP-based medication use. Awareness was highest for tirzepatide (88.6%) and semaglutide (73.4%), although understanding of medication mechanisms and adverse effects varied. Social media was the most frequently reported information source overall (56.0%); however, previous/current users were substantially more likely than never/considering users to report healthcare professionals as an information source (57.6% vs 10.2%, P < 0.001) and less likely to report social media (38.6% vs 63.3%, P < 0.001). Previous/current users were also less likely to perceive that medication risks outweighed benefits (24.2% vs 59.4%, P < 0.001). These differences persisted after adjustment for age, BMI, and weight-management intention.

Despite high awareness of GLP-1/GIP-based medications among women in Kuwait, understanding, information sources, and perceptions varied according to medication-use status. Differences in information sources and safety perceptions highlight an opportunity for healthcare professionals to provide accessible, evidence-based medication information and support informed treatment decisions.

artigos.titulo: Ensemble-Based Segmental Helical Organization in an Aib-Rich Lipidated Peptide: Biomacromolecular Insights from High-Field NMR
artigos.autores: Nordin N, Choi J, Lee J et al.
artigos.destaque: Structure calculations based on the 1.2 GHz NMR and CD experiments revealed that tirzepatide does not adopt a single rigid conformation in solution but instead exists as a conformational ensemble composed of locally ordered and flexible regions. These findings provide a residue-specific view of tirzepatide dynamics in solution and offer structural insights into the conformational landscape of this therapeutically important peptide.

resumo.texto: Tirzepatide (TZP) is a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that has demonstrated remarkable therapeutic efficacy for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Despite its clinical importance, residue-specific information on its solution conformation remains limited due to its structural complexity, including noncanonical amino acids and a lipidated side chain. In this study, we performed a solution NMR investigation of tirzepatide to establish residue-specific resonance assignments and characterize its conformational properties in an aqueous solution. Backbone and side-chain resonances were assigned using multidimensional NMR spectroscopy, including 1H-15N HMQC, TOCSY, and NOESY experiments. Reliable sequential NOE connectivities were identified for several peptide segments, while ambiguous and unresolved resonances were conservatively excluded from the structural interpretation. The N-terminal Aib2 residue served as an important assignment anchor but did not define a stable terminal structure. In contrast, the Aib13 region exhibited a locally organized backbone environment with a short helical-like conformational tendency, suggesting Aib13-centered local ordering within the peptide chain. Structure calculations based on the 1.2 GHz NMR and CD experiments revealed that tirzepatide does not adopt a single rigid conformation in solution but instead exists as a conformational ensemble composed of locally ordered and flexible regions. These findings provide a residue-specific view of tirzepatide dynamics in solution and offer structural insights into the conformational landscape of this therapeutically important peptide.

artigos.titulo: Administrative Harm and Workforce Strain Indicators
artigos.autores: Leventhal KG, Caudill D, Moss M et al.
artigos.destaque: The way work is structured within health care, from work environments to workloads, shapes both the workforce experience as well as job performance. Administrative harm describes the downstream effects of upstream decisions on the design of work itself, impacting workforce well-being and performance, patient care and outcomes, and organizational outcomes. The article reviews current and emerging opportunities to harness digital signals readily available within the electronic health record (EHR), including EHR use metadata and related data sources, to measure, monitor, and predict how work design (job demands and resources) affects workforce, patient, and organizational outcomes.
