artigos.titulo: Moral Distress, Burnout, and the Intensive Care Unit Environment
artigos.autores: Epstein EG, Bourne D, Taylor JF
artigos.destaque: Over time, unresolved moral distress contributes to chronic workplace stress and burnout. The authors emphasize that system-level interventions, particularly ethics consultation and organizational change, are essential to address root causes and improve clinician well-being and patient care.

resumo.texto: This article examines the relationship between moral distress and burnout among intensive care unit (ICU) clinicians and argues that moral distress acts as a precursor to burnout. Moral distress arises when clinicians cannot act according to ethical obligations due to systemic constraints, leading to cumulative moral residue. In high-intensity ICU environments, this distress is driven by nonbeneficial treatment, poor communication, and resource limitations. Over time, unresolved moral distress contributes to chronic workplace stress and burnout. The authors emphasize that system-level interventions, particularly ethics consultation and organizational change, are essential to address root causes and improve clinician well-being and patient care.

artigos.titulo: Oral Health-Related Quality of Life, Perceived Stress, and Well-Being in Oral Lichen Planus Subtypes
artigos.autores: Stolte KN, Dogan SS, Attia S et al.
artigos.destaque: Patients with OLP reported poorer OHRQoL than healthy controls, whereas differences between reticular and erosive OLP were not significant. The findings suggest that oral-specific and generic patient-reported outcome measures capture complementary aspects of patient experience, with OHIP-G14 reflecting oral disease-specific burden in OLP.

resumo.texto: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory mucosal disease with reticular and erosive clinical subtypes. This study aimed to compare oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL), stress, and general well-being between participants with reticular OLP, erosive OLP, and healthy controls.

In this single-center cross-sectional study, healthy controls (n = 20) and patients with reticular (n = 20) or erosive OLP (n = 20) completed the OHIP-G14, PSS-10, and WHO-5-questionnaires, and group differences were evaluated.

Patients with OLP reported significantly poorer OHRQoL than controls (OHIP-G14 total score: 13.18 ± 10.01 vs. 2.85 ± 6.54; p < 0.001). Significant group differences were observed across all OHIP-G14 subdomains. Erosive OLP showed higher scores than reticular OLP across domains, though subtype differences were not significant. In both OLP groups, the highest mean scores were observed for physical pain and psychological discomfort. No significant between-group differences were observed for PSS-10 or WHO-5 (all p ≥ 0.259). Interpretation is limited by differences in baseline characteristics between groups.

Patients with OLP reported poorer OHRQoL than healthy controls, whereas differences between reticular and erosive OLP were not significant. The findings suggest that oral-specific and generic patient-reported outcome measures capture complementary aspects of patient experience, with OHIP-G14 reflecting oral disease-specific burden in OLP.

artigos.titulo: Workplace Violence Against Physicians in Bangladesh: A Contemporary Systems-Based Narrative Review of Current Evidence
artigos.autores: Sufian MA, Satter NS, Shimul MMH
artigos.destaque: Workplace violence against physicians in Bangladesh is a systems-level occupational, governance, and healthcare-resilience challenge arising from interacting individual, interpersonal, organizational, health-system, and societal conditions. Prevention should extend beyond reactive security measures to workforce strengthening, standardized reporting and accountability, legal protection, occupational support, communication and de-escalation, and public engagement. Future research should prioritize standardized measurement, longitudinal and intervention studies, and underrepresented healthcare settings.

resumo.texto: Workplace violence against physicians is an occupational and public health challenge in resource-constrained healthcare systems. In Bangladesh, physician shortages, overcrowding, service delays, inadequate security, and institutional constraints may increase exposure to clinical environments. This narrative review synthesized evidence on forms, perpetrators, determinants, consequences, institutional responses, and prevention using a systems-based and socio-ecological perspective.

A narrative review was conducted with reference to the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for peer-reviewed publications from January 2022 to May 2026. The primary evidence comprised studies reporting workplace violence among physicians or physician-specific findings in Bangladeshi healthcare settings. Contextual evidence was considered separately to inform interpretation. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Findings were synthesized thematically because methodological heterogeneity precluded quantitative pooling.

Twelve studies constituted the evidence base. Psychological and verbal violence were most common, with patients' relatives or attendants frequently identified as perpetrators. Younger and early-career physicians, emergency department staff, and night-shift workers appeared particularly vulnerable, although demographic associations varied. Recurring determinants included treatment delays, overcrowding, staffing constraints, communication difficulties, inadequate security, weak reporting mechanisms, governance limitations, and health-system pressures. Workplace violence was associated with psychological distress, burnout, reduced job satisfaction, defensive medical practice, workforce instability, and disruption of healthcare delivery. Institutional reporting, investigation, and post-incident support remained inadequate.

Workplace violence against physicians in Bangladesh is a systems-level occupational, governance, and healthcare-resilience challenge arising from interacting individual, interpersonal, organizational, health-system, and societal conditions. Prevention should extend beyond reactive security measures to workforce strengthening, standardized reporting and accountability, legal protection, occupational support, communication and de-escalation, and public engagement. Future research should prioritize standardized measurement, longitudinal and intervention studies, and underrepresented healthcare settings.

artigos.titulo: A National Research Agenda to Advance Physician Well-Being
artigos.autores: Dyrbye LN, Trockel M, Bilimoria K et al.
artigos.destaque: Through this process, the group developed a research agenda focused on four prioritized domains: (1) strengthening causal evidence linking occupational well-being to core system outcomes, (2) evaluating scalable organizational interventions to improve clinician well-being, (3) advancing pragmatic operational strategies for cultivating wellness-centered leadership, and (4) generating evidence to inform optimal interdisciplinary clinical work design. The intent of this research agenda is to define the evidence needed to help accelerate system level action to drive improvement and enhance the long-term stability and performance of the healthcare workforce.

resumo.texto: Physician well-being is increasingly recognized as essential to healthcare system performance, workforce sustainability, and the capacity for organizational change. However, healthcare systems continue to lack sufficiently evaluated, scalable strategies to advance well-being (meaning, purpose, professional fulfillment) and address challenges, including occupational burnout, depression, and workforce retention. In response to persistent gaps in knowledge regarding scalable solutions and organizational action, the Stanford Medicine WellMD & WellPhD Center convened a national Physician Well-Being Think Tank in 2025. The Think Tank brought together well-being researchers, chief wellness officers, and healthcare executives who reviewed current evidence, identified critical knowledge gaps, and completed pre-meeting prioritization activities, voted on high-priority evidence gaps, and engaged in iterative small-group and full-group consensus discussions to develop priorities for future research. Through this process, the group developed a research agenda focused on four prioritized domains: (1) strengthening causal evidence linking occupational well-being to core system outcomes, (2) evaluating scalable organizational interventions to improve clinician well-being, (3) advancing pragmatic operational strategies for cultivating wellness-centered leadership, and (4) generating evidence to inform optimal interdisciplinary clinical work design. The intent of this research agenda is to define the evidence needed to help accelerate system level action to drive improvement and enhance the long-term stability and performance of the healthcare workforce.

artigos.titulo: Moral Injury in Nursing as a Moral Ecology: A Mid-Range Theory of Professional Moral Identity Alignment
artigos.autores: Norton AH, Rainbow J
artigos.destaque: Seven propositions explain how ecological conditions sustain alignment, generate cumulative misalignment, and contribute to injury or repair. The framework differentiates moral injury from burnout and moral distress and shifts intervention toward structural and relational accountability.

resumo.texto: Moral injury in nursing may develop when persistent structural and relational constraints disrupt nurses' ability to enact professional moral commitments. This article develops the Nursing Moral Ecology Framework, a nursing-specific mid-range theory derived from Copeland's Moral Ecology Framework and informed by a nursing-focused scoping review and a national study of registered nurses (N = 189). Professional moral identity alignment is proposed as the mechanism linking moral ecology to moral injury. Seven propositions explain how ecological conditions sustain alignment, generate cumulative misalignment, and contribute to injury or repair. The framework differentiates moral injury from burnout and moral distress and shifts intervention toward structural and relational accountability.

artigos.titulo: The Impact of Loadshedding on the Psychosocial Well-Being of Older Adults in Residential Facilities in South Africa: Implications for Gerontological Social Services
artigos.autores: Wysoke G, Geyer S, Graham MA
artigos.destaque: The experiences reported by older adults in residential facilities suggested associations with feelings of stress and loneliness during loadshedding. Recommendations for individual psychosocial support, group support among similarly affected older adults, advocacy, and long-term solutions to secure alternative power supplies that enable older adults to resile amid loadshedding are offered.

resumo.texto: Planned rolling electricity outages in South Africa when electricity demand exceeds supply ("loadshedding") have a multifaceted impact on the population. To the authors' knowledge, the impact of loadshedding on the psychosocial well-being of South African older adults (60+) in residential facilities has not been investigated. The phenomenon was considered from an ecosystem lens. The study aimed to determine the impact of loadshedding on the psychosocial well-being of South African older adults in residential care and provide guidelines for gerontological social services. Quantitative research utilising a cross-sectional design and non-probability sampling was undertaken. Face-to-face surveys were conducted with 68 older adults at five facilities, both public and private, in the Gauteng Province of South Africa. Stress (Perceived Stress Scale), resilience (Brief Resilience Scale), and loneliness (Brief Loneliness Scale) were investigated. Participants reported moderate levels of perceived stress (M = 17.7) and moderate feelings of loneliness (M = 14.7) during loadshedding. A significant proportion of participants (67.6%) reported that loadshedding affected their psychosocial well-being. Participants' resilience scores were within the "normal" range (M = 3.7) regarding loadshedding. The experiences reported by older adults in residential facilities suggested associations with feelings of stress and loneliness during loadshedding. Recommendations for individual psychosocial support, group support among similarly affected older adults, advocacy, and long-term solutions to secure alternative power supplies that enable older adults to resile amid loadshedding are offered.

artigos.titulo: Time-dependent efficacy of vitamin D3 against chronic stress-induced behavioral and circadian deficits via the hepatic VDR-clock axis
artigos.autores: Guo Y, Yang T, Xu Y et al.
artigos.destaque: This study is the first to reveal the time-dependent antidepressant effects of VitD3 and identify the VDR-circadian clock axis as the underlying mechanism. These findings highlight the importance of intervention timing for VitD3 efficacy and support precision nutrition strategies aligned with CR for stress disorders.

resumo.texto: Vitamin D3 (VitD3) is an essential fat-soluble micronutrient that protects against chronic stress-related disorders through its neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects. Major depressive disorder is accompanied by circadian rhythm (CR) disruption, and evidence from chrono-nutrition studies suggests that nutrient effects are strongly influenced by administration timing. However, whether VitD3 efficacy against chronic stress depends on intervention timing remains unclear. This study assessed the chrono-nutrition potential of VitD3 in a mouse model of chronic stress. Mice subjected to 4 weeks of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) received daily VitD3 either in the morning (AM) or evening (PM). VitD3 treatment mitigated CUMS-induced behavioral impairments, neuroinflammation, and neuronal damage in a time-dependent manner, with superior outcomes observed with PM administration. PM administration enhanced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, hippocampal integrity, TNF-α levels, sleep duration, and serotonin synthesis. Mechanistically, PM administration more effectively restored hepatic Vdr rhythmic oscillation, coupled with re-synchronization of the core clock network. Genetic validation in Caenorhabditis elegans further supported the essential role of VDR in circadian restoration. This study is the first to reveal the time-dependent antidepressant effects of VitD3 and identify the VDR-circadian clock axis as the underlying mechanism. These findings highlight the importance of intervention timing for VitD3 efficacy and support precision nutrition strategies aligned with CR for stress disorders.

artigos.titulo: Evidence of high rates of burnout symptoms in a cohort with cluster headache
artigos.autores: Jennysdotter Olofsgård F, Ran C, Spulber S et al.
artigos.destaque: Participants with cluster headache in our Swedish cohort reported higher scores for burnout symptoms, particularly during active bout. For participants in remission, the burnout symptoms score was inversely correlated to the number of years since their last active headache bout. When managing cluster headache in a clinical setting, it should be taken into consideration that this patient group has a substantial risk for developing burnout symptoms both in and out of an active bout. Future studies should evaluate how to best support patients with cluster headache handling exhaustion and promote recovery to improve their quality of life.

resumo.texto: Cluster headache is a debilitating primary headache disorder. During active bouts, headache attacks occur daily and can last up to 3 h. Besides the excruciating pain, the disorder can greatly impact a patient's mental health, sleep, and life quality. The reoccurring attacks as well as sleep problems may lead to energy depletion and burnout symptoms, which can limit a person's ability to participate in society to the extent they would like to.

Our aim was to investigate the extent of burnout symptoms in a Swedish cluster headache cohort using a cross-sectional approach. We further wanted to study if burnout symptoms can be linked to disease status-and if sex, lifestyle factors, or any specific clinical characteristics may be linked to change in burnout symptoms.

Between January 2024 and September 2025, the Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire was sent out via the Research Electronic Data Capture platform to 839 study participants with cluster headache. Global scores from the questionnaire were compared between study participants in active bout and remission. Likewise, the scores were analyzed between participants whose remission period had lasted longer than 5 years (long-term) compared to less than 5 years (short-term). Lifestyle and clinical factors were further analyzed in study participants with high Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire scores (global score >3.75).

The total number of individuals included in the analysis was 373/839 (44.5%). Scores above threshold (>3.75) were recorded in 65.9% (58/88) of study participants in an active bout compared to 37.5% (90/240) in the remission group (odds ratio [OR] = 3.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.93-5.38; p < 0.001). Participants in short-term remission similarly had a higher percentage of scores above threshold compared to participants in long-term remission (42.0% [73/174] vs. 22.2% [12/54], OR = 2.53, 95% CI = 1.25-5.14; p = 0.009). Participants with burnout scores above 3.75 were more likely to be females (OR = 3.25, 95% CI = 2.04-5.19; pcorrected <0.001) and report sleep deprivation as an attack trigger (OR = 2.24, 95% CI = 1.32-3.82; pcorrected = 0.034).

Participants with cluster headache in our Swedish cohort reported higher scores for burnout symptoms, particularly during active bout. For participants in remission, the burnout symptoms score was inversely correlated to the number of years since their last active headache bout. When managing cluster headache in a clinical setting, it should be taken into consideration that this patient group has a substantial risk for developing burnout symptoms both in and out of an active bout. Future studies should evaluate how to best support patients with cluster headache handling exhaustion and promote recovery to improve their quality of life.

artigos.titulo: Burnout in European Paediatric Residents-A Pan European Survey
artigos.autores: Copley S, Karara N, Erdi J et al.
artigos.destaque: Burnout remains a significant issue. Modifiable workplace factors contribute to burnout and are urgent targets for change.

resumo.texto: Recruitment and retention are significant issues in paediatrics. High workload, poor working conditions, and burnout are reported. Burnout is associated with physician ill-health and dissatisfaction at work. Understanding burnout among paediatric residents may aid in supporting doctors' wellbeing and maintaining a sustainable paediatric workforce. We aimed to establish the prevalence of burnout in European paediatric residents and identify associated factors.

A survey was disseminated via SurveyMonkey via the Young European Academy of Paediatrics (YEAP) to residents. Demographic data was collected; burnout was assessed using the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI). Burnout prevalence was calculated, regression analysis performed on potential associated factors, and COVID-19 impact assessed. Content analysis was performed on free text responses.

Two hundred and five residents from 11 countries responded. 60% (124/205) scored as burnt-out (43% primarily personally related, 15% primarily work-related or patient related). Thirty-nine percent considered quitting paediatric training. Scoring as burnt-out was associated with lack of training flexibility, working over 40 h/week and 24-h oncall. Content analysis highlighted practical organisational challenges, excessive administrative work and additional working outside of working hours. COVID-19 increased burnout and impacted on training for 73%.
Burnout remains a significant issue. Modifiable workplace factors contribute to burnout and are urgent targets for change.

artigos.titulo: White matter damage across frontal-subcortical circuits in carbon monoxide intoxication: Insights from fixel-based analysis
artigos.autores: Chang CC, Cheng JS, Chang HI et al.
artigos.destaque: Damage in the frontal-subcortical circuits can be found in patients with carbon monoxide intoxication, which was correlated to the severity in the affected cognitive domains.

resumo.texto: Carbon monoxide intoxication (COI) can cause white matter damage through neurotoxic effects. This study investigated these abnormalities within frontal-subcortical circuits and their association with cognitive impairment.

91 COI patients at chronic stage and 20 heathy controls were enrolled. Patients were divided into 3 severity groups (normal cognition; mild cognitive impairment, MCI; and dementia). Voxel-based morphometry and fixel-based analysis were evaluated between patients, as well as across different severity subgroups, and healthy controls. Regression analysis was conducted between the fixel derived metrics and the cognitive composite scores. Significance was set as family-wise error-corrected p < 0.05.

White matter damage can be detected across frontal-subcortical circuits at chronic stage of CO intoxication. Compared with healthy controls, damage in COI patients with normal cognition can be found in the cingulum even without significant grey matter lesion. The COI-MCI group showed sporadically localized white matter abnormalities in motor, dorsolateral prefrontal and anterior cingulate circuits, whereas the COI-Dementia group demonstrated deficits involving multiple major white matter tracts, including the anterior limb of the internal capsule and anterior thalamic radiation, as well as basal ganglia, temporal and occipital lobes. Reduced fixel derived metrics in periventricular and frontal bundles, including the internal capsule, superior corona radiata and cingulum were highly correlated with cognitive performance in executive function (Pearson's r up to 0.674).
Damage in the frontal-subcortical circuits can be found in patients with carbon monoxide intoxication, which was correlated to the severity in the affected cognitive domains.

artigos.titulo: Loss of DUSP2-RPA signaling enhances virtual memory T cell-mediated innate-like antiviral immunity
artigos.revista: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
artigos.autores: Tian W, Qiu Y, Wang W et al.
artigos.destaque: T cell-specific deletion of RPA1 phenocopies these effects, leading to spontaneous TVM cell accumulation and rapid effector-like responses upon viral challenge. Together, our findings establish a DUSP2-RPA-R-loop axis that restrains TVM cell development and innate-like antiviral immunity.

resumo.texto: Virtual memory CD8+ T (TVM) cells are antigen-inexperienced cells with rapid effector potential, but how their differentiation and antiviral activity are regulated remains unclear. Here, using an autoantibody-based screening strategy, we identify the phosphatase DUSP2 as a key regulator of TVM cell responses. Dual-specificity phosphatase 2 (DUSP2) deficiency enhances CD8+ T cell-dependent antiviral immunity and promotes the expansion of a highly activated CD44super-high TVM subset. Upon viral challenge, these TVM cells respond rapidly without antigen recognition and display enhanced effector and cytokine programs, supporting an innate-like mode of antiviral immunity rather than conventional antigen-specific recall. Mechanistically, DUSP2 interacts with the replication protein A (RPA) complex to regulate RPA2 phosphorylation and chromatin association. Disruption of the DUSP2-RPA axis promotes R-loop accumulation and increases chromatin accessibility, which in turn activates Eomesodermin (EOMES)-associated transcriptional programs, eventually promoting TVM cell differentiation. T cell-specific deletion of RPA1 phenocopies these effects, leading to spontaneous TVM cell accumulation and rapid effector-like responses upon viral challenge. Together, our findings establish a DUSP2-RPA-R-loop axis that restrains TVM cell development and innate-like antiviral immunity.

artigos.titulo: Safety, Accuracy, Empathy, Information Quality, and Readability of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Health Advice Generated by 6 Large Language Models: Cross-Sectional Comparative Evaluation Study
artigos.autores: Fan L, Liu R, Wu Z et al.
artigos.destaque: In this standardized single-turn COPD question set, model performance differed across several evaluated outcomes, whereas the first-round safety test neither established a between-model difference nor demonstrated equivalence. All 6 models produced potentially unsafe advice, and 9 safety classifications changed between rounds conducted several months apart despite high pooled agreement. These findings support cautious use of LLMs for supplementary COPD education, with clinician oversight for individualized treatment decisions and ongoing reassessment as public-facing systems change.

resumo.texto: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for health information, but chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)-related questions often involve safety-sensitive decisions, including treatment escalation, oxygen therapy, and exacerbation management. Because generative outputs may vary across repeated prompts, response stability is also relevant to comparative evaluation.

This study aims to compare 6 public-facing LLM chatbots in answering COPD-related public health questions across safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality, source transparency, readability, and 2-round response stability.

We developed a 55-question English COPD question bank from an initial 108-question pool using web-based retrieval, Google Trends, PubMed-informed topic review, patient education resources, and expert screening. Six public-facing chatbot products were evaluated in a primary first round and a post hoc independent second round, added after first-round data collection, using the same 55 questions. Visible model/mode labels are provided in the supplementary materials. Five blinded raters assessed manually scored outcomes against a Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) 2026-centered reference standard, and 6 readability indices were calculated. The primary cross-model analysis used the first round; the second round was analyzed as a matched retest sensitivity analysis. Stability was assessed using exact agreement and Cohen κ for safety, quadratic-weighted κ for ordinal ratings, and absolute-agreement single-measure intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) for continuous scores and readability indices; 95% CIs used question-level bootstrap resampling.

The first round yielded 330 responses. Unsafe responses occurred in every model: ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and DeepSeek each generated 4 unsafe responses (7.3%); Qwen generated 5 (9.1%); and Doubao generated 6 (10.9%). The overall safety comparison was not statistically significant (Cochran Q=1.909, df=5; P=.86); this finding should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent safety. Accuracy, empathy, information-quality measures, source-transparency scores, and readability indices differed significantly across models. Across 330 matched question-model pairs, safety classifications agreed in 97.3% of pairs (κ=0.821, 95% CI 0.543-0.979); accuracy and empathy showed weighted κ values of 0.872 and 0.856, respectively; DISCERN (an instrument for judging the quality of written consumer health information on treatment choices) and adapted Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP) showed ICCs of 0.954 and 0.925. Most readability indices also showed high overall 2-round stability, although model-specific variability remained. Nine safety classifications changed across the 2 rounds (5 from safe to unsafe and 4 from unsafe to safe).

In this standardized single-turn COPD question set, model performance differed across several evaluated outcomes, whereas the first-round safety test neither established a between-model difference nor demonstrated equivalence. All 6 models produced potentially unsafe advice, and 9 safety classifications changed between rounds conducted several months apart despite high pooled agreement. These findings support cautious use of LLMs for supplementary COPD education, with clinician oversight for individualized treatment decisions and ongoing reassessment as public-facing systems change.

artigos.titulo: Regional cortical thinning in cerebral small vessel disease: associations with disease burden and cognitive and motor impairment
artigos.autores: Fu Y, Zhang F, Li M et al.
artigos.destaque: Exploratory incremental analyses showed that regional cortical thickness remained associated with cognitive performance in several regions after accounting for the corresponding regional cortical volume, intracranial volume, and other covariates. These findings suggest that cortical thickness and cortical volume may capture partly distinct aspects of cortical morphology in CSVD, with cortical thickness potentially providing complementary information related to cognitive performance.

resumo.texto: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major cause of cognitive decline and mobility impairment, yet whether cortical thickness and cortical volume provide similar or complementary information across different levels of CSVD burden remains unclear. We examined regional cortical thickness and cortical volume in healthy controls and participants with CSVD using high-resolution structural magnetic resonance imaging and FreeSurfer-based parcellation. Greater CSVD burden was associated with thinning across bilateral insular, occipital, temporal, cingulate, and cuneal regions, whereas cortical volume alterations were more spatially restricted, with only the left parahippocampal gyrus surviving Bonferroni correction. After adjustment for demographic characteristics, vascular risk factors, apolipoprotein E genotype, and mean cortical thickness, associations remained evident in the bilateral insulae and selected occipital and temporal regions. Regional cortical thickness was also related to cognitive and mobility performance. Exploratory incremental analyses showed that regional cortical thickness remained associated with cognitive performance in several regions after accounting for the corresponding regional cortical volume, intracranial volume, and other covariates. These findings suggest that cortical thickness and cortical volume may capture partly distinct aspects of cortical morphology in CSVD, with cortical thickness potentially providing complementary information related to cognitive performance.

artigos.titulo: Effects of Probiotics/Synbiotic Interventions on Cognitive Dysfunction in Alzheimer's or MCI: A Systematic Review and Meta‑Analysis of randomized controlled trials
artigos.autores: Zhang M, Zhang H, Fu B et al.
artigos.destaque: Probiotics or synbiotics may improve cognitive test performance, but the certainty of evidence is very low because of risk of bias, substantial heterogeneity, and imprecision. Exploratory subgroup analyses did not provide clear evidence that disease category, intervention duration, intervention type, study-level mean age, strain composition, dosage, or cognitive assessment instrument modified the treatment effect. Larger, well-designed randomized trials are needed.

resumo.texto: To systematically evaluate the effects of probiotics or synbiotics on cognitive function in individuals with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, and related cognitive decline.

PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 20 September 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing viable probiotics or synbiotics with placebo or usual care were included. Cognitive changes were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMDs) using a random-effects model. Subgroup, sensitivity, RoB 2, Egger, and GRADE assessments were conducted.

Ten trials involving 739 participants were included. Probiotics or synbiotics were associated with a possible improvement in cognitive function (SMD = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.19, 0.81; P = 0.002; Ι2 = 76%). The approximate 95% prediction interval was -0.57 to 1.57. No statistically significant differences in treatment effects were detected between subgroups defined by disease category, intervention duration, intervention type, study-level mean age, strain composition, dosage, or cognitive instrument. The effect was numerically larger in studies with a mean age ≤ 70 years, but this difference was not significant (P = 0.17) and was sensitive to individual studies. Sensitivity analyses maintained the direction and statistical significance of the pooled effect. Egger's test showed no significant small-study effects (Z = 1.00, P = 0.318). The certainty of evidence was very low.

Probiotics or synbiotics may improve cognitive test performance, but the certainty of evidence is very low because of risk of bias, substantial heterogeneity, and imprecision. Exploratory subgroup analyses did not provide clear evidence that disease category, intervention duration, intervention type, study-level mean age, strain composition, dosage, or cognitive assessment instrument modified the treatment effect. Larger, well-designed randomized trials are needed.

artigos.titulo: The joint association of cognitive function and sedentary time on mortality risk in older adults: National health and nutrition examination survey 2011-2014
artigos.autores: Wilson SA, Churilla JR, Bigliassi M et al.
artigos.destaque: The combination of cognitive function scores with sedentary time has been shown to be strongly associated with increased risks of both all-cause and cardiovascular disease-related mortality.

resumo.texto: Examining the joint association of cognitive function and sedentary time may provide insight into the complex mechanisms underlying mortality risk within older adults. This longitudinal observational study examines the joint association of cognitive function and sedentary time on mortality risk in older adults.

Sample included older adult participants from the 2011-2014 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. The Digit Symbol Substitution Test, Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease subtests, and Animal Fluency were used to assess cognitive function. Average daily sitting and television time represented sedentary time. Cognitive function (lowest quartile) and sedentary time (above median) were combined for analysis.

Older adult participants (N = 2,230; ≥ 60 years; 49% male) were shown to have a significant (p < 0.05) increase in mortality within the lowest quartile of cognitive function and above-median sedentary time. A 2.8, 3.9, 2.8, and 2.5-fold increased risk for all-cause mortality for the Digit Symbol Substitution Test, Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease Immediate Learning, Delayed Learning, Animal Fluency test, respectively, were observed. Our analysis also revealed a 3.8, 3.2, 3.5, and 2.7-fold increased risk for cardiovascular disease-related mortality for the Digit Symbol Substitution Test, Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease Immediate Learning, Delayed Learning, and Animal Fluency test, respectively.
The combination of cognitive function scores with sedentary time has been shown to be strongly associated with increased risks of both all-cause and cardiovascular disease-related mortality.

artigos.titulo: Neurocognitive Outcomes After Cranial and Craniofacial Surgery: Global Research Trends and Emerging Themes
artigos.autores: Kincaid E, Baer TM, Ganti L
artigos.destaque: Research on neurocognitive outcomes after cranial and craniofacial surgery has expanded and become increasingly patient-centered. Recent themes emphasize neurodevelopment, long-term cognitive function, quality of life, and multidisciplinary perioperative management.

resumo.texto: Neurocognitive outcomes are increasingly recognized as important after cranial and craniofacial procedures, but the structure and evolution of this literature have not been characterized comprehensively. The Web of Science Core Collection was used to identify 657 publications from 1991 through June 2026. Publication output, citations, contributing countries and institutions, international collaboration, and keyword co-occurrence were examined using Web of Science, VOSviewer, and Microsoft Excel. Annual publication output increased substantially over the study period. The United States produced the most publications (n=241), followed by China (n=81), Italy and Japan (n=49 each), and England (n=34). The University of California system and Harvard University were the leading institutional contributors. Keyword mapping demonstrated an interdisciplinary literature spanning craniotomy, craniosynostosis, traumatic brain injury, anesthesia, neuro-oncology, neurodevelopment, cognition, and quality of life. Research on neurocognitive outcomes after cranial and craniofacial surgery has expanded and become increasingly patient-centered. Recent themes emphasize neurodevelopment, long-term cognitive function, quality of life, and multidisciplinary perioperative management.

artigos.titulo: Uncontrolled metabolic syndrome associated with poorer sleep quality in adults in rural areas: a secondary analysis
artigos.autores: Hastert MC, Kurz D, Siengsukon C et al.
artigos.destaque: Poorly controlled MetS was associated with poorer sleep quality, whereas clinically controlled MetS was not. Future research is needed to determine if effective clinical management of MetS may confer benefits for sleep health in rural populations.

resumo.texto: To examine whether clinical management of metabolic syndrome (MetS) is associated with sleep health among adults receiving care in rural primary care settings.

This cross-sectional analysis used baseline data from adults (age 20-75 years; body mass index (BMI) 30-45 kg/m2) enrolled in the RE-POWER trial, a pragmatic behavioral weight loss intervention implemented in rural primary care clinics. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). MetS was defined according to American Heart Association/National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (AHA/NHLBI) criteria and categorized as: (1) no-MetS, (2) controlled MetS (criteria met via medication use), and (3) uncontrolled MetS (criteria met via abnormal laboratory values). Linear mixed models evaluated whether MetS status predicted global PSQI, PSQI subcomponents, and sleep duration, adjusting for age, sex, and BMI.

Among 1406 adults (mean age 54.6 ± 11.8 years; 76.8% female), those with uncontrolled MetS (n = 634) had significantly worse global PSQI, sleep latency, and sleep disturbance scores compared with adults without MetS (n = 483) (P < .05). Sleep outcomes did not differ between adults with controlled MetS (n = 289) and those without MetS (P > .05).

Poorly controlled MetS was associated with poorer sleep quality, whereas clinically controlled MetS was not. Future research is needed to determine if effective clinical management of MetS may confer benefits for sleep health in rural populations.

artigos.titulo: Weight management in people with HIV
artigos.autores: Manne-Goehler J, Magodoro I, Ramírez BC et al.
artigos.destaque: Finally, bariatric surgical interventions are suggested to be safe and efficacious for those with chronic HIV infection and comorbid obesity. This Series paper identifies a range of key evidence gaps and research priorities for obesity management in people with HIV, including a lack of trials of GLP-1 therapies in people with HIV powered to key clinical outcomes, such as major adverse cardiovascular events and body composition endpoints, implementation science to define models of care, and research on the heterogeneities in clinical outcomes of obesity treatment by sex.

resumo.texto: Excess weight gain in people with HIV is now recognised as a common risk associated with the use of guideline-recommended antiretroviral therapy, such that nearly 50% of people with HIV are living with comorbid obesity. Weight gain and clinical obesity exacerbate cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health complications in this population and chronic weight management strategies that reduce these risks are now an urgent priority. Behavioural interventions can be offered to improve diet and increase physical activity, including increasing protein intake and promoting regular physical activity. Additionally, there is a growing body of evidence to support the use of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapies in people with HIV, along with a historical literature showing the efficacy of tesamorelin; however, there are sparse data to direct the use of other approved obesity management medicines specific to this population. Finally, bariatric surgical interventions are suggested to be safe and efficacious for those with chronic HIV infection and comorbid obesity. This Series paper identifies a range of key evidence gaps and research priorities for obesity management in people with HIV, including a lack of trials of GLP-1 therapies in people with HIV powered to key clinical outcomes, such as major adverse cardiovascular events and body composition endpoints, implementation science to define models of care, and research on the heterogeneities in clinical outcomes of obesity treatment by sex.

artigos.titulo: Motivation in adolescents and caretakers undergoing a weight management program - longitudinal data from the cluster-randomized, motivation-focused STARKIDS trial
artigos.autores: Herschbach A, Junne F, Erschens R et al.
artigos.destaque: This motivation-focused weight management program produced motivational gains at the Maintenance stage, supporting sustained behavioral change. Baseline obesity-related quality of life predicted motivational change, suggesting its value as a clinical marker for tailoring interventional approaches. Future research should explore distinct motivational trajectories to inform more individualized pediatric weight management strategies.

resumo.texto: Motivation towards behavior change is an important determinant of long-term weight management. Previous research demonstrates that children's and adolescents' motivation can be increased through participation in weight management programs. However, little is known about motivational changes in caretakers of children and adolescents with overweight and obesity despite their recognized role as "agents of change" in pediatric weight management. The study aims to compare motivational changes in caretakers and adolescents between a group receiving a motivation-focused weight management program and a control group. Furthermore, predictors for motivational changes are unknown.

This study is a secondary analysis of the cluster-randomized STARKIDS trial. The intervention group received an 18-month motivation-focused weight management program, the control group received optimized treatment-as-usual. Motivation was assessed based on Transtheoretical Model, using the University of Rhode Island Change Assessment-Short, as well as the related parent-perspective version. Each of these instruments contains four subscales: Precontemplation, Contemplation, Action, and Maintenance. Linear mixed models with multiply imputed data were employed to evaluate changes within the subscales between pre- to post-intervention measurements and to compare these changes between the intervention and control group. A multiple linear regression was subsequently used to identify predictors of motivational change.

Caretakers in the intervention group showed significantly greater changes on Maintenance subscale compared to caretakers in the control group at both T0-T1 and T0-T2 and trends for these changes on Action subscale. No group differences were found in adolescents. Among caregivers in the intervention group, multiple regression analysis for T0-T1 changes on Action subscale identified parent-reported adolescents' obesity-related quality of life as significant negative predictor for an increase on Action stage.

This motivation-focused weight management program produced motivational gains at the Maintenance stage, supporting sustained behavioral change. Baseline obesity-related quality of life predicted motivational change, suggesting its value as a clinical marker for tailoring interventional approaches. Future research should explore distinct motivational trajectories to inform more individualized pediatric weight management strategies.
Preregistered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) DRKS000228 13 (acknowledged primary register of the World Health Organization) on 27 November 2020 (Universal Trial Number U111112549536).

artigos.titulo: Effects of exercise interventions on leptin and ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis
artigos.autores: Guo Z, Guo W, Gu Y et al.
artigos.destaque: Exercise interventions were associated with reduced leptin levels and increased ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity. The leptin finding appeared relatively consistent, whereas the ghrelin finding should be interpreted cautiously because of fewer comparisons and substantial heterogeneity. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and should not be used to define an optimal exercise prescription. Further randomized controlled trials with more standardized exercise protocols, clearer dietary control, and consistent hormone measurement are needed to clarify the clinical relevance of these changes.

resumo.texto: Overweight and obesity are common among middle-aged and older adults, and obesity is a chronic, multifactorial disease that, particularly when accompanied by central adiposity or metabolic abnormalities, is associated with increased cardiometabolic, cancer-related, musculoskeletal, and functional risks. Leptin and ghrelin are key hormones involved in energy balance regulation and may be dysregulated in obesity, but evidence regarding the effects of exercise interventions on leptin and ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity remains inconsistent. This review aimed to evaluate the effects of exercise interventions on leptin and ghrelin levels in this population.

PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched from database inception to 5 July 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials that enrolled middle-aged or older adults with overweight or obesity and reported leptin or ghrelin levels before and after an exercise intervention. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were synthesized using Review Manager 5.4 and Stata 15. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using I 2; a fixed-effect model was used when I 2 < 50%, and a random-effects model when I 2 ≥ 50%. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and publication-bias assessments were conducted.

Twenty-one randomized controlled trials were included. Exercise interventions were associated with significantly lower leptin levels than control conditions based on 18 comparisons (SMD = -0.32, 95% CI [-0.47 to -0.18], P < 0.0001), with low between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 22%). Exercise interventions were also associated with significantly higher ghrelin levels based on nine comparisons (SMD = 0.45, 95% CI [0.11-0.79], P = 0.01), although heterogeneity was substantial (I 2 = 74%). Subgroup analyses suggested that exercise-related characteristics may partly contribute to variability in leptin and ghrelin responses, but these findings were exploratory. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses supported the stability of the main estimates. For leptin, Egger's test suggested possible funnel-plot asymmetry, but trim-and-fill analysis did not impute any missing comparison and the pooled estimate remained unchanged.

Exercise interventions were associated with reduced leptin levels and increased ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity. The leptin finding appeared relatively consistent, whereas the ghrelin finding should be interpreted cautiously because of fewer comparisons and substantial heterogeneity. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and should not be used to define an optimal exercise prescription. Further randomized controlled trials with more standardized exercise protocols, clearer dietary control, and consistent hormone measurement are needed to clarify the clinical relevance of these changes.

artigos.titulo: Phenotypic Clustering as a Tool for Uncovering Hidden Risk Profiles in End-stage Liver Disease: An Exploratory Analysis of Sarcopenia and 1-Year Mortality
artigos.autores: Dhami-Shah H, Pranesh G, Mogre D et al.
artigos.destaque: Exploratory clustering analysis suggests that phenotypic variation in muscle composition exists among ESLD patients undergoing liver transplantation, with differential associations with short-term mortality. Muscle quality, as reflected by PMDI, may provide additional prognostic information beyond conventional measures of disease severity. These findings are hypothesis generating and require validation in larger, prospective studies before clinical application.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is associated with adverse outcomes in patients with end-stage liver disease (ESLD), but the relative contribution of muscle quantity versus muscle quality to posttransplant outcomes remains incompletely understood. Radiological indices such as psoas muscle area index (PMAI), transverse psoas muscle thickness index (TPMTI), and psoas muscle density index (PMDI) provide objective measures of muscle mass and myosteatosis. This study aimed to explore phenotypic patterns in ESLD patients using clinical and radiological parameters and examine their association with 1-yr posttransplant mortality.

In this retrospective study, 86 adult ESLD patients who underwent liver transplantation were analyzed. Clinical and radiological variables (age, PMAI, TPMTI, PMDI, MELD, Child-Turcotte-Pugh score, and body mass index) were normalized and subjected to hierarchical and k-means clustering to identify phenotypic groups. One-year posttransplant mortality rates were compared across clusters. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess the discriminative ability of PMDI.

Five phenotypic clusters were identified, demonstrating heterogeneity in muscle quantity, muscle quality, and disease severity. A cluster characterized by relatively preserved muscle mass but reduced muscle density exhibited the highest 1-yr mortality (41.7%), whereas a cluster with preserved muscle density showed no mortality although these data were limited by a small sample size. Intermediate clusters demonstrated mortality rates ranging from 15.8% to 17.9%. PMDI showed modest discriminative ability for 1-yr mortality (area under the curve [AUC] 0.662), comparable to MELD (AUC 0.659).

Exploratory clustering analysis suggests that phenotypic variation in muscle composition exists among ESLD patients undergoing liver transplantation, with differential associations with short-term mortality. Muscle quality, as reflected by PMDI, may provide additional prognostic information beyond conventional measures of disease severity. These findings are hypothesis generating and require validation in larger, prospective studies before clinical application.

artigos.titulo: Circulating Tsukushi Predicts Incident Sarcopenia and Functional Decline in Older Adults: A Prospective Cohort Study
artigos.autores: He MQ, Dai XN, Zhang M et al.
artigos.destaque: Lower circulating TSK levels are associated with a higher risk of incident sarcopenia in older adults, particularly subsequent muscle-related functional decline. TSK may be a candidate biomarker for early sarcopenia risk stratification and may reflect systemic metabolic processes relevant to muscle health.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is a major age-related condition associated with functional decline, disability and mortality in older adults, yet reliable circulating biomarkers for early risk stratification remain limited. Tsukushi (TSK), a secreted hepatokine involved in systemic metabolic regulation, has recently been implicated in skeletal muscle homeostasis. However, prospective clinical evidence linking circulating TSK to sarcopenia development is lacking. We therefore investigated the association between serum TSK levels and incident sarcopenia in a community-based cohort of older adults.

A total of 1370 community-dwelling individuals aged ≥ 65 years were followed for 4 years. Baseline serum TSK levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the association between TSK and incident sarcopenia after adjustment for confounding factors. Restricted cubic spline analyses were applied to explore dose-response relationships, and predictive performance was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.

Lower baseline TSK levels were associated with a higher cumulative incidence of sarcopenia. In multivariable analyses, higher TSK levels were associated with a lower risk of incident sarcopenia (hazard ratio per SD increase = 0.64, 95% CI = 0.53-0.76, p < 0.001). Dose-response analyses demonstrated a non-linear association with overall sarcopenia risk, whereas associations with low muscle strength and low physical performance were more nearly linear. The association appeared more evident in women than in men. TSK alone showed moderate discrimination for incident sarcopenia (AUC = 0.700), while a combined clinical model improved discrimination (AUC = 0.808 at 4 years).

Lower circulating TSK levels are associated with a higher risk of incident sarcopenia in older adults, particularly subsequent muscle-related functional decline. TSK may be a candidate biomarker for early sarcopenia risk stratification and may reflect systemic metabolic processes relevant to muscle health.

artigos.titulo: Sleep characteristics and sarcopenia in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis: nonlinear associations and a potential adiposity-related pathway
artigos.autores: Sun X, Lin X, Deng J et al.
artigos.destaque: Albumin interacts with PBF, yet does not significantly modify the overall indirect pathway. Due to the cross-sectional design, findings are hypothesis-generating and not causal.

resumo.texto: Sleep disturbances are common in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD), yet the pathways linking sleep characteristics to sarcopenia remain poorly understood. We examined associations of sleep duration and quality with sarcopenia and whether these associations included an indirect component involving percent body fat (PBF), with albumin and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) as potential modifiers. This cross-sectional study included 562 patients receiving PD. Sleep was assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Sarcopenia was defined by 2025 Asian Working Group criteria; PBF was assessed by bioelectrical impedance. Restricted cubic splines, mediation/moderated mediation analyses, and sensitivity tests (E-values) were used. Sleep duration showed a U-shaped association with sarcopenia (p-nonlinear < 0.001), with the lowest estimated odds at approximately 7.29 h/night. PSQI score was positively associated with sarcopenia (OR = 1.12 per one-point increase). An indirect association involving PBF was observed for PSQI (ACME = 0.002, p = 0.031) and short sleep (ACME = 0.026, p = 0.030), but not for long sleep. Albumin interacted with PBF in the sarcopenia model for the PSQI (p = 0.042) and short-sleep (p = 0.031) pathways, but the indices of moderated mediation were not statistically significant. NLR showed no evidence of interaction. Mediation sensitivity analysis suggested that the observed indirect associations were not readily explained by modest residual confounding. Sleep duration and quality are associated with sarcopenia in PD patients. An indirect association involving PBF was observed for poorer sleep quality and short sleep, but not for long sleep. Albumin interacts with PBF, yet does not significantly modify the overall indirect pathway. Due to the cross-sectional design, findings are hypothesis-generating and not causal.

artigos.titulo: Kidney dysfunction under cardiometabolic stress promotes calorie-intake-independent wasting and frailty-like muscle phenotypes
artigos.autores: Kojima M, Sato Y, Hirayama A et al.
artigos.destaque: Cornstarch-based nutritional modulation improved exercise capacity, muscle mass, and serum albumin, highlighting slow-release carbohydrate modulation as a potential therapeutic entry point. These findings support a model in which kidney dysfunction promotes wasting by limiting systemic metabolic reserve and skeletal muscle metabolic flexibility.

resumo.texto: Although age-related sarcopenia and frailty are linked to impaired metabolic flexibility and disrupted energy homeostasis, whether this framework explains chronic kidney disease (CKD)-related wasting remains unclear. We show that superimposed nephron loss redirects cardiometabolic stress from obesity and glucose intolerance toward calorie-intake-independent wasting with sarcopenic and physical frailty features. This switch was accompanied by impaired skeletal muscle glucose-utilization programs, a blunted glycemic response to gluconeogenic substrates, and altered hepatic-renal gluconeogenic programs. Integrated omics revealed suppressed glucose programs, impaired fatty acid utilization-related compensation, and amino acid catabolic signatures in skeletal muscle. Similar features occurred with aging plus nephron loss and in older human CKD kidneys with reduced renal PCK1 expression. Cornstarch-based nutritional modulation improved exercise capacity, muscle mass, and serum albumin, highlighting slow-release carbohydrate modulation as a potential therapeutic entry point. These findings support a model in which kidney dysfunction promotes wasting by limiting systemic metabolic reserve and skeletal muscle metabolic flexibility.

artigos.titulo: Weaker or Just Lighter? Monitoring Strength and Function, Not Just Lean Mass, During GLP-1 Weight Loss
artigos.autores: O'Leary RT
artigos.destaque: Functional discordance is a confirmed within-person decline in strength or physical performance beyond measurement error without an adverse lean-mass signal (exploratory default: lean loss beyond the scan's least significant change and above 40% of weight lost). For higher-risk patients (older adults; low strength, frailty or rapid weight loss), the review proposes grip strength, five-times chair-stand time and usual gait speed, with a timed stair climb where feasible, before treatment, at 3, 6 and 12 months and around dose changes, with declines confirmed by repeat testing, assistance recorded and stepwise clinical review. The schedule is pragmatic and not validated. If lean-mass change identifies the patients whose function declines, functional monitoring may add little; if discordance is common, lean mass is an inadequate surrogate.

resumo.texto: Body-composition studies of GLP-1-based therapy report how much of the weight lost is lean mass, not whether the patient is getting weaker. This review asks how to monitor strength and function during treatment.
Narrative review of October 2026 PubMed searches pairing incretin drugs with strength, performance, walking and measurement-error terms, plus hand-checked reference lists.

In older adults, strength declines about three times faster than lean mass and predicts mortality where lean mass does not. On GLP-1-based therapy, randomized trials show longer walks and better reported function, while some cohorts of older adults show falling strength and gait speed; a 2026 review of 35 body-composition trials found none that measured objective physical function. Recent recommendations advise assessing strength and function, but none identified here judges change against measurement error.

Functional discordance is a confirmed within-person decline in strength or physical performance beyond measurement error without an adverse lean-mass signal (exploratory default: lean loss beyond the scan's least significant change and above 40% of weight lost). For higher-risk patients (older adults; low strength, frailty or rapid weight loss), the review proposes grip strength, five-times chair-stand time and usual gait speed, with a timed stair climb where feasible, before treatment, at 3, 6 and 12 months and around dose changes, with declines confirmed by repeat testing, assistance recorded and stepwise clinical review. The schedule is pragmatic and not validated. If lean-mass change identifies the patients whose function declines, functional monitoring may add little; if discordance is common, lean mass is an inadequate surrogate.

artigos.titulo: Body composition in octogenarians with chronic kidney disease. Role of gender
artigos.autores: Cigarrán Guldris S, Sanjurjo Amado A, Rios Guillermo J et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings highlight a marked sexual dimorphism in body composition and functional status among octogenarians with CKD, with important clinical implications for risk stratification and individualized management in this population.

resumo.texto: The population with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is undergoing marked ageing, and octogenarian patients represent a growing group with distinctive clinical and functional characteristics. In this context, alterations in fluid status and body composition (BC) limit the usefulness of body mass index, necessitating a more accurate assessment with bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). The aim of this study was to evaluate gender-related differences in body composition in octogenarian patients with CKD in a prospective observational cohort study with a 14-year longitudinal follow-up of clinical events.

A total of 724 patients were included (46.4% women), with a mean age of 84.7 years and a mean estimated glomerular filtration rate of 36.6 ml/min/1.73 m2. Vectorial tetrapolar BIA was used to analyse body composition parameters, hydration status, and bioelectrical variables, while muscle strength was assessed by handgrip dynamometry. In addition, risk of progression to kidney replacement therapy, fracture risk, cardiovascular risk, and age-adjusted comorbidity were evaluated.

The results revealed clinically relevant gender differences. Women exhibited lower comorbidity and a lower risk of initiating kidney replacement therapy, but a significantly higher risk of osteoporotic and hip fractures. From a BC perspective, women showed higher adiposity and a greater proportion of ECW, together with lower muscle mass, lower TBW and ICW, and reduced muscle strength. Men presented greater muscle mass and strength but a higher prevalence of dynapenia. Overall sarcopenia was infrequent in the cohort.

These findings highlight a marked sexual dimorphism in body composition and functional status among octogenarians with CKD, with important clinical implications for risk stratification and individualized management in this population.

artigos.titulo: The impact of the gut microbiome on skeletal muscle in health and disease
artigos.autores: Bongers KS
artigos.destaque: Several clinical trials of microbiome-focused therapies have also been conducted, with suggestion of benefits as well as potential harms. Taken together, the gut microbiome plays a key role in modulating skeletal muscle physiology, and may serve as the basis for novel therapeutics targeting muscle disease.

resumo.texto: The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria residing the lower gastrointestinal tract, is increasingly recognized as an important influence on skeletal muscle physiology, with critical implications for muscle disorders such as sarcopenia and muscular dystrophy. Researchers have uncovered multiple microbiome-derived metabolites that alter skeletal muscle protein synthesis, mitochondrial biogenesis, protein degradation, and glucose transport. Moreover, the microbiome mediates systemic cytokine release of interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor alpha, which can drive muscle loss. These studies have led to the identification of gut bacterial species (such as Veillonella atypica and Roseburia inulinivorans) that improve muscle endurance and strength when administered as probiotics in animal models. Several clinical trials of microbiome-focused therapies have also been conducted, with suggestion of benefits as well as potential harms. Taken together, the gut microbiome plays a key role in modulating skeletal muscle physiology, and may serve as the basis for novel therapeutics targeting muscle disease.

artigos.titulo: Evolution and impact of sarcopenia and myosteatosis in the context of liver transplantation
artigos.autores: Villeret F, Herreros V, Cayot B et al.
artigos.destaque: Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia and myosteatosis have a well-documented adverse impact on survival in liver cirrhosis patients. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors associated with muscle impairment before liver transplantation (LT), their evolution after LT, and to determine their prognostic value.

All cirrhotic patients listed for LT at our center between 2006 and 2010 were included. Sarcopenia and myosteatosis were assessed on transverse L3 CT images at LT listing and at 12 (M12), 60, 120, and 180 months after LT.

The study population consisted of 198 patients, 75.3% of whom were men, and 149 underwent LT. At LT listing, sarcopenia was diagnosed in 45.5% of patients and myosteatosis in 36.5% and 20.1% had both sarcopenia and myosteatosis. One year after LT, 56.1% of patients had persistent sarcopenia and 15.3% had de novo sarcopenia. Sarcopenia significantly improved at M12 post-LT (p=0.034). Post-LT patient survival was 89.2%, 76.3%, and 59.3% at 1, 5, and 10 years respectively. In multivariate analysis, at LT listing, MELD score ≥ 25 (HR: 2.549; p=0.001), sarcopenia (HR: 1.749; p=0.004) and myosteatosis (HR: 1.630; p=0.012) were found to be independent risk factors for overall mortality. The effects of sarcopenia and myosteatosis were additive: overall survival was significantly reduced in patients with both sarcopenia and myosteatosis compared to patients with isolated sarcopenia/myosteatosis (p=0.001).
Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.

artigos.titulo: Factors associated with skeletal muscle mass in patients with Behçet's disease: An exploratory study
artigos.autores: Hayashi T, Tsutsui H, Tomiyama N et al.
artigos.destaque: Low skeletal muscle mass is common in BD ambulatory outpatients and is associated with muscle-, nutrition-, and body composition-related measures. However, clear associations with disease activity and current systemic glucocorticoid use were not observed.

resumo.texto: To investigate the prevalence of low skeletal muscle mass and factors associated with skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) in Japanese outpatients with Behçet's disease (BD), while assessing sarcopenia according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2025 criteria.

This cross-sectional study included ambulatory outpatients with BD aged ≥40 years. SMI was measured using multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis. Sarcopenia was defined as low SMI with low handgrip strength. Clinical characteristics, physical functions, nutrition- and body composition-related measures, rectus femoris ultrasonography, and laboratory parameters were compared between the low- and normal-SMI groups. Associations with SMI were examined using age- and sex-adjusted and domain-specific multivariable linear regression models.

Among 48 patients (mean age: 65.4±11.8 years; 45.8% women), 52.1% had Low SMI, and 10.6% of 47 participants with available SMI and handgrip strength data had sarcopenia. In multivariable analyses, higher SMI remained associated with higher body mass index, greater handgrip strength, larger calf circumference, higher phase angle, and greater rectus femoris muscle thickness.

Low skeletal muscle mass is common in BD ambulatory outpatients and is associated with muscle-, nutrition-, and body composition-related measures. However, clear associations with disease activity and current systemic glucocorticoid use were not observed.

artigos.titulo: Molecular targets for the treatment of sarcopenia: a geroscience approach
artigos.autores: Picca A, Calvani R, Coelho-Júnior HJ et al.
artigos.destaque: The future of therapeutics against sarcopenia will likely depend less on identifying increasingly anabolic agents than on matching molecular targets to the dominant biological mechanisms limiting muscle function in individual patients. Biomarkers of target engagement, deep phenotyping, and mechanism-informed combination strategies integrating pharmacological, nutritional, and exercise interventions will be essential to improve patient stratification and translate molecular target modulation into meaningful functional benefit.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as a multisystem geroscience condition. The limited efficacy of first-generation anabolic therapies has challenged the paradigm that increasing muscle mass is sufficient to restore physical performance, highlighting the need for therapeutic strategies that address the biological complexity of muscle aging.

This review examines the evolution of molecular targets for sarcopenia, from anabolic pathways to emerging geroscience-based targets. We discuss mechanistic and clinical evidence supporting these approaches, emphasizing the distinction between molecular target engagement and functional efficacy, and examine how biological context, patient stratification, and multicomponent interventions influence therapeutic outcomes. The literature was identified through a comprehensive PubMed search, with emphasis on mechanistic studies, clinical trials, and recent advances in geroscience.

The future of therapeutics against sarcopenia will likely depend less on identifying increasingly anabolic agents than on matching molecular targets to the dominant biological mechanisms limiting muscle function in individual patients. Biomarkers of target engagement, deep phenotyping, and mechanism-informed combination strategies integrating pharmacological, nutritional, and exercise interventions will be essential to improve patient stratification and translate molecular target modulation into meaningful functional benefit.

artigos.titulo: Longitudinal Taxonomic and Predicted Functional Gut Microbiome Responses to Tirzepatide and Semaglutide: An Exploratory Secondary Analysis of the OMDOT-1 Randomized Controlled Trial
artigos.autores: Morioka T, Miyaoka D, Nakatani S et al.
artigos.destaque: Tirzepatide and semaglutide were associated with partially distinct taxonomic changes, accompanied by broadly similar predicted functional patterns. These longitudinal findings complement, while remaining distinct from, Week-16 shotgun metagenomic endpoint analyses.

resumo.texto: Glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies improve metabolic outcomes, but longitudinal gut microbiome dynamics remain poorly characterized. We compared taxonomic and predicted functional microbiome responses to tirzepatide and semaglutide in Type 2 diabetes.

This exploratory secondary analysis included 36 participants from a randomized controlled trial comparing tirzepatide, semaglutide and conventional treatment. Faecal samples were collected at five time points over 16 weeks and analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Genus-level features were screened using MaAsLin2, and candidate genera were further evaluated using longitudinal mixed-effects models. Predicted microbial functions were inferred using PICRUSt2 and analyzed using MaAsLin2. Primary analyses were adjusted for baseline body mass index, with exploratory sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for changes in body weight and haemoglobin A1c.

No significant between-group differences in beta diversity were observed. Alpha diversity increased predominantly in the tirzepatide group, with a significant time-by-treatment interaction versus control. Longitudinal trajectories relative to the control group differed for several genera, including Romboutsia_B, Barnesiella and Ruminococcus_E with both treatments and Vescimonas with tirzepatide (q < 0.05). Across 2106 predicted EC features, longitudinal effects were positively correlated between tirzepatide and semaglutide (67.1% concordant direction; Pearson r = 0.450, p < 0.001). Treatment-versus-control analyses identified predicted functional changes involving energy and carbohydrate metabolism.

Tirzepatide and semaglutide were associated with partially distinct taxonomic changes, accompanied by broadly similar predicted functional patterns. These longitudinal findings complement, while remaining distinct from, Week-16 shotgun metagenomic endpoint analyses.
Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCT), jRCT1051240017.

artigos.titulo: Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Hyperuricemia, Serum Uric Acid and Gout: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
artigos.autores: Lee YH, Song GG
artigos.destaque: Incretin-based therapies were associated with modest reductions in SUA and with a lower incidence of gout flares and hyperuricemia, an effect largely related to weight loss. The clinical relevance of these effects, and the mechanism of any weight-independent component, remains uncertain and warrant confirmation in dedicated trials.

resumo.texto: Hyperuricemia and gout are common but underappreciated comorbidities in Type 2 diabetes (T2D), obesity and chronic kidney disease (CKD). We aimed to quantify the pooled effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists on serum uric acid (SUA), incident gout and hyperuricemia, and to determine whether these effects vary by drug class and are mediated by weight loss.

We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov through July 2026 for RCTs of ≥ 12 weeks' duration reporting SUA change, gout flares or hyperuricemia incidence. Random-effects meta-analysis, subgroup and sensitivity analyses and meta-regression were performed. Registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261468511).

Eighteen RCTs (77 942 participants) met inclusion criteria. Incretin-based therapy significantly reduced SUA versus control (weighted mean difference [WMD] -0.44 mg/dL, 95% CI -0.52 to -0.35), reduced incident gout flares (hazard ratio [HR] 0.62, 95% CI 0.53-0.72), and reduced hyperuricemia incidence (odds ratio [OR] 0.61, 95% CI 0.53-0.70). Dual GIP/GLP-1 RA (tirzepatide) produced greater SUA lowering than mono GLP-1 RAs (-0.62 vs. -0.35 mg/dL, p = 0.001). Body-weight loss was a significant moderator of SUA reduction (β = -0.041 mg/dL per kg, p < 0.001), explaining 84.7% of between-trial heterogeneity, with a significant weight-independent intercept (-0.19 mg/dL, p < 0.001). The SUA reduction was robust in all sensitivity analyses, including restriction to placebo-controlled trials. GRADE certainty was high for SUA and moderate for gout flares (owing to small-study effects) and hyperuricemia incidence.

Incretin-based therapies were associated with modest reductions in SUA and with a lower incidence of gout flares and hyperuricemia, an effect largely related to weight loss. The clinical relevance of these effects, and the mechanism of any weight-independent component, remains uncertain and warrant confirmation in dedicated trials.

artigos.titulo: Medicaid Coverage Withdrawal and Dispensing of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists for Obesity
artigos.autores: Nyambod FT, Msemakweli JG, Onesphore M
artigos.destaque: In this quasi-experimental study, withdrawal of Medicaid coverage was associated with the loss of most reimbursed dispensing of GLP-1 RAs for obesity within one quarter, with little replacement by other agents. Protecting enrollees already receiving these drugs, for example, by honoring existing authorizations, might limit treatment interruption, but this has not been evaluated.

resumo.texto: Five state Medicaid programs withdrew coverage of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) for obesity in late 2025 and January 2026, and others have narrowed coverage or are reconsidering it. The benefits of these drugs appear to depend on continued use, but whether withdrawal interrupts treatment for current users is unknown. This study examined changes in dispensing of obesity-indicated GLP-1 RAs after state Medicaid programs withdrew or restricted coverage.

This quasi-experimental study used quarterly Medicaid State Drug Utilization Data for 50 states and the District of Columbia from 2021 through the first quarter of 2026. Difference-in-differences and event-study models compared dispensing in states that withdrew coverage with dispensing in states that continued it, using each state's dispensing of diabetes-indicated GLP-1 RAs as a within-state comparison. The exposure was withdrawal or restriction of Medicaid coverage of GLP-1 RAs for obesity, identified from state agency documents. The main outcome was reimbursed prescriptions for obesity-indicated GLP-1 RAs per 1,000 enrollees per quarter. Estimates are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Data were analyzed from September to October 2026.

The five withdrawing states accounted for 2,428,709 (65.2%) of 3,725,732 obesity-indicated GLP-1 RA prescriptions reimbursed by Medicaid in 2025. Compared with 12 continuing states, withdrawal was associated with an 84.7% decline in obesity-indicated dispensing (95% CI: 64.5%-93.4%; exact permutation p < 0.001), or 29.1 fewer prescriptions per 1,000 enrollees per quarter (95% CI: 14.3-43.9). No significant change was detected in diabetes-indicated dispensing (-3.2%; 95% CI: -23.4% to 22.2%), and differences between the two groups before the withdrawals were announced were small and not statistically significant. In the first quarter without coverage, obesity-indicated dispensing fell by 61% to 96% in individual withdrawing states. The four states that withdrew on January 1, 2026, reimbursed 661,353 obesity-indicated prescriptions in the preceding quarter and 134,647 in the next, a decline of 526,706 (79.6%). Dispensing of older antiobesity medications increased by at most 2.9 prescriptions per 1,000 enrollees. Narrower criteria in two states were followed by declines of 23%-37%.

In this quasi-experimental study, withdrawal of Medicaid coverage was associated with the loss of most reimbursed dispensing of GLP-1 RAs for obesity within one quarter, with little replacement by other agents. Protecting enrollees already receiving these drugs, for example, by honoring existing authorizations, might limit treatment interruption, but this has not been evaluated.
