artigos.titulo: Will GLP-1-based therapies reshape the epidemiology of MASLD? An emerging public health perspective
artigos.autores: Pereira ENGDS, Rodrigues KL
artigos.destaque: We identify observations that would refute these expectations and discuss implications for prevention, healthcare systems, and the natural history of MASLD. Population benefits will depend on sustained treatment, accessibility, affordability, and equitable implementation, alongside confirmation that histological improvements translate into fewer liver-related clinical events.

resumo.texto: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the leading cause of chronic liver disease worldwide, driven by increasing obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The expanding use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) raises an epidemiological question: could therapies targeting these metabolic drivers reshape the future burden of chronic liver disease? GLP-1-based therapies reduce body weight and improve metabolic dysfunction, with potential implications for hepatic steatosis and disease progression. The phase 3 ESSENCE trial demonstrated histological benefits of semaglutide in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis, supporting accelerated or conditional regulatory approvals. However, effects on liver-related clinical outcomes remain unproven. In this Perspective, we examine the evidence and translate it into an explicitly parameterized scenario using a potential impact fraction. Combining published estimates of eligibility, relative risk, treatment persistence, and effectiveness with coverage scenarios of 5%, 10%, and 20%, the model suggests relative reductions of approximately 0.3% to 1.1% in the global incidence of cirrhosis among individuals with prevalent MASLD, at equilibrium (95% uncertainty interval at 20% coverage and intermediate persistence, 0.6% to 1.6%; best-case envelope, 4.6%). These estimates represent testable hypotheses rather than established clinical effects. Effective coverage, defined as coverage multiplied by persistence, is the principal constraint. We identify observations that would refute these expectations and discuss implications for prevention, healthcare systems, and the natural history of MASLD. Population benefits will depend on sustained treatment, accessibility, affordability, and equitable implementation, alongside confirmation that histological improvements translate into fewer liver-related clinical events.

artigos.titulo: Implications of Economic Hardship for Child Well-Being in Active and Reserve Component U.S. Military Families: Applying the Family Stress Model
artigos.autores: Lucier-Greer M, Saxey MT, Hanson E et al.
artigos.destaque: Notably, parent psychological distress was more strongly associated with child mental health symptoms among active-duty than NG/R families. Findings provide further support for the utility of the family stress model in studying military families while underscoring the importance of considering contextual differences.

resumo.texto: The family stress model has guided examinations of how economic hardship is linked to child outcomes with various populations, including military families. However, many studies have relied on smaller convenience samples with insufficient variation to address unique aspects of the military community context that may moderate the associations. Military families' duty status (i.e., full-time versus part-time service) is one such consideration because it can shape access to military-provided financial supports and may have implications for relational processes that are linked to hardship. Grounded in the family stress model, this study leveraged national data from 5529 military families who participated in the U.S. Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey to assess the prevalence of economic hardship, how economic hardship was associated with economic pressure, parent psychological distress, and child mental health, and whether these patterns differed between active-duty (n = 3128) and National Guard/Reserve families (NG/R; n = 2401). On average, active-duty and NG/R respondents similarly reported few economic hardships (M = 0.74 out of 8 for both). Support for the family stress model was observed for both groups. Greater economic hardship was associated with greater economic pressure, while economic pressure was related to more parent psychological distress, and, ultimately, more child mental health symptoms. Notably, parent psychological distress was more strongly associated with child mental health symptoms among active-duty than NG/R families. Findings provide further support for the utility of the family stress model in studying military families while underscoring the importance of considering contextual differences.

artigos.titulo: Health-care burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in European tertiary-care outpatient clinics (CONSTANS): a prospective multicentre cohort study
artigos.autores: Ratziu V, Dufour JF, Ponnaiah M et al.
artigos.destaque: MASLD was the second most frequent single cause for outpatient visits in eight European tertiary care centers. Significant fibrosis including cirrhosis was diagnosed in 44% of patients. The cost of required additional visits and procedures was equivalent to that recommended for hepatitis C before antiviral treatment.

resumo.texto: Despite modeling-based epidemiological studies of MASLD, precise estimates of the prevalence and health-care resource utilization in outpatient clinical practice are unknown. We assessed, in a real-life setting, the prevalence of suspected/confirmed MASLD and described health-care resource utilization.

A prospective, observational study of patients attending the outpatient hepato-gastroenterology clinics of eight European tertiary care centers during three months. Follow-up data of patients with suspected/confirmed MASLD were recorded 12 months after the screening visit: final diagnosis, disease stage, diagnostic work-up and the use of health-care resources.

5240 outpatients from Germany, France, United Kingdom, Switzerland, Italy, Spain and Slovakia were screened. The main reasons for visit were: chronic viral hepatitis, 33.4% (1749/5240), miscellaneous hepatobiliary conditions including neoplasms, 32.9% (1725/5240) and known/suspected MASLD, 24.7% (1293/5240) (pooled prevalence of 26.1% (95% CI: 19.1-34.7)). 1134 suspected/confirmed MASLD patients were included, the diagnosis was confirmed in 80.2% (909/1134). Significant fibrosis was documented in 22.7% (257/1134) and cirrhosis (including burn-out MASLD) in 21.3% (241/1134). Procedures performed differed between countries, overall 66.4% (753/1134) had imaging studies, 65.3% (740/1134) non-invasive fibrosis tests, 20.4% (231/1134) liver biopsy, while referral for further cardiometabolic assessment or therapy was minimal (144/1134, 15.8%). The cost of all procedures and visits was in the range of that recommended for exploring hepatitis C before treatment, although highly variable between countries.

MASLD was the second most frequent single cause for outpatient visits in eight European tertiary care centers. Significant fibrosis including cirrhosis was diagnosed in 44% of patients. The cost of required additional visits and procedures was equivalent to that recommended for hepatitis C before antiviral treatment.
IMI2-Grant Agreement 777377-LITMUS.

artigos.titulo: Effects of melatonin and transcranial photobiomodulation on neuroinflammation-related gene expression and anxiety-like behaviors in rats under chronic restraint stress
artigos.autores: Mazaheri M, Radahmadi M, Hosseini-Nasab F et al.
artigos.destaque: Stress-induced anxiety-like behaviors were significantly reduced by MLT, with effects similar to those of the combined treatment, which outperformed tPBM alone. These findings suggest the potential of tPBM and melatonin as complementary approaches for mitigating stress-related alterations, highlighting further investigation to optimize their doses and treatment parameters.

resumo.texto: Psychological stress causes immunological and behavioral alterations that can maladaptively affect the quality of life. However, melatonin (MLT) and transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) have promising effects on brain functions. This study investigated the effects of MLT and tPBM in rats under chronic stress by evaluating neuroinflammation-related gene expression and anxiety-like behaviors. Sixty-three male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to nine groups: Control (Co), Sham injection (Sh-I), Sham tPBM (Sh-tPBM), MLT, tPBM, Stress (St), Stress with Melatonin (St-MLT), Stress with tPBM (St-tPBM), and Stress with Melatonin and tPBM (St-MLT-tPBM). Chronic restraint stress (2 h/day for 21 days) was applied to all stressed rats. MLT (20 mg/kg; intraperitoneal) and tPBM (808 nm; delivered to the scalp surface) were administered following restraint stress. Gene expression of hippocampal neuroinflammation-associated genes (IL-17A, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, IL-1β, and Aif1) was measured by real-time PCR. Additionally, anxiety-like behaviors were evaluated by the elevated-plus maze test. Hippocampal IL-17A and ICAM-1 gene expression was higher in stressed rats than in normal subjects. However, in the St group, IL-1β expression remained unchanged, whereas Aif1 expression was decreased compared with the Co group. tPBM reversed the stress-induced upregulation of IL-17A and ICAM-1 expression, whereas MLT could not mitigate them compared with normal subjects. The combined MLT and tPBM treatment elicited gene expression changes similar to those observed with tPBM alone. Stress-induced anxiety-like behaviors were significantly reduced by MLT, with effects similar to those of the combined treatment, which outperformed tPBM alone. These findings suggest the potential of tPBM and melatonin as complementary approaches for mitigating stress-related alterations, highlighting further investigation to optimize their doses and treatment parameters.

artigos.titulo: Predictive Analytics and Workflow Automation to Reduce Administrative Burden and Clinician Burnout in United States Clinical Settings: A Systematic Review
artigos.autores: Akosah A, Hunt TJ
artigos.destaque: Workflow-integrated predictive analytics and automation interventions were associated with measurable improvements in documentation workload and selected burnout indicators in US clinical settings. However, evidence remains mixed and largely observational. Rigorous, multisite, longitudinal evaluations using standardized workload and burnout metrics are needed to determine sustainability and generalizability.

resumo.texto: Electronic health record (EHR)-related administrative burden remains a frequently cited contributor to clinician burnout in the United States. Although digital systems were implemented to improve quality, safety, and care coordination, expanded documentation requirements, inbox messaging, and regulatory reporting have increased clerical workload. Traditional interruptive clinical decision support tools may further increase cognitive demands through alert fatigue and workflow disruption. Health systems have increasingly adopted predictive analytics and workflow-integrated automation, including ambient artificial intelligence (AI) documentation, inbox prioritization, and audit log-based workflow monitoring. However, their effects on operational efficiency and clinician well-being remain uncertain. This review examined clinician-facing interventions in US clinical settings and their impact on documentation workload, operational efficiency, and burnout-related outcomes.

A systematic review guided by Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, and Embase. The search included English-language studies published between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2025, with an updated search capturing eligible early online publications through 2026. Eligible studies evaluated clinician-facing predictive analytics or workflow automation in US clinical settings and reported measurable outcomes, including documentation time, after-hours EHR use, alert burden, cognitive task load, productivity, or validated burnout measures. Findings were synthesized narratively because interventions and outcome measures varied.

Of 520 records identified, 173 unique records were screened; 24 (13.9%) underwent full-text review, and 7 of 24 (29.2%) met inclusion criteria. Ambient AI documentation platforms were associated with approximately 10%-30% reductions in documentation time, although findings on after-hours EHR activity varied. Several multisite implementations reported improvements in validated burnout measures and cognitive task load. AI-driven inbox prioritization reduced message review time, while audit log-based clinical decision support monitoring identified changes in EHR activity patterns following intervention. Evidence quality varied, and follow-up periods were generally short.

Workflow-integrated predictive analytics and automation interventions were associated with measurable improvements in documentation workload and selected burnout indicators in US clinical settings. However, evidence remains mixed and largely observational. Rigorous, multisite, longitudinal evaluations using standardized workload and burnout metrics are needed to determine sustainability and generalizability.

artigos.titulo: Mangiferin Buffers Depressive-Like Behaviors by Modulating Astrocytic DHHC2 in the Hippocampus
artigos.autores: Xia ZX, Zhao YL, Tian D et al.
artigos.destaque: Further mechanistic studies showed that MGF reverses reactive astrogliosis by regulating astrocytic DHHC2-Nrf2 signaling, including Nrf2 palmitoylation and its nuclear translocation, thereby protecting Nrf2 from Keap1-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and sustaining its transcriptional activity in reactive astrocytes. These findings demonstrate that MGF alleviates chronic stress-induced anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors by engaging the astrocytic DHHC2-Nrf2 signaling, suppressing reactive astrogliosis and reversing hippocampal synaptic and neurogenic deficits, which provides novel insights into the therapeutic potential of MGF for chronic stress-related mood disorders.

resumo.texto: Several lines of evidence indicate that mangiferin (MGF) ameliorates chronic stress-induced anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors, yet its precise role and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that MGF effectively alleviates anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors in mice exposed to chronic stress, accompanied by reduced synaptic loss and ameliorated hippocampal neurogenesis deficits. Notably, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) expression is preferentially altered in hippocampal astrocytes but not in neurons or microglia after chronic stress and MGF treatment, and knockdown of astrocytic Nrf2 abrogates the antidepressant effect of MGF. Further mechanistic studies showed that MGF reverses reactive astrogliosis by regulating astrocytic DHHC2-Nrf2 signaling, including Nrf2 palmitoylation and its nuclear translocation, thereby protecting Nrf2 from Keap1-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and sustaining its transcriptional activity in reactive astrocytes. These findings demonstrate that MGF alleviates chronic stress-induced anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors by engaging the astrocytic DHHC2-Nrf2 signaling, suppressing reactive astrogliosis and reversing hippocampal synaptic and neurogenic deficits, which provides novel insights into the therapeutic potential of MGF for chronic stress-related mood disorders.

artigos.titulo: Temporal and Spatial Dynamics and Mechanisms of Brain-Gut Axis Injury Induced by Confinement-Like Physical Restraint Stress in Mice
artigos.autores: Qiao Y, Cheng R, Zhang X et al.
artigos.destaque: Chronic confinement-like restraint stress induces triphasic nonlinear gut-brain axis injury rather than linear damage. PLA is a promising candidate target for mental health protection in isolated, confined, extreme environment populations and stress-related depression intervention.

resumo.texto: Long-term SIS exposure across aerospace, deep-sea, underground, and quarantine settings increases depression and gut-brain axis dysfunction risk, but long-term nonlinear injury dynamics remain poorly understood.

We analyzed GBD 2023 depression burden data in adults aged 15-49, then established a 0-35 day (d) chronic restraint stress mouse model that isolates the core physical confinement and activity-restriction component of SIS. Integrating behavior, histology, biochemistry, 16S sequencing, metabolomics, and formal nonlinear changepoint analysis, we validated picolinic acid (PLA) effects via in vivo intervention, in silico docking, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT).

Population data showed that the global depression burden during the COVID-19 period followed a rapid rise-partial recovery-persistent disability pattern, providing a temporal reference for the experimental model. In mice, confinement-like restraint stress induced triphasic nonlinear gut-brain injury with changepoints at ~7 and ~21 days: early HPA/inflammatory activation, mid-phase gut barrier disruption and anxiety-like behavior, and late hippocampal damage with despair-like behavior. Microbiota remodeling and tryptophan metabolic shift formed the core signaling cascade, with PLA identified as the key gut-brain metabolite. Exogenous PLA dose-dependently improved depressive phenotypes, repaired barriers, and suppressed HPA hyperactivity and inflammation. FMT provided suggestive evidence that gut microbiota contribute to PLA's protective effects.

Chronic confinement-like restraint stress induces triphasic nonlinear gut-brain axis injury rather than linear damage. PLA is a promising candidate target for mental health protection in isolated, confined, extreme environment populations and stress-related depression intervention.

artigos.titulo: Autistic matrescence as dynamic person-environment fit: a theoretical model of regulatory resources and support usability
artigos.autores: Steinbrück PC
artigos.destaque: Five propositions address within-person variation, sensory and communication moderation, recovery mediation, support usability, and reciprocal developmental feedback. Candidate measures are mapped onto instruments, including the Glasgow Sensory Questionnaire, state anxiety, perceived stress, the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, parenting confidence, parenting styles, and preliminary autistic-burnout measures. Generalization beyond autistic matrescence is presented as a transfer hypothesis rather than an established contribution.

resumo.texto: Matrescence is a developmental transition involving bodily, psychological, relational, and social change. Research on autistic pregnancy and early parenthood documents sensory overload, communication barriers, disrupted routines, professional scrutiny, and limited recovery alongside attachment, commitment, competence, and self-knowledge. Such divergence requires a model treating neither autism nor parenthood as sufficient explanations of psychological outcomes.

This theoretical paper reuses the 25-publication corpus of a published mapping review on autistic pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum experience, infant feeding, and early parenting. It develops a distinct theoretical synthesis by integrating that corpus with theories of stress, resource loss, functioning, and person-environment-occupation fit; it does not report a new review or formal study-quality appraisal.

The paper proposes that proximal psychological outcomes are shaped by dynamic person-environment fit among transition demands, state-dependent regulatory resources, and environmental demands and affordances. Its specific extension is the distinction between support availability and usability. Support usability is modelled as a staged conversion process through which available support must be accessed, processed, trusted, and implemented to become psychologically effective. The model specifies boundary conditions under which minority stress, trauma, psychopathology, acute clinical complications, or structural violence should be treated as primary explanations.

Five propositions address within-person variation, sensory and communication moderation, recovery mediation, support usability, and reciprocal developmental feedback. Candidate measures are mapped onto instruments, including the Glasgow Sensory Questionnaire, state anxiety, perceived stress, the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, parenting confidence, parenting styles, and preliminary autistic-burnout measures. Generalization beyond autistic matrescence is presented as a transfer hypothesis rather than an established contribution.

artigos.titulo: Burnout Among Professionals in ABA-Based Services in Brazil
artigos.autores: Sarilho C, Monteleone TV, Franklin BM et al.
artigos.destaque: These descriptive findings, which characterize the professionals surveyed rather than the Brazilian ABA workforce as a whole, point to the relevance of systemic and organizational responses to burnout in ABA services in Brazil. Improving working conditions, supervision quality, and support systems may contribute to better professional well-being and, consequently, to higher quality of care for individuals with autism.

resumo.texto: Burnout among professionals working in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)-based services has received increasing attention internationally; however, there is limited empirical data from low- and middle-income countries. This study aimed to describe the prevalence and characteristics of burnout among ABA professionals in Brazil and to examine how burnout indicators were distributed across professional and organizational characteristics within the sample.

A cross-sectional survey was conducted with ABA professionals working in different regions of Brazil. Participants completed the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS), together with a questionnaire covering demographic, professional, and work-related variables. Burnout was analyzed descriptively, with each dimension classified into low, moderate, and high categories using established cutoff scores, and distributions were examined across professional roles, age groups, academic backgrounds, salary ranges, and caseload.

Burnout indicators were highly prevalent in this sample. High emotional exhaustion was identified in 77.4% of participants and low personal accomplishment (indicating greater burnout on that dimension) in 89.9%, whereas high depersonalization was less frequent (34.1%). Within this sample, the proportion of participants classified in the most severe category increased from behavior technicians to coordinators to supervisors across all three dimensions, and professionals managing more than 10 concurrent cases showed higher proportions of high depersonalization and low personal accomplishment. Categorical burnout distributions were similar across salary ranges.

These descriptive findings, which characterize the professionals surveyed rather than the Brazilian ABA workforce as a whole, point to the relevance of systemic and organizational responses to burnout in ABA services in Brazil. Improving working conditions, supervision quality, and support systems may contribute to better professional well-being and, consequently, to higher quality of care for individuals with autism.

artigos.titulo: High stocking density impaired growth and induced oxidative stress, lipid metabolism disorder, and ferroptosis in grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella)
artigos.autores: Zidan SRS, Yuan Y, Li W et al.
artigos.destaque: Furthermore, PUFAs overflow into acsl4 (upregulated) increased membrane lipid peroxidation, and gpx4 (downregulated) failed to reduce resulting lipid hydroperoxides, causing ferroptosis execution. In conclusion, chronic crowding stress disrupts growth, causes physiological responses, and disrupts hepatopancreas health by inducing oxidative stress, altered lipid metabolism, and induced ferroptosis in grass carp reared in RAS.

resumo.texto: Intensive aquaculture via increasing fish density became an inevitable choice to increase aquaculture output. However, crowding stress compromises growth and fish health. The present study investigated the impacts of stocking density on growth, stress responses, oxidative status, lipid metabolism, and ferroptosis in grass carp. Fish (128.02 ± 2.35 g) were reared at three densities: LSD (low stocking density, 5 kg/m3), MSD (medium stocking density, 10 kg/m3), and HSD (high stocking density, 20 kg/m3) for 65 days in the recirculating aquaculture system (RAS). The results showed that increasing fish density negatively influenced the growth performance and feed utilization. The HSD group induced a stress response by significantly increasing the serum cortisol, glucose, and cholesterol levels, as well as AST and ALT activity. Crowding stress conditions induced oxidative stress and ferroptosis, marked by depleted antioxidants including catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione (GSH), and total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC), decreased glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), while raising malondialdehyde (MDA) and iron content in both serum and hepatopancreas tissue (p < 0.05). Additionally, transcriptomic analysis detected that HSD treatment changed lipid metabolism and promoted ferroptosis. Interestingly, HSD treatment prompted fatty acid synthesis, causing an increase in polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) synthesis and their elongation (acaca, acsbg1, elovl2, elovl5, and elovl6 were upregulated), while it suppressed fatty acid oxidation (cpt1ab and dgat2 were downregulated), diverting PUFAs toward membrane phospholipids. Furthermore, PUFAs overflow into acsl4 (upregulated) increased membrane lipid peroxidation, and gpx4 (downregulated) failed to reduce resulting lipid hydroperoxides, causing ferroptosis execution. In conclusion, chronic crowding stress disrupts growth, causes physiological responses, and disrupts hepatopancreas health by inducing oxidative stress, altered lipid metabolism, and induced ferroptosis in grass carp reared in RAS.

artigos.titulo: Beyond adversity: Dispositional mindfulness as a potential link between positive childhood experiences and lower hair cortisol concentration in adulthood
artigos.autores: Bartolen I, Soláriková P
artigos.destaque: These findings extend existing evidence on the psychological benefits associated with PCEs by providing preliminary support for dispositional mindfulness as a potential link between PCEs and lower cumulative cortisol exposure in adulthood. Considering positive developmental experiences alongside adversity may improve understanding of individual differences in psychological functioning and long-term HPA-axis activity.

resumo.texto: Advers childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with altered stress regulation, yet less is known about how positive childhood experiences (PCEs) contribute to adaptive physiological functioning. PCEs may represent developmental resources that promote adaptive psychological and biological functioning. This study examined whether PCEs were associated with cumulative cortisol exposure, indexed by hair cortisol concentration (HCC), through dispositional mindfulness and resilience, and whether these associations varied according to cumulative childhood adversity.

A community sample of 210 adults (M age = 28.95, SD = 10.20, range = 19-77; 74.8% female) completed an online assessment battery. A subsample of 120 participants provided hair samples for cortisol assessment. Participants completed measures of Protective and Compensatory experiences (PACE significance), ACEs, dispositional mindfulness (MAAS), resilience (RS-14), and current stress (LSC-R). Hair cortisol concentration (HCC) from 3 cm proximal segment was assessed as an indicator of cumulative hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity.

PACE sig. showed indirect association with lower HCC through greater dispositional mindfulness, whereas resilience did not. Moderation analyses suggested that the positive PACE sig.-MAAS association was stronger at higher levels of ACE exposure. Positive and adverse childhood experiences frequently co-occurred among participants with higher cumulative adversity.

These findings extend existing evidence on the psychological benefits associated with PCEs by providing preliminary support for dispositional mindfulness as a potential link between PCEs and lower cumulative cortisol exposure in adulthood. Considering positive developmental experiences alongside adversity may improve understanding of individual differences in psychological functioning and long-term HPA-axis activity.

artigos.titulo: AI Scribe in Specialized Rehabilitation: Usability Study of Perceived Usability and Usefulness Among Physicians and Psychologists
artigos.autores: Engan HK, Landstad I, Sand K et al.
artigos.destaque: This study demonstrated broad acceptance of an AI-based ambient scribe among physicians and psychologists working in specialized rehabilitation. The AI scribe was generally perceived as valuable, easy to use, and clinically relevant. Most participants reported a reduced perceived documentation burden and improved attentiveness during consultations. These findings suggest that clinicians perceived the AI scribe as supporting more focused patient interactions. Some concerns were noted regarding completeness and occasional inaccuracies, highlighting areas for refinement. Future research should explore long-term implementation in routine rehabilitation settings and its effects on workflow, documentation quality, and patient experience.

resumo.texto: Clinical documentation in specialized, interdisciplinary rehabilitation is often time-consuming and complex and may contribute to clinician burnout and reduced time for patient interaction. AI-based scribes transcribe and summarize clinical notes and may reduce documentation burden; however, their usefulness and usability in specialized rehabilitation remain uninvestigated.

This study aimed to assess the use of an ambient AI scribe tool among physicians and psychologists in specialized rehabilitation, focusing on perceived usefulness, usability, note quality, impact on patient interaction, perceptions of time spent on documentation, and documentation-related fatigue.

Over approximately 4 weeks, physicians and psychologists at 9 specialized rehabilitation centers used an ambient AI scribe during clinical consultations. Usability and user experience were assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and a modified technology acceptance model (TAM). Participants rated an AI-generated note using a modified 8-item Physician Documentation Quality Instrument (PDQI-8) questionnaire to evaluate documentation quality. Additional questions explored perceived impact on patient interaction, documentation-related fatigue, and general attitudes toward AI technology.

Thirty-one clinicians (18 physicians and 13 psychologists) used the AI scribe over approximately one month and completed evaluation questionnaires. The mean SUS score was 78.3 (SD 10.4), with 86.7% of participants scoring above the usability threshold. Perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) were relatively high (mean PU score 5.65, SD 1.33; mean PEOU score 5.56, SD 1.17), and 87.1% expressed intention to use the AI scribe in future practice. Most participants (80.6%) agreed that using the AI scribe reduced time spent on documentation, while 66.6% reported a reduced perception of documentation-related fatigue. The quality of AI-generated notes was rated relatively high, with a mean modified PDQI-8 score of 4.3 (SD 0.3) out of 5. Comprehensibility received the highest rating (mean 4.6, SD 0.6), whereas thoroughness received the lowest rating (mean 3.9, SD 1.0) among the note quality variables. Overall, 71.0% of participants expressed some level of agreement that the AI scribe enhanced attentiveness during patient consultations, while a similar proportion (70.9%) agreed that it made active listening easier by reducing distractions associated with note-taking. A few participants reported that some notes were incomplete, lacked biopsychosocial details, and contained inaccuracies.

This study demonstrated broad acceptance of an AI-based ambient scribe among physicians and psychologists working in specialized rehabilitation. The AI scribe was generally perceived as valuable, easy to use, and clinically relevant. Most participants reported a reduced perceived documentation burden and improved attentiveness during consultations. These findings suggest that clinicians perceived the AI scribe as supporting more focused patient interactions. Some concerns were noted regarding completeness and occasional inaccuracies, highlighting areas for refinement. Future research should explore long-term implementation in routine rehabilitation settings and its effects on workflow, documentation quality, and patient experience.

artigos.titulo: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study
artigos.autores: Vithal R, Krönlein A, El-Merhi A et al.
artigos.destaque: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.

resumo.texto: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke.

In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter.

Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047).

GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.

A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery.
ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

artigos.titulo: Hemp bark extract attenuates scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction through multi-target cholinesterase, MAO-B, and antioxidant mechanisms
artigos.autores: Heo HY, Kim JK, Park S et al.
artigos.destaque: Docking, GNINA rescoring, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM-GBSA/MM-PBSA analyses further supported stable interactions of these cannabinoids with the target enzymes, particularly cannabidiolic acid with acetylcholinesterase and MAO-B. These findings suggest that HBE protects against scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction through coordinated cholinesterase inhibition, MAO-B modulation, and antioxidant defense, with cannabidiol, cannabidiolic acid, and cannabichromenic acid acting as key multi-target constituents.

resumo.texto: Cognitive decline associated with Alzheimer's disease is driven by several interconnected mechanisms, including impaired cholinergic signaling, MAO-B-linked oxidative stress, and reduced neuronal antioxidant capacity. In this study, ethanol extracts prepared from hemp root, stem, bark, leaf, and seed were compared to identify hemp-derived materials with multi-target neuroprotective potential. Among the tested extracts, hemp bark extract (HBE) showed the most balanced activity profile, inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, butyrylcholinesterase, and MAO-B with IC50 values of 0.56, 0.01, and 0.02 mg/mL, respectively. HBE at 0.2 μg/mL suppressed H2O2-induced intracellular reactive oxygen species formation and recovered superoxide dismutase activity in SH-SY5Y neuronal cells. In a scopolamine-induced mouse model, oral HBE administration at 100 and 200 mg/kg improved performance in the passive avoidance test and reduced escape latency in the water maze test, indicating protection against scopolamine-induced cognitive deficits. Chemical profiling by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry revealed several cannabinoids in HBE, including cannabidiol, cannabidiolic acid, and cannabichromenic acid. Enzyme assays showed that cannabichromenic acid potently inhibited acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, with IC50 values of 1.3 and 6.6 μM, respectively, whereas cannabidiol and cannabidiolic acid were the most active MAO-B inhibitors, with IC50 values of 2.3 and 5.3 μM. Docking, GNINA rescoring, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM-GBSA/MM-PBSA analyses further supported stable interactions of these cannabinoids with the target enzymes, particularly cannabidiolic acid with acetylcholinesterase and MAO-B. These findings suggest that HBE protects against scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction through coordinated cholinesterase inhibition, MAO-B modulation, and antioxidant defense, with cannabidiol, cannabidiolic acid, and cannabichromenic acid acting as key multi-target constituents.

artigos.titulo: Enhanced Ferroelectric Performance of P(VDF-TrFE) Composites via MAPbI3-Mediated Crystallization for Flexible Memory Applications
artigos.autores: Kim H, Seo H, Han M et al.
artigos.destaque: Using P(VDF-TrFE) composites with optimized MAPbI3 composition, the composite FeFETs achieve extended retention up to 103 s, while the flexible ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) maintains stable ferroelectric switching after 10,000 mechanical bending cycles, demonstrating excellent mechanical resilience. These results demonstrate a practical material-engineering strategy for high-performance and mechanically reliable ferroelectric memory using a polymer-perovskite composite design.

resumo.texto: We report a material-engineering strategy in which methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite is added to poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)) composites to overcome intrinsic polarization and stability limitations. MAPbI3 incorporation enhances crystalline ordering and ferroelectric response in P(VDF-TrFE) composites, enhancing β-phase formation and strengthening dipole alignment through electrostatic interactions with -CF2- dipoles while simultaneously increasing dielectric permittivity and suppressing depolarization-field-driven polarization loss. With increasing MAPbI3 content, the composite films exhibit progressively improved ferroelectric performance and reach an optimum at 1.0 wt %, exhibiting a substantial increase in remanent polarization (2Pr from 13.7 to 18.4 μC/cm2), a 2.6-fold enhancement in the ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) on/off ratio, and a memory window expansion of 0.3 V. However, extremely high loadings and excessive MAPbI3 incorporation lead to aggregation and leakage-related degradation, resulting in reduced crystallinity and switching stability. Using P(VDF-TrFE) composites with optimized MAPbI3 composition, the composite FeFETs achieve extended retention up to 103 s, while the flexible ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) maintains stable ferroelectric switching after 10,000 mechanical bending cycles, demonstrating excellent mechanical resilience. These results demonstrate a practical material-engineering strategy for high-performance and mechanically reliable ferroelectric memory using a polymer-perovskite composite design.

artigos.titulo: A systematic review of group-based trajectory modeling studies on depressive symptoms in middle-aged and older adults: A life course and health ecology integrated perspective
artigos.autores: Chen Y, Yan X, Bai J et al.
artigos.destaque: Depressive symptoms among middle-aged and older adults follow heterogeneous trajectories. Persistent high patterns indicate a higher risk of adverse health outcomes, highlighting the need for early identification and targeted interventions. For high-risk groups, interventions should span the entire life course and integrate resources at the individual, interpersonal, community and policy levels. Future research should focus on modifiable risk factors and validate the effectiveness of synergistic interventions through empirical studies within the framework of the life-course health ecology model.

resumo.texto: Depressive symptoms are prevalent among middle-aged and older adults and exhibit dynamic changes over time. This systematic review synthesises research using group-based trajectory modeling to analyse depressive symptom trajectories, identify determinants within the life-course health ecology model, and explore health outcome associations.

This systematic review conducted a comprehensive search of eight databases to identify longitudinal studies on the trajectories of depressive symptoms. Study quality was assessed using the NOS tool, and a narrative synthesis was performed due to the heterogeneity of the data.

78 studies were included. Four patterns of depressive symptom trajectories were identified: stable low (61%), slowly worsening (21%), improving (8%), and persistently high (10%). Factors influencing the development of depressive symptom trajectories include adverse childhood experiences, personal characteristics, behavioral lifestyles, interpersonal networks, living and working conditions, policy environments, and stressful life events. Furthermore, evidence from multiple studies indicates that a persistently high depressive symptom trajectory is associated with a range of adverse health outcomes, such as cognitive decline and increased all-cause mortality.

Depressive symptoms among middle-aged and older adults follow heterogeneous trajectories. Persistent high patterns indicate a higher risk of adverse health outcomes, highlighting the need for early identification and targeted interventions. For high-risk groups, interventions should span the entire life course and integrate resources at the individual, interpersonal, community and policy levels. Future research should focus on modifiable risk factors and validate the effectiveness of synergistic interventions through empirical studies within the framework of the life-course health ecology model.

artigos.titulo: Drinking 2–3 cups of coffee a day linked to dramatically lower dementia risk
artigos.destaque: Drinking two to three cups of caffeinated coffee daily was linked to a dramatically lower risk of dementia and better cognitive functioning in a study spanning up to 43 years. The benefits appeared regardless of genetic risk, but decaffeinated coffee did not show the same association.

artigos.titulo: Magic mushrooms rewire the brain in a way scientists didn't expect
artigos.destaque: A surprising discovery reveals how psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms, rapidly reshapes the brain by creating new neural connections and strengthening them. Researchers found that the drug behaves differently in healthy and chronically stressed mice, potentially helping repair brain circuits damaged by prolonged stress. Most intriguingly, they identified a way to trigger this brain rewiring without the behavioral response associated with psychedelic effects.

artigos.titulo: Sleeve Gastrectomy With Jejunojejunal Bypass Versus Sleeve Gastrectomy: 12-Month Outcomes From a Propensity Score-Matched Analysis
artigos.autores: Sun Y, Zhang Y, Xue JM et al.
artigos.destaque: Evidence for differences in metabolic, nutritional and safety-related outcomes remained inconclusive. The central observed bypass-proportion interval may inform prospective evaluation but not current operative selection.

resumo.texto: Sleeve gastrectomy is widely used to treat obesity, but inadequate weight loss or weight regain remains a clinical concern. Comparative evidence for sleeve gastrectomy with jejunojejunal bypass (SG-JJB) versus standard sleeve gastrectomy (SG) is limited. This single-centre retrospective cohort compared 12-month outcomes and examined bypass proportion in relation to weight loss. Among 191 propensity score-matched patients (126 SG; 65 SG-JJB), matching-weighted mean percentage total weight loss (%TWL) was 26.59% after SG and 30.16% after SG-JJB. The adjusted difference was 3.55 percentage points (95% CI, 0.36 to 6.74; p = 0.030). After multiplicity adjustment, no clear between-group differences were identified in glycemic, lipid, hepatic, or nutritional outcomes. Recorded complications and complaints were infrequent, limiting comparative safety inference. Among all 70 SG-JJB patients, restricted cubic spline analysis suggested a non-linear association between bypass proportion and %TWL (P for non-linearity = 0.044). The fitted curve peaked at a bypass proportion of 0.359, with predicted %TWL of 35.62% (pointwise 95% CI, 32.86% to 38.39%). This peak was within the observed 10th-to-90th percentile interval of 0.272 to 0.371, although bootstrap analyses indicated uncertainty in its location. In this matched cohort, SG-JJB was associated with greater 12-month weight loss than SG. Evidence for differences in metabolic, nutritional and safety-related outcomes remained inconclusive. The central observed bypass-proportion interval may inform prospective evaluation but not current operative selection.

artigos.titulo: Impacts of wild blueberries on weight regulation, appetite, and cardiometabolic biomarkers of adults: A randomized clinical trial
artigos.autores: Kern M, Contreras P, Hickey E et al.
artigos.destaque: Consumption of intact wild blueberries within a yogurt-based snack did not impact acute appetitive responses or longer-term weight loss and cardiometabolic outcomes compared to a refined syrup-sweetened control yogurt during 8 weeks of energy restriction despite a tendency to improve cravings control. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05736432.

resumo.texto: Blueberries are rich in polyphenols and other bioactive compounds that may influence appetite regulation, weight management, and cardiometabolic health. The effects of daily wild blueberry consumption on appetite, body weight (primary long-term phase endpoint) and composition, and cardiometabolic biomarkers were evaluated during an energy-restricted weight loss intervention. In a randomized, single-blind, parallel-arm trial, 38 adults (BMI 25-40 kg/m2) were randomly assigned to consume daily a 170 kcal yogurt parfait made with either 1 cup of wild blueberries (n = 18 completers) or with an isocaloric artificially-flavored, sugar-sweetened blueberry syrup (n = 18 completers) for 8 weeks within a structured weight loss program. Acute postprandial (2 h) appetite ratings and hormonal responses (glucose, insulin, ghrelin, pancreatic polypeptide) were assessed at baseline as primary acute phase endpoints. Secondary outcomes included changes in body composition, blood lipids, glucose, insulin, C-reactive protein, blood pressure, food cravings and self-reported appetite and physical activity. Both groups exhibited significant weight loss (1.1 ± 1.8 kg for blueberry vs. 1.3 ± 1.3 kg for syrup) over time (p < 0.05) with no differences between treatments, despite a tendency for blueberries to enhance cravings control compared to syrup (p = 0.059). Main effects of time for reduced lean and fat masses and body water were detected, but post-hoc analyses revealed significant (p < 0.05) differences within syrup consumers only. No significant between-group differences were observed for cardiometabolic biomarkers. Insulin tended (p = 0.055 for main effect of time) to decrease but with no differences between groups. Acutely, both groups exhibited similar changes in appetite ratings and hormones over time. Consumption of intact wild blueberries within a yogurt-based snack did not impact acute appetitive responses or longer-term weight loss and cardiometabolic outcomes compared to a refined syrup-sweetened control yogurt during 8 weeks of energy restriction despite a tendency to improve cravings control. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05736432.

artigos.titulo: Evaluation of anti-obesity effects of ethanolic extract of Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides and its phytosomal formulation in high-fat diet-induced obesity in Wistar rats
artigos.autores: Tirthe VG, Nikam OV, Solas NS et al.
artigos.destaque: It ameliorated metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative, and histopathological alterations associated with HFD-induced obesity. The present findings suggest that EEHS may be a promising natural approach for the management of obesity.

resumo.texto: Obesity is a chronic metabolic disorder characterised by dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, oxidative stress, inflammation and organ dysfunction. The anti-obesity drugs available are effective but adverse effects often limit their long-term use. Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides is a medicinal plant rich in flavonoid and phenolic compounds, with reported antioxidant and metabolic regulatory properties. The present study was aimed at investigating the anti-obesity potential of ethanolic extract of Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides (EEHS) and its phytosomal formulation in a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity model. EEHS was characterised by phytochemical screening, thin-layer chromatography and determination of total phenolic and flavonoid contents. Obese male Wistar rats induced by HFD were treated with EEHS (100-400 mg/kg), EEHS phytosomes (400 mg/kg) or orlistat (25 mg/kg) for seven weeks. Physiological, biochemical, and histopathological parameters were assessed. EEHS exhibited significant anti-obesity effects in a dose-dependent manner, with the phytosomal formulation being the most significant efficacy. Treatment resulted in marked improvement in body weight, fasting blood glucose, lipid profile, liver enzyme levels, liver lipid accumulation, total body fat, TNF-α, antioxidant status and organ weights. Histopathological analysis confirmed reduced hepatic and vascular damage, inflammatory cell infiltration and adipocyte hypertrophy. The phytosomal formulation showed effects similar to those of orlistat and was more effective than the traditional extract. EEHS, especially as a phytosomal preparation, exhibited a potent anti-obesity effect. It ameliorated metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative, and histopathological alterations associated with HFD-induced obesity. The present findings suggest that EEHS may be a promising natural approach for the management of obesity.

artigos.titulo: Genomic and probiotic characterization of newly isolated Akkermansia strains from camel and horse feces in alleviating obesity and metabolic dysregulation
artigos.autores: Dai J, Li Z, Zheng C et al.
artigos.destaque: Collectively, Muc_T9 and Mas_DA effectively alleviate HFD-induced metabolic disturbances, providing a theoretical foundation for preventing obesity and metabolic diseases. However, due to the relatively short intervention period and the limitations of functional predictions, extended intervention combined with multi-omics approaches is warranted to further clarify the strain-specific regulatory mechanisms and sustained effects.

resumo.texto: Accumulating evidence points to Akkermansia muciniphila as a promising candidate to improve obesity-associated metabolic disorders. However, studies on the isolation, identification, and functional validation of Akkermansia strains from the intestines of animals occupying specialized ecological niches (such as camel and horse) remain limited. In this study, we isolated an Akkermansia muciniphila strain Muc_T9 and an Akkermansia massiliensis strain Mas_DA from camel and horse feces, respectively. In vitro assessment revealed divergent probiotic adaptive traits between the two strains, particularly in gastrointestinal stress tolerance. Genomic analysis revealed the presence of genes encoding the functionally related effector proteins P9 and Amuc_1100. In high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice, supplementing with Muc_T9 and Mas_DA significantly ameliorated HFD-induced obesity, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, and alleviated colonic inflammation and histological damage. Notably, divergent expression patterns of key genes involved in lipid metabolism and adipose tissue remodeling suggest potential differences in host metabolic regulatory modes. Furthermore, both strains restored gut microbial diversity and increased the relative abundance of putative short-chain fatty acids (SCFA)-producing bacteria. Collectively, Muc_T9 and Mas_DA effectively alleviate HFD-induced metabolic disturbances, providing a theoretical foundation for preventing obesity and metabolic diseases. However, due to the relatively short intervention period and the limitations of functional predictions, extended intervention combined with multi-omics approaches is warranted to further clarify the strain-specific regulatory mechanisms and sustained effects.

artigos.titulo: Plasma-membrane proteins in human skeletal muscle for targeted drug delivery: An annotated resource
artigos.autores: Stanojević N, Kjems J, Dalgaard LT
artigos.destaque: In addition, we discuss potential disease contexts in which to employ these. Together, these analyses generate a curated resource of candidate targets and provide a conceptual framework for developing next-generation delivery platforms for RNA therapeutics and other modalities aimed at skeletal muscle across a broad range of muscle-related diseases.

resumo.texto: Skeletal muscle is essential for metabolic regulation, energy homeostasis, and physical function. Its dysfunction contributes to disorders such as type 2 diabetes, muscular dystrophies, sarcopenia, cachexia, and muscle wasting linked to aging, cancer, and immobilization. Despite advances in RNA-based therapeutics, achieving efficient and selective delivery to skeletal muscle remains a major translational barrier. Targeting muscle-enriched cell-surface proteins represents a promising strategy to improve therapeutic specificity while limiting systemic exposure. Here, we combine a systematic literature review with database-driven analyses to identify and prioritize skeletal muscle-enriched plasma membrane proteins as candidate entry points for targeted delivery. The review summarizes current targeting approaches, highlighting their strengths and limitations. In parallel, integrative mining of the Human Protein Atlas, Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx), and CellxGene datasets identified 76 high-confidence skeletal muscle-enriched membrane-associated proteins. These were further functionally annotated and ranked using multi-parameter criteria, including relevance to internalization and suitability for nucleic acid-based delivery. In addition, we discuss potential disease contexts in which to employ these. Together, these analyses generate a curated resource of candidate targets and provide a conceptual framework for developing next-generation delivery platforms for RNA therapeutics and other modalities aimed at skeletal muscle across a broad range of muscle-related diseases.

artigos.titulo: Metabolic exhaustion underlies sarcopenic obesity susceptibility in aging mice as revealed by multi-omics factor analysis
artigos.autores: De Lorenzo R, Sciorati C, Avola A et al.
artigos.destaque: Plasma acetylcarnitine and pantothenol achieved area under curve (AUC) 0.91 for discriminating sarcopenia phenotypes. Individual susceptibility to SO reflects differential metabolic exhaustion rather than obesity severity, detectable through circulating biomarkers.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenic obesity (SO) affects up to 40% of older adults with obesity, yet many remain protected despite comparable metabolic burden. The molecular basis for this heterogeneity remains unknown. We exposed 12-month-old female mice to high-fat diet (HFD) or standard diet for 7 months. Multi-omics factor analysis integrated muscle transcriptomics and metabolomics to identify factors explaining phenotypic variation. Despite uniform obesity development, aging HFD mice showed marked heterogeneity in muscle outcomes. Factor 3 uniquely distinguished dietary groups and predicted muscle dysfunction independent of adiposity severity. It revealed metabolic exhaustion: lipid overload-induced upregulation of fatty acid oxidation genes and oxidative markers, long-chain acylcarnitine accumulation, and free L-carnitine depletion, indicating incomplete β-oxidation. Activation of p53, TNF/NFκB, and oxidative stress pathways indicated comprehensive metabolic decompensation. Plasma acetylcarnitine and pantothenol achieved area under curve (AUC) 0.91 for discriminating sarcopenia phenotypes. Individual susceptibility to SO reflects differential metabolic exhaustion rather than obesity severity, detectable through circulating biomarkers.

artigos.titulo: Adult-onset Still's disease and sarcopenia-related traits - muscle mass, strength, and function: A bi-directional Mendelian randomization study
artigos.autores: Wang J, Peng P, Wang Y et al.
artigos.destaque: AOSD leading to a decline in muscle mass, strength However, it does not significantly affect muscle function, whereas most sarcopenia-related traits showed no convincing causal effect on AOSD. Nominally significant associations observed for low hand grip strength in participants over 60 years and WP were not robust across sensitivity analyses and await further validation.

resumo.texto: The causal relationship between adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) and sarcopenia remains unclear. Therefore, we employed Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate the causal link between these 2 conditions. This study investigated the causal relationships between AOSD (n = 201,947) and sarcopenia-related traits, including low handgrip strength (n = 256,523), left handgrip strength (n = 406,552), right handgrip strength (n = 461,089), appendicular lean mass (ALM, n = 450,243), and walking pace (WP, n = 459,915). In the first stage, AOSD served as the exposure variable, while the sarcopenia-related traits treated as the outcome variables; in the second stage, the roles were reversed. MR analysis employed inverse variance-weighted, weighted median, weighted mode, and MR-Egger methods. Cochran's Q statistic was used to assess heterogeneity, while MR-Egger regression and MR-PRESSO were utilized to evaluate pleiotropy. The robustness of the findings, risk of bias, and causal direction were assessed using leave-one-out analysis, funnel plots, and R2 statistics. AOSD may contribute to reduced muscle mass and strength, but not to impaired muscle function. Genetically predicted AOSD is causally associated with reduced ALM (odds ratio [OR] = 0.971, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.951-0.991; P = .005) and increased risk of low hand grip strength in individuals over 60 (OR = 1.046, 95% CI: 1.001-1.091; P = .048). It also reduces left hand grip strength (OR = 0.984, 95% CI: 0.976-0.992; P < .001), with no significant effect on right hand grip strength (OR = 0.995, 95% CI: 0.987-1.003; P = .240). with no effect on WP is also observed (OR = 0.994, 95% CI: 0.988-1.001; P = .080). Genetically predicted sarcopenia-related traits (ALM and bilateral grip strength) had no robust causal effect on AOSD. While inverse variance-weighted suggested nominally significant associations of reduced grip strength (≥60 years) and slower WP with AOSD, these results were inconsistent across MR methods and warrant cautious interpretation. AOSD leading to a decline in muscle mass, strength However, it does not significantly affect muscle function, whereas most sarcopenia-related traits showed no convincing causal effect on AOSD. Nominally significant associations observed for low hand grip strength in participants over 60 years and WP were not robust across sensitivity analyses and await further validation.

artigos.titulo: Trends in screening tools for sarcopenia: A bibliometric analysis
artigos.autores: Guan L, Duan F, Qin C et al.
artigos.destaque: This bibliometric analysis maps global advancements in sarcopenia screening tools, highlighting China's prolific research output (30% of publications) and the development of culturally adapted instruments in Japan (Ishii test, Yubi-wakka method). The SARC-F questionnaire dominates research focus, spurring innovations including SARC-CalF and calf circumference metrics. The findings advocate standardized validation frameworks and integration of evidence-based screening into geriatric care policies, emphasizing tool accessibility and clinical utility to combat sarcopenia in aging populations.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia, characterized by the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass, strength, and function, poses a significant health challenge in aging populations. Early identification through effective screening tools is critical to mitigate risks such as falls, fractures, and frailty. This study aimed to analyze global research trends in sarcopenia screening tools using bibliometric methods to identify key contributors and emerging hotspots, thereby guiding future research directions.

Data were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) for the period from January 2013 to March 2025. A total of 180 articles were analyzed using bibliometric tools such as the R package bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace. The analysis focused on publication trends, citation impact, co-authorship networks, and keyword co-occurrence to map research trends and identify influential studies and screening tools.

The analysis revealed a steady increase in research output since 2013, with an annual growth rate of 38.16%. China emerged as the leading contributor, accounting for 30% of publications, followed by Japan and Brazil. Among the screening tools investigated, the Strength, Assistance in walking, Rise from a chair, Climb stairs, and Falls (SARC-F) questionnaire was the most studied tool, followed by SARC-F combined with calf circumference (SARC-CalF) and calf circumference measurements. Citation analysis highlighted pivotal studies on SARC-F validation, while emerging hotspots included tools like the Mini Sarcopenia Risk Assessment (MSRA) and Ishii test, reflecting a shift toward more practical and accessible screening methods.

This bibliometric analysis maps global advancements in sarcopenia screening tools, highlighting China's prolific research output (30% of publications) and the development of culturally adapted instruments in Japan (Ishii test, Yubi-wakka method). The SARC-F questionnaire dominates research focus, spurring innovations including SARC-CalF and calf circumference metrics. The findings advocate standardized validation frameworks and integration of evidence-based screening into geriatric care policies, emphasizing tool accessibility and clinical utility to combat sarcopenia in aging populations.

artigos.titulo: Zebrafish models for investigating skeletal muscle aging and sarcopenia
artigos.autores: Lee S, Lee H, Park S et al.
artigos.destaque: Current studies, however, have notable limitations: swimming performance reflects whole-animal physiology rather than muscle strength, many markers do not directly measure pathway activity, and some models represent specific stress rather than primary sarcopenia. Across these models, shared phenotypes do not establish a common causal mechanism; model-specific findings require validation during natural aging and in mammalian and human studies.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is characterized by progressive loss of skeletal muscle strength, mass, and function during aging, driven by impaired proteostasis, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered metabolism, regenerative failure, and neuromuscular decline. Experimental models are needed to determine how these processes drive muscle degeneration and identify testable therapeutic mechanisms. Zebrafish combine whole-animal physiology with genetic manipulation, live imaging, and scalable phenotypic analysis, making them well suited to this purpose. Natural-aging, telomerase-deficient, dexamethasone-induced, high-fat-diet, and genetically defined zebrafish models each reproduce distinct structural, functional, metabolic, regenerative, or neuromuscular changes relevant to sarcopenia. In this Review, we compare study designs, measured endpoints, and mechanistic evidence to distinguish age-associated phenotypes from responses to induced stresses or defined molecular perturbations. Natural-aging models capture spontaneous age-associated changes in muscle structure, performance, and mitochondrial integrity; telomerase-deficient models reveal defects in tissue maintenance and regeneration; and dexamethasone- and high-fat-diet-induced models enable controlled analysis of proteostatic and metabolic stress. Genetic models directly test relationships between molecular perturbations and muscle phenotypes. Current studies, however, have notable limitations: swimming performance reflects whole-animal physiology rather than muscle strength, many markers do not directly measure pathway activity, and some models represent specific stress rather than primary sarcopenia. Across these models, shared phenotypes do not establish a common causal mechanism; model-specific findings require validation during natural aging and in mammalian and human studies.

artigos.titulo: From NAD+ elevation to clinical benefit: Tissue-specific regulation and translational barriers in aging and age-related disease
artigos.autores: Pei Z, Zhong M, Jiang Q et al.
artigos.destaque: We propose a precision-medicine framework that shifts the core question from whether NAD+ can be elevated to whether a defined intervention corrects a specific NAD+ defect in the appropriate tissue and subcellular compartment. This framework provides a structured basis for designing next-generation NAD+-targeted trials with tissue-specific biomarkers and function-oriented endpoints.

resumo.texto: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) decline has been implicated in aging and age-related disease, and precursor supplementation with nicotinamide riboside (NR) or nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) has shown efficacy in preclinical models. Human trials, however, have produced inconsistent functional outcomes, and the sources of this translational gap remain poorly defined. We combined a bibliometric analysis of 3271 aging-focused NAD+ publications (2004-2025) with a critical synthesis of mechanistic and clinical evidence to localize where and why preclinical findings fail to translate. The bibliometric analysis revealed three structural features of the literature: (i) original research articles dominated the corpus, whereas the document-type classification cannot distinguish preclinical experiments from human observational or interventional studies; (ii) research is siloed across disease domains with limited cross-tissue comparison; and (iii) intervention-oriented keywords (NMN, NR, supplementation, drug delivery) have outpaced empirical clinical validation. Mechanistic synthesis showed that these structural gaps correspond to biological heterogeneity: NAD+ biosynthesis, consumption, redox balance, and subcellular compartmentalization are tissue- and compartment-specific, such that systemic precursor elevation does not uniformly restore functional NAD+ in disease-relevant tissues. Four subcellular pools-nuclear, cytosolic, mitochondrial, and axonal-each possess distinct rate-limiting bottlenecks, and hepatic metabolic reserve introduces an overlooked source of inter-individual variability. Across neurodegeneration, metabolic disease, cardiovascular aging, and sarcopenia, NAD+ dysregulation follows disease-specific mechanisms rather than a universal decline phenotype. We propose a precision-medicine framework that shifts the core question from whether NAD+ can be elevated to whether a defined intervention corrects a specific NAD+ defect in the appropriate tissue and subcellular compartment. This framework provides a structured basis for designing next-generation NAD+-targeted trials with tissue-specific biomarkers and function-oriented endpoints.

artigos.titulo: Prevalence of Muscle loss during and after Pelvic Radiotherapy in Gynecological Cancer Patients
artigos.revista: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
artigos.autores: Laan JJ, Westerveld H, Hinnen KA et al.
artigos.destaque: The prevalence of sarcopenia is high in women treated with radiotherapy for gynecological cancer. An increase in the prevalence of sarcopenia was observed, reaching its highest point at the three-month follow-up. Sarcopenia may be underestimated when assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, as indicated by the low sensitivity observed.

resumo.texto: Women undergoing pelvic radiotherapy are at risk of developing sarcopenia, defined by muscle loss. In patients treated with radiotherapy for cervical cancer, post-treatment muscle loss has been associated with poorer cancer-specific and overall survival. This study aimed to longitudinally assess sarcopenia and changes in muscle during radiotherapy and follow-up, and to evaluate whether bioelectrical impedance analysis can serve as an accurate bedside alternative to computed tomography (CT) for sarcopenia assessment.

This prospective cohort study included women with histologically confirmed primary cervical, endometrial, vulvar, or vaginal cancer, all scheduled to undergo external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with curative intent. Sarcopenia was assessed at baseline, during the last week of EBRT, and at the three- and six-month follow-up. Two methods were used to evaluate sarcopenia: lumbar skeletal muscle index measured via CT scan (gold standard) and appendicular skeletal muscle mass via bioelectrical impedance analysis. Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test were used to compare baseline characteristics between women with and without sarcopenia during the last week of radiotherapy.

A total of 31 women were included. Based on CT scans, the prevalence of sarcopenia was 23% at baseline, 32% at the last week of radiotherapy, and 42% at the three-month follow-up. At the six-month follow-up, 29% of the women were sarcopenic. Bioelectrical impedance analysis detected sarcopenia in only 0% to 50% of cases across the various time points. Patients with FIGO stage III were significantly more frequently sarcopenic based on their appendicular skeletal muscle index as assessed by CT scan during the last week of EBRT.

The prevalence of sarcopenia is high in women treated with radiotherapy for gynecological cancer. An increase in the prevalence of sarcopenia was observed, reaching its highest point at the three-month follow-up. Sarcopenia may be underestimated when assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, as indicated by the low sensitivity observed.

artigos.titulo: Relationship Between Swallowing Dynamics and Suprahyoid Muscle Activity in Sarcopenic Dysphagia
artigos.autores: Kim MJ, Kim KH, Jung HY et al.
artigos.destaque: Aspiration in possible sarcopenic dysphagia appears to be more closely associated with prolonged suprahyoid muscle contraction-deactivation duration, suggesting a slowing of the overall contraction process rather than impaired contraction amplitude. Peak-to-end duration measured by sEMG showed modest-to-moderate discrimination with high specificity for identifying aspiration risk, suggesting a potential role in the early screening of patients who may require further evaluation and targeted swallowing rehabilitation.

resumo.texto: To investigate sarcopenic dysphagia characteristics and the relationship between suprahyoid muscle activity and swallowing dynamics using concurrent surface electromyography (sEMG) and videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS). 56 elderly (≥ 65 years) with possible sarcopenia were prospectively enrolled and classified into aspiration (Penetration Aspiration Scale [PAS] ≥ 6, n = 27) and non-aspiration (PAS < 6, n = 29) groups. Swallowing dynamics (Videofluoroscopic Dysphagia Scale [VDS]) and suprahyoid sEMG activity were evaluated concurrently during 2 ml water swallows. Mean and maximum sEMG amplitudes showed no significant differences between 2 groups. However, total (p = 0.035) and peak-to-end (p = 0.008) durations were significantly longer in the aspiration group. Adjusted multivariable linear regression analysis revealed that prolonged peak-to-end duration was significantly associated with higher total VDS (B = 0.007, p = 0.015), pharyngeal VDS (B = 0.009, p = 0.019), and VDS aspiration sub-item scores (B = 0.030, p = 0.005). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis showed that a peak-to-end duration cutoff of 1.64 s predicted aspiration with a specificity of 93.1%, an area under the curve of 0.71, and a diagnostic odds ratio of 14.54 (95% CI 2.87-73.66). Aspiration in possible sarcopenic dysphagia appears to be more closely associated with prolonged suprahyoid muscle contraction-deactivation duration, suggesting a slowing of the overall contraction process rather than impaired contraction amplitude. Peak-to-end duration measured by sEMG showed modest-to-moderate discrimination with high specificity for identifying aspiration risk, suggesting a potential role in the early screening of patients who may require further evaluation and targeted swallowing rehabilitation.

artigos.titulo: Urinary metabolomic biomarkers of wine (poly)phenol intake and their association with sarcopenia-related parameters in older adults: a cross-sectional study
artigos.autores: Nicolás Marzo J, Marti-Anders C, Besora-Moreno M et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings support associations between wine-derived (poly)phenol metabolites and muscle health. Prospective studies and intervention trials, ideally using dealcoholized wine to isolate the effects of (poly)phenols from those of ethanol, are warranted.

resumo.texto: The influence of (poly)phenols from red wine on muscle health in older adults remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate associations between urinary biomarkers of wine (poly)phenol intake and sarcopenia-related parameters in older adults. Fifty participants, classified as probable sarcopenic (n = 29) or non-sarcopenic (n = 21), with a mean age of 69.1 ± 4.3 years, underwent assessment of muscle strength, bioimpedance, muscle ultrasound, isokinetic performance, and urinary (poly)phenol biomarkers quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography. Urinary biomarkers, including catechin sulfate, methyl-catechin sulfate, and resveratrol derivatives, showed positive associations with handgrip strength, skeletal muscle mass, appendicular skeletal muscle mass and indices. Positive associations were also observed with ultrasound-derived quadriceps and rectus femoris muscle thickness and rectus femoris cross-sectional area, predominantly in women. These findings support associations between wine-derived (poly)phenol metabolites and muscle health. Prospective studies and intervention trials, ideally using dealcoholized wine to isolate the effects of (poly)phenols from those of ethanol, are warranted.

artigos.titulo: Efficacy of Nutritional Intervention in Adult Patients With Heart Failure: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
artigos.autores: Batool M, Duseja N, Mustafa MS et al.
artigos.destaque: Exercise capacity improved significantly (6-minute walk distance mean difference 25.01, 95% confidence interval: 5.26-44.76, P = 0.013), while quality of life, creatinine, and B-type natriuretic peptide showed no significant change. Nutritional intervention was associated with reduced mortality and improved exercise capacity in HF, though effects on hospitalization, BMI, and biomarkers were nonsignificant, warranting cautious interpretation.

resumo.texto: Approximately 50% of heart failure (HF) patients are malnourished, doubling mortality risk; however, interventional evidence remains limited. A previously published meta-analysis found modest weight improvements only in malnourished/cachectic patients (5 studies, n = 275). This review updates the evidence in a broader HF population to evaluate the effect of nutritional interventions on all-cause mortality, hospital readmissions, and body mass index (BMI) in HF, determine whether intervention type moderates effect size, and identify sources of heterogeneity via meta-regression. This PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered (CRD420261445761) systematic review and meta-analysis searched PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane, and Embase for randomized controlled trials, quasi-randomized, and observational studies evaluating nutritional interventions (supplements, fortification, enteral/parenteral nutrition, counseling, with or without exercise) to increase protein/energy intake in HF, updating a 2021 search. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2.0 for randomized controlled trials; ROBINS-I for observational studies). Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs), with subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses. Of 7190 records screened, 23 studies (n = 2240) were included; 18 contributed to meta-analysis. Risk of bias was predominantly low. Nutritional intervention significantly reduced all-cause mortality (RR 0.43, 95% confidence interval: 0.26-0.71, P = 0.001), with no significant effect on readmission or BMI. Exercise capacity improved significantly (6-minute walk distance mean difference 25.01, 95% confidence interval: 5.26-44.76, P = 0.013), while quality of life, creatinine, and B-type natriuretic peptide showed no significant change. Nutritional intervention was associated with reduced mortality and improved exercise capacity in HF, though effects on hospitalization, BMI, and biomarkers were nonsignificant, warranting cautious interpretation.
