resumo.texto: Body weight (BW) and body mass index (BMI) are commonly used to assess obesity and response to weight-management interventions in patients with hormone receptor-positive (HR+) early breast cancer (eBC) receiving endocrine therapy. However, these measures do not adequately reflect changes in fat mass, visceral adiposity, lean mass and sarcopenia-related phenotypes.

This focused narrative review examines whether BW and BMI are sufficient endpoints for evaluating obesity management and anti-obesity pharmacotherapy in patients with HR+ eBC receiving endocrine therapy. PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for relevant evidence until 23 June 2026, including BC-specific studies of obesity pharmacotherapy and registered interventional trials. Studies have reported increases in total and visceral fat mass after adjuvant BC treatment, while changes in lean mass have been less consistent. The identified BC-specific studies remain mainly retrospective and weight-centric, with none assessing body composition as a key outcome.

BW and BMI may be useful entry and monitoring variables, but insufficient as stand-alone endpoints. Body composition should be considered as a complementary endpoint, alongside metabolic, functional and oncologic outcomes. Future studies should also assess endocrine therapy adherence and persistence to better characterize the benefits and risks of anti-obesity pharmacotherapy in patients with HR+ eBC.

artigos.titulo: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
artigos.autores: Börchers S, Mazzini G, Zetterberg H et al.
artigos.destaque: This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

resumo.texto: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

artigos.titulo: Obesity management medications: The way forward
artigos.autores: Blüher M
artigos.destaque: Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

resumo.texto: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

artigos.titulo: Plant-Forward Dietary Patterns and Cardiometabolic Risk Among US Adults: Findings From the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2009-2023
artigos.autores: Lov D
artigos.destaque: Greater adherence to plant-forward dietary patterns was associated with lower BMI and reduced odds of obesity and diabetes among US adults.

resumo.texto: The objective of this study was to describe the relationship between plant-forward dietary patterns and metabolic profiles.

A repeated cross-sectional analysis of adults aged 18 years or older was conducted using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), 2009-2023. Plant-forward dietary adherence was estimated from the mean of two 24-hour dietary recalls and categorized into tertiles. Survey-weighted multivariable regression examined associations with body mass index (BMI), obesity, prediabetes, and diabetes, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, dietary, and behavioral factors.

Among 33,532 NHANES participants, greater plant-forward dietary adherence was associated with lower BMI (β = -1.45; 95% CI, -1.82 to -1.09), lower odds of obesity (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.62-0.79) and diabetes (AOR = 0.72; 95% CI, 0.62-0.84) but not prediabetes (AOR = 0.92; 95% CI, 0.82-1.04).
Greater adherence to plant-forward dietary patterns was associated with lower BMI and reduced odds of obesity and diabetes among US adults.

artigos.titulo: Completeness of care provision and inequalities in care for people with hypertension, diabetes, and obesity: an analysis of the Brazilian National Basic Health Units Census
artigos.autores: Facchini LA, Tomasi E, Thumé E et al.
artigos.destaque: After adjusting for contextual and BHU characteristics, the family health was associated with 70% higher completeness of care provision. Although access to consultations is well established, weaknesses persist in comprehensiveness and care coordination for chronic diseases, highlighting the need for structural policies that strengthen the capacity of PHC to effectively address health needs.

resumo.texto: This study aimed to identify patterns and inequalities in the completeness of care provision for people with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and obesity in Brazilian primary health care (PHC), drawing on the 2024 Brazilian National Basic Health Units Census (BHU Census). This was a cross-sectional online survey covering 44,938 BHUs registered in the Brazilian National Registry of Health Establishments and validated by municipal health managers. Variables related to geographic region, municipal characteristics, and health service characteristics were analyzed. Care provision was considered complete when the response was positive for all 14 actions related to hypertension, 15 for diabetes, and 10 for obesity. A low proportion of BHUs demonstrated complete provision of care for people with hypertension (15.3%), diabetes (15.6%), and obesity (13.4%), across all regions and municipality profiles. Completeness was higher in the Southeast and Northeast and lower in the South. Large municipalities, municipalities with high or very high social vulnerability, and municipalities with 100% family health coverage also showed higher completeness levels. After adjusting for contextual and BHU characteristics, the family health was associated with 70% higher completeness of care provision. Although access to consultations is well established, weaknesses persist in comprehensiveness and care coordination for chronic diseases, highlighting the need for structural policies that strengthen the capacity of PHC to effectively address health needs.

artigos.titulo: NUTRITIONAL OUTCOMES AFTER ONE ANASTOMOSIS GASTRIC BYPASS VERSUS ROUX-EN-Y GASTRIC BYPASS: A ONE-YEAR COMPARATIVE STUDY
artigos.autores: Sampaio P, Pajecki D, Santo Filho MA et al.
artigos.destaque: Under structured multidisciplinary follow-up, OAGB and RYGB demonstrated comparable nutritional outcomes. OAGB appears to be a nutritionally safe alternative at one year of follow-up, with the need for ongoing monitoring of iron and vitamin D status.

resumo.texto: Metabolic and bariatric surgery is an effective obesity treatment. One anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) has emerged as an alternative to Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB); however, evidence regarding its postoperative nutritional outcomes remains limited. Objective: To compare food tolerance, gastrointestinal symptoms, and nutritional status between OAGB and RYGB one year after surgery.

This retrospective, observational, comparative study included 46 patients (16 OAGB and 30 RYGB). Weight loss, laboratory parameters, dietary intake, food tolerance, and gastrointestinal symptoms were evaluated one year postoperatively. Linear regression models were adjusted for relevant confounding variables, including age, sex, and baseline values when appropriate.

The percentage of total weight loss (29.55% vs 26.32%) and excess weight loss (63.36% vs 58.29%) were similar between RYGB and OAGB groups (P>0.05). A high prevalence of vitamin D deficiency was observed in both groups (RYGB: 82% vs. OAGB: 92%). Elevated parathyroid hormone levels were more frequent in the OAGB group (75% vs 50%), although the difference was not statistically significant. OAGB patients showed numerically lower serum iron and reduced transferrin saturation; however, none of the patients developed anemia. Mean protein intake met the recommended levels in both groups, whereas fiber intake was below the minimum recommended level. OAGB patients presented significantly lower gastrointestinal symptom scores for diarrhea, indigestion, and total score (P<0.05). Food tolerance was satisfactory and similar between groups.

Under structured multidisciplinary follow-up, OAGB and RYGB demonstrated comparable nutritional outcomes. OAGB appears to be a nutritionally safe alternative at one year of follow-up, with the need for ongoing monitoring of iron and vitamin D status.

artigos.titulo: Cutoff values of muscle-specific strength using arm circumference: Results from NHANES 2011-2014
artigos.autores: Costa-Pereira JP, Prado CM, Bennet JP et al.
artigos.destaque: Our study provides practical, sex-specific reference cutoff values for MUAC-based muscle-specific strength (HGS/MUAC) derived from a population-based sample. This accessible anthropometric metric showed strong correlations with DXA-based muscle-specific strength and small average standardized differences, supporting its potential as a pragmatic surrogate when regional body composition assessment is unavailable. Further validation is needed before its clinical or diagnostic application.

resumo.texto: Muscle-specific strength, the ratio of muscle strength to muscle mass, reflects functional capacity and has been incorporated into contemporary conceptual definitions of sarcopenia, although its operational diagnostic role remains undefined. Ideally, muscle-specific strength relates muscle strength to the mass of the muscles that generate it; however, such measures are rarely available in clinical practice. Mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) may serve as a practical regional surrogate for muscle mass.

To examine the relationship between conventional muscle-specific strength from dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and a MUAC-based muscle-specific strength, and to propose sex-specific cutoff values for the latter.

This cross-sectional study used NHANES 2011-2014 data from adults aged 20-59 years with MUAC, right-hand HGS, and right-arm DXA measurements. Adults aged 20-39 years with normal-range body mass index (BMI, 18.5-24.9 kg/m2) served as the reference subsample. Survey-weighted Pearson correlations and linear regression models were used to examine relationships between MUAC- and DXA-based muscle-specific strength. Cutoff values were derived at 1 and 2 standard deviations (SD) below the survey-weighted sex-specific reference mean. Bland-Altman analyses assessed agreement between the two metrics after transformation to sex-specific standardized scores.

A total of 4,518 participants were included (survey-weighted proportion: 52.7% males). MUAC was strongly correlated with DXA-derived arm lean soft tissue in males (r = 0.80) and females (r = 0.74). MUAC-based muscle-specific strength was also strongly correlated with DXA-based muscle-specific strength in males (r = 0.79) and females (r = 0.72). Associations between the two metrics remained significant after adjustment for age, race and ethnicity, and BMI. Rounded cutoff values for MUAC-based muscle-specific strength were <1.3 kg/cm for low and <1.0 kg/cm for very low values in males. In females, the corresponding cutoff values were <0.9 kg/cm for low and <0.8 kg/cm for very low muscle-specific strength. Exploratory Bland-Altman analyses showed small mean differences between the standardized metrics (0.14 SD in males and -0.02 SD in females), although the 95% limits of agreement indicated individual variability (-1.12 to 1.40 SD in males and -1.79 to 1.74 SD in females).

Our study provides practical, sex-specific reference cutoff values for MUAC-based muscle-specific strength (HGS/MUAC) derived from a population-based sample. This accessible anthropometric metric showed strong correlations with DXA-based muscle-specific strength and small average standardized differences, supporting its potential as a pragmatic surrogate when regional body composition assessment is unavailable. Further validation is needed before its clinical or diagnostic application.

artigos.titulo: Dietary 1,5-anhydro-D-fructose attenuates sarcopenia-related phenotypes: Insights from C. elegans and aged mouse models
artigos.autores: Komiya Y, Sakashita R, Sugiyama M et al.
artigos.destaque: Collectively, these findings demonstrate associations between dietary 1,5-AF supplementation and selected age-related functional and tissue phenotypes in C. elegans and mice. These results highlight the potential of 1,5-AF as a dietary component to support muscle health and promoting healthy aging.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia, the age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass and function, represents a major health challenge. Although 1,5-anhydro-D-fructose (1,5-AF) has been investigated in relation to gut microbiota, oxidative stress, and metabolic disorders, its impact on aging remains unclear. Here, we evaluated the potential of 1,5-AF as a nutrition-based intervention using cross-species aging models. In Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans), 1,5-AF enhanced late-life locomotor activity and upregulated transcripts encoding myofibrillar proteins. In aged mice, 1,5-AF administration improved forelimb grip strength, reduced rimmed vacuole-containing muscle fibers. In addition, 1,5-AF promoted a shift toward a more oxidative muscle fiber phenotype and increased expression of mitochondrial-related proteins. Beyond skeletal muscle, 1,5-AF attenuated hepatic lipid accumulation and fibrosis, while showing a trend toward reduced macrophage accumulation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate associations between dietary 1,5-AF supplementation and selected age-related functional and tissue phenotypes in C. elegans and mice. These results highlight the potential of 1,5-AF as a dietary component to support muscle health and promoting healthy aging.

artigos.titulo: Incretin-Based Therapies and Pulmonary Fibrosis: Preclinical Evidence, Body Composition, and Translational Perspectives: A Narrative Review
artigos.autores: Pianigiani T, Postiferi S, Simoncini F et al.
artigos.destaque: This narrative review integrates current preclinical evidence on the potential antifibrotic effects of incretin-related pathways with clinical evidence on body weight, adiposity, and skeletal muscle in pulmonary fibrosis. Future clinical and translational studies are required to determine whether the potential pulmonary and metabolic effects of incretin-based therapies translate into meaningful clinical benefits in fibrotic interstitial lung disease.

resumo.texto: Pulmonary fibrosis comprises a heterogeneous group of interstitial lung diseases characterized by progressive extracellular matrix deposition and structural remodeling. Although currently available antifibrotic therapies can slow disease progression, additional biological pathways remain under investigation. Incretin-based therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors, have attracted increasing interest because their biological effects extend beyond glucose regulation and may involve pathways relevant to pulmonary fibrogenesis. Preclinical studies suggest that incretin-related pathways may modulate transforming growth factor-β signaling, fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix deposition, mesenchymal transition, inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic mechanisms involved in fibrosis. However, these findings remain predominantly experimental, and evidence of antifibrotic efficacy in patients with fibrotic interstitial lung disease is currently lacking. A complementary aspect is represented by the profound effects of incretin-based therapies on body weight and composition. This is particularly relevant in pulmonary fibrosis, where excess adiposity may contribute to metabolic and functional burden, whereas low body mass index, unintentional weight loss, and skeletal muscle depletion are associated with adverse outcomes. Incretin-induced weight loss predominantly reflects reduction in adipose tissue, but is accompanied by variable reductions in lean or fat-free mass, whose implications for skeletal muscle and functional reserve remain incompletely defined. This narrative review integrates current preclinical evidence on the potential antifibrotic effects of incretin-related pathways with clinical evidence on body weight, adiposity, and skeletal muscle in pulmonary fibrosis. Future clinical and translational studies are required to determine whether the potential pulmonary and metabolic effects of incretin-based therapies translate into meaningful clinical benefits in fibrotic interstitial lung disease.

artigos.titulo: Experiences of compassion fatigue among health and social care practitioners supporting children and young people who self-harm
artigos.revista: Int J Qual Stud Health Well-being
artigos.autores: Fox C, Lee L
artigos.destaque: Clinical implications include the need for health and social care organisations to prioritise targeted workforce wellbeing interventions to better support practitioners and improve care for CYP who self-harm.

resumo.texto: Health and social care (HSC) practitioners are at an increased risk of developing compassion fatigue, particularly when working with vulnerable children and young people (CYP) who self-harm. This can negatively impact both practitioner wellbeing and the quality of patient care. Despite this, no research has explored experiences of compassion fatigue among HSC practitioners supporting CYP who self-harm. This study aimed to explore HSC practitioners' experiences of compassion fatigue when working with this population.
Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 HSC practitioners supporting CYP who self-harm who identified as having experienced compassion fatigue.

Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis (RTA) and three key themes were generated: 'compassion fatigue as an emotional balancing act', 'compassion fatigue as a mismatch between responsibility and influence', and 'professional evolution through compassion fatigue'. The findings highlight the complex interplay of relational, emotional and systemic factors influencing HSC practitioners' experiences of compassion fatigue when supporting CYP who self-harm.

Clinical implications include the need for health and social care organisations to prioritise targeted workforce wellbeing interventions to better support practitioners and improve care for CYP who self-harm.

artigos.titulo: Sleep disturbance and enhanced aggression after chronic mild stress in mice: Association with hypothalamic nerve growth factor
artigos.autores: Chikahisa S, Shiuchi T, Chiba S et al.
artigos.destaque: Intracerebroventricular administration of NGF promoted sleep in control and CMS mice (n = 6-7 per group), but aggressive behaviour was suppressed only in CMS mice (n = 8 per group). These findings suggest that hypothalamic NGF may contribute to mechanisms that link chronic stress-related sleep disturbances with aggressive behaviour, although the precise downstream mechanisms are not known.

resumo.texto: Chronic stress disrupts sleep and induces behavioural abnormalities. However, the mechanisms linking stress-related sleep disturbances to abnormal social behaviour are unclear. In this study, a predictable chronic mild stress (CMS) paradigm was used, in which male mice were housed on a wire mesh for 3 weeks. CMS mice (n = 7 per group) had reduced non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and NREM slow-wave activity, and they had enhanced aggressive behaviour, whereas anxiety- and depression-related behavioural measures were not markedly altered. At the molecular level, CMS was associated with lower hypothalamic Ngf mRNA levels, and hypothalamic NGF protein levels were related to aggressive behaviour. Intracerebroventricular administration of NGF promoted sleep in control and CMS mice (n = 6-7 per group), but aggressive behaviour was suppressed only in CMS mice (n = 8 per group). These findings suggest that hypothalamic NGF may contribute to mechanisms that link chronic stress-related sleep disturbances with aggressive behaviour, although the precise downstream mechanisms are not known.

artigos.titulo: Association of LATE-NC With Neuropathologic Lesions and Cognitive Abilities: A Population-Based Autopsy Study
artigos.autores: Matos Silva C, Justo AFO, Ribeiro Paes V et al.
artigos.destaque: LATE-NC was prevalent and associated with cognitive impairment in this ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and some estimates had wide confidence intervals due to the small number of advanced-stage cases.

resumo.texto: Limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy neuropathologic change (LATE-NC) is a common finding in aging brains. However, most previous studies were limited to ethnoracially homogeneous cohorts from high-income countries. The objective of this study was to investigate the associations between LATE-NC, cognitive performance, and coexisting neuropathologic lesions in a large, ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample from Brazil.

This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the Biobank for Aging Studies, a Brazilian population-based autopsy study based at the University of São Paulo. The study included a consecutive series of autopsies performed between 2004 and 2024. Inclusion criteria required participants to be at least 18 years old with a knowledgeable informant. LATE-NC, Alzheimer disease neuropathologic change (ADNC), Lewy body pathology (LBP), lacunar infarcts, small vessel disease, cerebral amyloid angiopathy, and hippocampal sclerosis were assessed following international criteria. Cognitive abilities were evaluated with the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SOB). Logistic and linear regression models were applied to examine associations of LATE-NC with comorbid neuropathologies and cognitive outcomes, with adjustments for sociodemographic, clinical, and neuropathologic covariates.

The sample comprised 1,860 participants (mean age = 72.6 ± 14.2 years; 49.1% female; 62.2% White; 35.4% Black). LATE-NC was present in 7.4% of participants (stage 1: 3.0%; stage 2: 4.0%; stage 3: 0.4%). After adjustment for sociodemographic, clinical, and other neuropathologic covariates, LATE-NC (stages 2-3) was associated with hippocampal sclerosis (OR = 14.95; 95% CI 7.42-30.27; p < 0.001), advanced Braak NFT stages (OR = 2.23; 95% CI 1.32-3.83; p = 0.003), and LBP (OR = 1.89; 95% CI 1.02-3.37; p = 0.036). Factoring in other pathologies, LATE-NC was associated with the CDR-SOB score (β = 4.06; 95% CI 2.95-5.18; p < 0.001), demonstrating a consistent association with cognition, similar to the one observed for moderate/severe ADNC (β = 3.78; 95% CI 3.14-4.42; p < 0.001) in the same sample.

LATE-NC was prevalent and associated with cognitive impairment in this ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and some estimates had wide confidence intervals due to the small number of advanced-stage cases.

artigos.titulo: Reinterpreting homographs in context
artigos.autores: Woerle TA, Dixon P
artigos.destaque: These ratings were compared to ratings obtained when an unambiguous synonym was substituted for the homograph. The results suggest that in many cases, readers can identify both possible interpretations of the homograph, even after an intervening sentence. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

resumo.texto: When readers encounter an ambiguous homograph, they are typically able to immediately select an appropriate meaning based on the preceding context. However, in cases where there is not enough context to select the correct meaning, it is unclear how readers process the ambiguous word. In the present study, we investigated how readers select meanings of homographs when the disambiguating information is delayed. Participants read two or three sentence passages in which a homograph appeared in the first sentence and the disambiguating information was in the last. After each passage, participants rated how much sense the passage made. These ratings were compared to ratings obtained when an unambiguous synonym was substituted for the homograph. The results suggest that in many cases, readers can identify both possible interpretations of the homograph, even after an intervening sentence. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

artigos.titulo: Mechanistic understanding of the role of the lung-brain axis in the pathogenesis of PM2.5-induced Alzheimer's disease
artigos.autores: Defrancesco AD, Wang B, Yi C et al.
artigos.destaque: We also discuss important modifiers of susceptibility and heterogeneity in reported associations, including pollutant composition, co-exposure to other air pollutants, sex, APOE genotype, and epigenetic reprogramming. Overall, the present review proposes an integrated multi-organ model of PM2.5 neurotoxicity that aligns environmental exposure with key mechanisms of AD pathogenesis and highlights priorities for strengthening causal inference and future translational research.

resumo.texto: Air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5), has emerged as an important yet under-recognised environmental contributor to cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD) across the life course. Although epidemiological studies consistently associate long-term PM2.5 exposure with impaired cognition, from reduced neurodevelopmental performance in children to accelerated neurodegeneration in older adults, the biological mechanisms linking inhaled particles to AD-related brain pathology remain incompletely defined. In the present review, we synthesise current epidemiological and experimental evidence to position the lung-brain axis as a central mechanistic framework through which PM2.5 may influence brain aging and AD pathogenesis. Rather than acting solely through direct particle entry into the brain, PM2.5-induced pulmonary injury initiates systemic signalling cascades, including inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress, blood-brain barrier disruption, and extracellular vesicle-mediated intercellular communication, which together propagate disease signals from the lung to the brain. We further examine how these pathways intersect with core AD-related processes, including amyloid-β accumulation, tau pathology, impaired protein clearance, maladaptive microglial responses, and autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction. We also discuss important modifiers of susceptibility and heterogeneity in reported associations, including pollutant composition, co-exposure to other air pollutants, sex, APOE genotype, and epigenetic reprogramming. Overall, the present review proposes an integrated multi-organ model of PM2.5 neurotoxicity that aligns environmental exposure with key mechanisms of AD pathogenesis and highlights priorities for strengthening causal inference and future translational research.

artigos.titulo: A surprising discovery could help aging muscles repair themselves
artigos.destaque: Scientists have discovered a compound that transforms a natural muscle-repair protein into a more powerful version dubbed "Super HGF," more than doubling its ability to bind to a key receptor while protecting it from age-related chemical damage. The breakthrough, supported by early mouse experiments, could eventually help combat muscle loss and preserve strength as people age.

artigos.titulo: Scientists may have finally explained why our brains and bodies are cross-wired
artigos.destaque: Scientists propose that the brain’s mysterious cross-wiring, which connects each hemisphere to the opposite side of the body, may have originated more than 500 million years ago in the visual systems of ancient fish. Rather than evolving for a specific advantage, this unusual arrangement may simply be a legacy of evolution building new brain circuits on an ancient foundation.

artigos.titulo: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage
artigos.destaque: Stanford researchers have discovered an AI-identified natural molecule that dramatically suppresses appetite and promotes fat loss in animals, potentially offering an Ozempic-like weight-loss treatment without common digestive side effects or significant muscle loss. Called BRP, the molecule reduced food intake by up to 50% and targets a different brain pathway, raising hopes for a more precise obesity treatment if future human trials prove successful.

artigos.titulo: A randomized comparison of comprehensive weight loss intervention vs. usual care on recurrences of atrial fibrillation in obese patients after catheter ablation: HOBIT-AF trial
artigos.autores: Koščálová K, Novodvorský P, Jakubíková I et al.
artigos.destaque: HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

resumo.texto: Obesity is one of the strongest risk factors for the development of atrial fibrillation (AF), and its reduction is associated with the alleviation of AF burden. The HOBIT-AF study aimed to evaluate the impact of complex weight loss interventions on AF recurrence rate in obese individuals after catheter ablation (CA).

The HOBIT-AF was a randomized controlled trial with a 15-month treatment period (3-18 months post CA) involving complex weight-reducing interventions in the active arm. The primary outcome was the change in AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) burden assessed from baseline and the final 14-day Holter monitoring. A total of 167 individuals (aged 59 years, body mass index of 35.6 kg/m2) were randomized into the active (n = 85) and control group (n = 82). At the end of the treatment period, a mean reduction of 6.8 ± 7.0% of the initial body weight accompanied by improvement of metabolic parameters was achieved in the active group. The AF/AT burden change was 0.6 ± 2.5% (95% CI: -4.2-5.5%) in the active group and -0.9 ± 1.8% (95% CI: -4.5-3.0%) in the control group. The AF/AT recurrence-free survival during the 3-18-month follow-up period was comparable between groups (70.4% vs. 69.6%).

HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

artigos.titulo: Functional and body composition outcomes of pharmacological interventions for sarcopenia in older adults: A systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
artigos.autores: Tsutsumi T, Hieda S, Gnanavelou M et al.
artigos.destaque: Functional and body-composition estimates varied across therapeutic Groups and Classes. The observed functional differences were small relative to commonly cited benchmarks, and Class-level evidence was sparse. Future trials should prioritize durable mobility, independence, and safety outcomes.

resumo.texto: Pharmacological trials in sarcopenia have reported changes in muscle mass or selected functional measures, but the consistency and clinical importance of these effects remain uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults aged ≥65 years.
The original review search used MEDLINE and Embase from inception to 9 February 2026.

gov was checked immediately after completion of the systematic review. Interventions were analyzed within four broad therapeutic Groups and complementary pharmacological Classes. Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses used mean differences (MDs) for functional outcomes and Hedges' g standardized mean differences (SMDs) for body-composition outcomes.

Twenty-six RCTs including 3237 participants were included. At the Group level, Hormonal and anabolic therapies showed small pooled differences in grip strength (MD 1.003 kg, 95% CI 0.007 to 2.000) and 6-minute walk distance (MD 12.335 m, 95% CI 5.043 to 19.627). Myostatin inhibitors showed a gait-speed difference of 0.0300 m/s (95% CI 0.0295 to 0.0305) and a single-study estimate for appendicular lean body mass (SMD 0.573, 95% CI 0.291 to 0.855). The functional differences were below commonly cited meaningful-change benchmarks. Class-level evidence was sparse, with several Classes represented by one trial. Functional estimates for RAAS-based and Metabolic therapies were based on few trials and varied across outcomes.

Functional and body-composition estimates varied across therapeutic Groups and Classes. The observed functional differences were small relative to commonly cited benchmarks, and Class-level evidence was sparse. Future trials should prioritize durable mobility, independence, and safety outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Muscle ultrasound for nutrition assessment: Practical clinical protocols
artigos.autores: Bode A, Russell L, Hawes C et al.
artigos.destaque: Limited standardization of acquisition protocols and insufficient access to structured, hands-on operator training continue to hinder reproducibility across clinical settings. Further implementation studies are needed to ensure high-quality measurements are conducted and incorporated into nutritional assessment.

resumo.texto: Muscle ultrasound (mUS) is an emerging and increasingly utilized tool for assessing body composition. Bedside mUS can provide reliable measurements of skeletal muscle and adipose tissue that can strengthen nutrition assessment. As current malnutrition diagnostic frameworks emphasize the evaluation of lean body mass, mUS offers a practical, radiation-free, serial, and accessible method for quantifying muscle status in real time. This review summarizes the existing literature on mUS-based body composition assessment, introduces the technical skills needed for high-quality image acquisition, describes the measurements that may be useful in the assessment of malnutrition, and outlines the need for skills-based training programs. Key parameters include muscle layer thickness, cross-sectional area, echo intensity, pennation angle, and fascicle length. Normative reference values and longitudinal changes are reviewed, as each can help clinicians identify low muscle mass and track meaningful changes over time. Despite the advantages of mUS, adoption within routine nutrition practice remains inconsistent. Limited standardization of acquisition protocols and insufficient access to structured, hands-on operator training continue to hinder reproducibility across clinical settings. Further implementation studies are needed to ensure high-quality measurements are conducted and incorporated into nutritional assessment.

artigos.titulo: Association of Respiratory-Related Sarcopenia Classification With Postoperative Complications and Overall Survival in Older Patients With Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
artigos.autores: Shi J, Tang S, Xu D et al.
artigos.destaque: The classification was associated with postoperative outcomes and overall survival. Its simpler grouping had observed discrimination close to the four-group framework. However, its clinical utility in preoperative optimization still requires further validation in prospective studies.

resumo.texto: Respiratory function and muscle measures have previously been studied together. We evaluated a classification combining peak expiratory flow and a computed tomography-derived pectoralis muscle index in older patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

This retrospective cohort included 742 patients aged ≥65 y undergoing minimally invasive McKeown esophagectomy during 2020-2021. Pectoralis muscle index was the bilateral pectoralis major area at T4 divided by height squared, a surrogate of chest-wall muscle reserve. Two isolated-abnormality phenotypes were combined exploratorily into mild, alongside normal and severe categories. Logistic and Cox regression evaluated associations. Survival discrimination was assessed in the development cohort; stratified Cox sensitivity analyses addressed nonproportional hazards.

Normal, mild, and severe comprised 340, 310, and 92 patients. Adjusted pneumonia odds ratios versus normal were 1.548 (95% confidence interval, 1.039-2.306) for mild and 2.973 (1.746-5.064) for severe. The leakage model retained no other covariates. In the T/N-stratified survival model, hazard ratios were 2.445 (1.948-3.067) and 3.585 (2.618-4.908), respectively. Adding the classification increased the apparent C-index from 0.837 to 0.861. Pneumonia areas under the curve were 0.616 for the four-group framework and 0.613 for the simplified classification.

The classification was associated with postoperative outcomes and overall survival. Its simpler grouping had observed discrimination close to the four-group framework. However, its clinical utility in preoperative optimization still requires further validation in prospective studies.

artigos.titulo: GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonism does not directly drive skeletal muscle atrophy or impair myogenesis in primary human myotubes
artigos.autores: Ditchfield C, Macleod M, Price JMJ et al.
artigos.destaque: Direct GLP-1 and GIP receptor activation did not produce major atrophic, inflammatory, morphological, myogenic, or mitochondrial effects on primary human skeletal muscle myotubes. These findings are consistent with an indirect mechanism underlying the lean mass loss observed with incretin-based therapies, a question of particular relevance as these agents are increasingly used in older adults at risk of sarcopenia.

resumo.texto: GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists produce substantial weight loss in clinical trials but significant loss of lean body mass is reported. Whether this reflects a direct pharmacological effect on skeletal muscle or an indirect consequence of caloric restriction and reduced mechanical loading is unknown. Primary myoblasts were isolated from skeletal muscle of older adults with obesity undergoing orthopaedic surgery. GIPR and GLP-1R expression was characterised by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry. Differentiated myotubes were treated with semaglutide or GIP peptide and assessed for atrophy-related gene expression (qPCR), secretome perturbation (Olink Reveal), mitochondrial and glycolytic bioenergetics (Seahorse XF Real-Time ATP Rate Assay, glucose uptake, lactate secretion) and myotube morphology and myogenesis (immunofluorescence). GIPR mRNA was consistently detected across all donors; GLP-1R mRNA was undetectable by PCR, though LUXendin645 flow cytometry in a subset of three donors identified low-level surface GLP-1R protein in 51-66% of myoblasts. Neither semaglutide nor GIP altered atrophy-related gene expression or the secretome, with no proteins reaching significance. Semaglutide reduced glycolytic and total ATP production rates, accompanied by reduced lactate secretion, suggesting modest suppression of glycolytic flux; mitochondrial parameters were unaffected. Neither treatment impaired myotube thickness or differentiation; GIP increased myotube thickness after 8 days. Direct GLP-1 and GIP receptor activation did not produce major atrophic, inflammatory, morphological, myogenic, or mitochondrial effects on primary human skeletal muscle myotubes. These findings are consistent with an indirect mechanism underlying the lean mass loss observed with incretin-based therapies, a question of particular relevance as these agents are increasingly used in older adults at risk of sarcopenia.

artigos.titulo: Exercise and Nutritional Interventions for Muscle Strength, Physical Performance, and Body Composition Among Older Adults With Sarcopenia or Pre-Sarcopenia: A Network Meta-Analysis
artigos.autores: Yang H, Wang Q, Wang B et al.
artigos.destaque: Exercise and nutritional strategies showed different relative effects across clinical outcomes in older adults with sarcopenia or pre-sarcopenia. Combined exercise and nutrition ranked more favorably for selected muscle-related outcomes, whereas exercise showed a more consistent pattern of benefit for physical performance. These findings require confirmation in high-quality trials because the overall certainty of evidence was limited.

resumo.texto: To compare the relative effects of exercise and nutritional interventions on muscle strength, physical performance, muscle mass, and body composition-related outcomes in older adults with sarcopenia or pre-sarcopenia using network meta-analysis.

PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to August 8, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing exercise, nutritional, or combined interventions with control strategies in older adults with sarcopenia or pre-sarcopenia were included. A frequentist network meta-analysis compared four intervention nodes (Control, Exercise, Nutrition, and Combined). Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2, and certainty of evidence with CINeMA.

Sixty-five reports representing 57 RCTs and 6017 participants were included. Compared with Control, Combined, Nutrition, and Exercise improved handgrip strength, with the largest estimate for Combined (mean difference [MD] 4.29 kg, 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.50-6.07; p-score 0.877). For physical function, Exercise improved the Timed Up and Go test (TUG; MD 1.19 s, 95% CI, 0.72-1.66) and ranked highly for gait speed (MD 0.11 m/s, 95% CI, 0.06-0.17). For appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI), Combined, Exercise, and Nutrition increased ASMI, with Combined ranked highest (MD 0.32 kg/m2, 95% CI, 0.17-0.48; p-score 0.831). Overall certainty of evidence was limited according to CINeMA.

Exercise and nutritional strategies showed different relative effects across clinical outcomes in older adults with sarcopenia or pre-sarcopenia. Combined exercise and nutrition ranked more favorably for selected muscle-related outcomes, whereas exercise showed a more consistent pattern of benefit for physical performance. These findings require confirmation in high-quality trials because the overall certainty of evidence was limited.

artigos.titulo: Shanyu Wan attenuates age-related muscle alterations in SAMP8 mice with improved mitochondrial function
artigos.autores: Hu Y, Xiang Q, Jiang C et al.
artigos.destaque: In vitro, SYW-containing serum attenuated t-BHP-induced oxidative and mitochondrial injury in C2C12 myoblasts, while pharmacological interference experiments suggested the involvement of PGC-1α-related signaling. These findings provide preclinical evidence that SYW may alleviate age-related muscle alterations by improving mitochondrial function and redox balance.

resumo.texto: The traditional Chinese formula Shanyu Wan (SYW), comprising Panax ginseng, Dioscorea opposita Thunb and Atractylodes Rhizoma, has been empirically employed for metabolic regulation, although its mechanistic basis remains incompletely elucidated.

Senescence-accelerated mouse prone 8 (SAMP8) mice were orally administered SYW by gavage at 2.56 g/kg for 8 weeks, with age-matched senescence-accelerated mouse resistant 1 (SAMR1) mice serving as controls. Muscle phenotype was evaluated by forelimb grip strength, rotarod performance, spontaneous locomotor activity, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Histopathological alterations were evaluated by Masson's trichrome staining. Mitochondrial ultrastructure was examined by transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and mitochondrial functional parameters were subsequently determined. Furthermore, the effects of SYW-containing serum on oxidative injury were examined in t-BHP-treated C2C12 myoblasts, together with pharmacological interference analysis of PGC-1α-related signaling.

Oral administration of SYW significantly improved muscle volume, grip strength, and motor performance in SAMP8 mice. These protective effects were accompanied by partial restoration of mitochondrial ultrastructure, increased mitochondrial respiratory chain complex activity, reduced oxidative stress, and changes in PGC-1α-related signaling. In vitro, SYW-containing serum attenuated t-BHP-induced oxidative and mitochondrial injury in C2C12 myoblasts, while pharmacological interference experiments suggested the involvement of PGC-1α-related signaling. These findings provide preclinical evidence that SYW may alleviate age-related muscle alterations by improving mitochondrial function and redox balance.

artigos.titulo: Tirzepatide for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea: from apnea-hypopnea index reduction to cardiometabolic risk mitigation-a narrative review
artigos.autores: Mesfin-Bireda S, Hillman Urek K
artigos.destaque: Tirzepatide may help frame OSA as a multifactorial and partially metabolically treatable disease and may represent a clinically meaningful expansion of treatment options alongside, rather than as a replacement for, established mechanical and procedural therapies. The available evidence is anchored in a single phase 3 trial program and limited by short follow-up and the absence of definitive comparative and long-term outcome data. Long-term durability of effect after discontinuation, generalizability beyond the SURMOUNT-OSA-eligible population, OSA-specific economic analysis, and head-to-head comparisons against CPAP remain the principal unsettled questions requiring dedicated long-term studies before firm clinical recommendations can be made.

resumo.texto: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a chronic respiratory disorder with nocturnal oxygen desaturation that is often associated with multisystemic sequelae such as hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, and increased morbidity and mortality. Obesity has been proposed as a modifiable risk factor; hence, the recent shift in focus to investigating anti-obesity medications for the management of OSA. Tirzepatide is the first U.S. FDA-approved pharmacotherapy for the treatment of moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity to be utilized in combination with low caloric intake and physical activity, given its prior success in managing type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity.

This narrative review evaluates tirzepatide and the SURMOUNT-OSA trial program as the key contemporary anchors for the pharmacological treatment of OSA in adults with concurrent obesity. Because the randomized evidence base currently comprises a single pivotal trial program, the review centers on SURMOUNT-OSA and its prespecified endpoints along with post hoc analyses, supplemented by observational, modeling, and mechanistic studies.

In the SURMOUNT-OSA program, tirzepatide produced randomized, placebo-controlled reductions in the apnea-hypopnea index, sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, and systemic inflammation. The program was designed around respiratory and metabolic endpoints rather than clinical events, so it cannot support conclusions about mortality, cardiovascular, or renal outcomes. Favorable signals for those events, including all-cause mortality, major adverse kidney events, and major adverse cardiovascular events, come only from nonrandomized observational cohorts and are best regarded as directional and exploratory rather than definitive.

Tirzepatide may help frame OSA as a multifactorial and partially metabolically treatable disease and may represent a clinically meaningful expansion of treatment options alongside, rather than as a replacement for, established mechanical and procedural therapies. The available evidence is anchored in a single phase 3 trial program and limited by short follow-up and the absence of definitive comparative and long-term outcome data. Long-term durability of effect after discontinuation, generalizability beyond the SURMOUNT-OSA-eligible population, OSA-specific economic analysis, and head-to-head comparisons against CPAP remain the principal unsettled questions requiring dedicated long-term studies before firm clinical recommendations can be made.

artigos.titulo: Next-generation incretin therapeutics for polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: navigating current pipeline and clinical considerations
artigos.autores: Ozgen Saydam B, Yıldız BO
artigos.destaque: Whether reproductive benefits are independent of weight loss, persist after treatment withdrawal, or differ across PMOS phenotypes is uncertain. Phenotype-stratified randomized trials with standardized reproductive, metabolic, cardiovascular and safety endpoints are needed to determine whether multi-incretins provide durable benefits beyond weight control while maintaining reproductive safety and accessibility.

resumo.texto: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a complex metabolic-reproductive disorder managed with lifestyle interventions, metformin, and symptom-directed therapies. Incretin-based therapies offer substantial metabolic benefits, but their reproductive efficacy, durability, and phenotypic safety remain incompletely defined.

This narrative review examines the therapeutic evolution from single glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists to dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonism with tirzepatide and triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonism with retatrutide. A structured PubMed search of studies published from January 2023 to October 2026 was supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov and reference-list screening. Evidence was evaluated across metabolic, hormonal, and reproductive outcomes.

Single GLP-1 receptor agonists, particularly semaglutide, improve weight, adiposity, and insulin resistance, with emerging evidence of reproductive benefits. Multi-incretin therapies may provide greater reductions in body weight, visceral and ectopic fat, and insulin resistance. However, PMOS-specific reproductive evidence remains limited. Whether reproductive benefits are independent of weight loss, persist after treatment withdrawal, or differ across PMOS phenotypes is uncertain. Phenotype-stratified randomized trials with standardized reproductive, metabolic, cardiovascular and safety endpoints are needed to determine whether multi-incretins provide durable benefits beyond weight control while maintaining reproductive safety and accessibility.

artigos.titulo: Psychosocial stressors at work and hypertension incidence: a prospective cohort study of multiple exposures
artigos.autores: Konan FA, Milot A, Brisson C et al.
artigos.destaque: Psychosocial stressors at work from the job strain and ERI models were associated, separately and in combination, with an increased risk of hypertension.

resumo.texto: Psychosocial stressors at work from the job strain and effort-reward imbalance (ERI) models are frequent and modifiable exposures associated with increased blood pressure levels. The adverse effect of combined exposure to both work stressors on hypertension incidence remains unknown. This study aimed to examine this association in a long-term prospective cohort.

The study included 9188 white-collar workers recruited at T1 (1991-1993), with follow-ups at T2 (1999-2001) and T3 (2015-2018). Exposures to psychosocial stressors at work from the job strain (T1 and T2) and ERI (T2) models were measured using validated instruments. Incident hypertension cases were identified using medico-administrative databases and automated office blood pressure measurements. Semi-parametric proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HR). Analyses included normotensive workers at baseline: N = 6732 over 24 years (T1 to T3) and N = 4516 over 18 years (T2 to T3).

Over 24 years, workers exposed to passive jobs [low psychological demands and low decision latitude; HR = 1.19 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.05-1.34)], active jobs [high psychological demands and high decision latitude; HR = 1.23 (95% CI: 1.08-1.40)], and high strain [high psychological demands and low decision latitude; HR = 1.26 (95% CI: 1.11-1.44)] had an increased risk of hypertension. Over 18 years, workers exposed to active jobs [HR = 1.20 (95% CI: 1.03-1.39)], ERI [HR = 1.19 (95% CI: 1.06-1.33)], and both [HR = 1.34 (95% CI: 1.14-1.56)] had an increased risk of hypertension.
Psychosocial stressors at work from the job strain and ERI models were associated, separately and in combination, with an increased risk of hypertension.

artigos.titulo: Shame as a Struggle for Human Worth and Belonging-Experiences of Shame Related to Life-Suffering
artigos.autores: Fjelltvedt RL, Koskinen C
artigos.destaque: Shame, as a lived and dynamic force intertwined with life suffering, shapes human beings' understanding of self, human worth, belonging, relationships and capacity to act. Being seen, acknowledged and received by others in ways that affirm human dignity and restore vitality and agency. Rather than needing to be eliminated, shame may be borne, reconciled with and transformed through experiences of meaning, recognition and connection. In this way, existential vulnerability emerges not only as a source of suffering but also as an opening toward renewed meaning, hope and courage to live.

resumo.texto: Research indicates that shame may undermine self-worth, particularly in societies marked by high demands for self-realization and individual responsibility, where failures are often internalized. Shame is a pervasive and potentially harmful affect, closely linked to self-evaluation, mental health and societal expectations, yet its lived and existential dimensions remain insufficiently explored. In this study, shame is understood in relation to life-suffering, an ontological dimension of suffering that touches the whole human being when dignity, belonging, life understanding and possibilities of being are challenged.
The study aims to deepen the understanding of shame as it is experienced and expressed, using life-suffering as a theoretical framework.

Hermeneutical reading of classic texts was used as the methodological framework and research method. Two contemporary novels written by Marie Aubert and Helga Flatland were selected as material for reading and interpretation.

The findings highlight shame as an interplay between desire and self-disqualification, embodied shame and the vanishing self, shame arising from the sense of being different, shame as a generalized sense of not being enough as a human being, the shame of wanting to stand out, shame as unmet expectations and the sense of living the wrong life, and shame as the breaking point that opens new possibilities and dreams.

Shame, as a lived and dynamic force intertwined with life suffering, shapes human beings' understanding of self, human worth, belonging, relationships and capacity to act. Being seen, acknowledged and received by others in ways that affirm human dignity and restore vitality and agency. Rather than needing to be eliminated, shame may be borne, reconciled with and transformed through experiences of meaning, recognition and connection. In this way, existential vulnerability emerges not only as a source of suffering but also as an opening toward renewed meaning, hope and courage to live.

artigos.titulo: The clinical impact of burnout among peritoneal dialysis patients
artigos.autores: Chen YA, Lin YC, Chou YH et al.
artigos.destaque: In contrast, the association between high cynicism and all-cause mortality was attenuated after adjustment for age and sex and did not reach statistical significance (adjusted HR, 3.80; 95% CI, 0.78-18.58; p = .099).ConclusionsBurnout and anxiety are common among patients undergoing PD. High cynicism was independently associated with an increased risk of transfer to HD, highlighting the potential importance of psychological well-being in PD care.

resumo.texto: BackgroundPeritoneal dialysis (PD) requires intensive daily self-management and may impose a substantial psychological burden on patients. However, the prevalence of burnout among PD patients and its association with clinical outcomes remain unclear. This study investigated the prevalence of burnout and anxiety among patients undergoing PD and their associations with clinical outcomes.MethodsIn this prospective observational cohort study, patients undergoing PD at National Taiwan University Hospital were assessed using the Maslach Burnout Inventory, and the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory. Patients were followed for transfer to hemodialysis (HD) and all-cause mortality. Associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.ResultsAmong 183 patients who completed the questionnaires, 24.0% had emotional exhaustion and 19.7% had severe anxiety. During follow-up, high cynicism was associated with an increased risk of transfer to HD. In the age- and sex-adjusted Cox proportional hazards model, high cynicism remained significantly associated with transfer to HD (adjusted hazard ratio (HR), 3.47; 95% CI, 1.14-10.58; p = .029). In contrast, the association between high cynicism and all-cause mortality was attenuated after adjustment for age and sex and did not reach statistical significance (adjusted HR, 3.80; 95% CI, 0.78-18.58; p = .099).ConclusionsBurnout and anxiety are common among patients undergoing PD. High cynicism was independently associated with an increased risk of transfer to HD, highlighting the potential importance of psychological well-being in PD care.

artigos.titulo: Bakuchiol mitigates neuronal dysfunction in estrogen deficient chronic unpredictable mild stress rats: insights from in vivo and in-silico studies
artigos.autores: Bag S, Bansal S, Chaudhary R et al.
artigos.destaque: Molecular dynamics studies also supported these results via showing stable and energetically favoured interactions of Bakuchiol with BDNF-TrkB and acetylcholinesterase. Our current study shows that Bakuchiol at doses of 20 & 40 mg/kg dose dependently possess the potential to alleviate the neurological disorder in estrogen deficient chronic stress conditions.

resumo.texto: Estrogen deficiency in post-menopausal women leads to the development of neurodegenerative disorders. Phytoestrogens are plant-derived compounds that represent novel and safer alternatives to hormone replacement therapy for the treatment of neurological disorders in postmenopausal complications. Bakuchiol is a phytoestrogen exhibiting selective estrogen like effects. The present study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective and antidepressant potential of bakuchiol in ovariectomised rats subjected to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) exposure. Adult Female Wistar rats were bilaterally ovariectomised (OVX) and subjected to CUMS over a period of four weeks in order to mimic the development of depression and cognitive deficits in menopause. At the end of the study, basic physiological and neurobehavioral parameters, biochemical estimation, and serum corticosterone levels were evaluated. Levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), Acetylcholinesterase were evaluated and histopathological changes were also studied. In silico Molecular docking studies carried out against proteins TrkB receptor (PDB ID: 4AT5) and Human Acetylcholinesterase (PDB ID: 4EY7). Molecular dynamics studies carried out to study ligand-protein interaction stability. Treatment with bakuchiol and 17-β estradiol (E2) significantly restores the pathological changes towards normal levels. However, the protective effect of bakuchiol was completely abolished when administered in the presence of Fulvestrant in OVX + CUMS groups of rats. The in-silico results further corroborate the observed in vitro results. Bakuchiol showed binding affinities of -6.052 kcal/mol and -5.493 kcal/mol toward BDNF-TrkB and AChE, respectively showing its neurotrophic and antidepressant effects. Molecular dynamics studies also supported these results via showing stable and energetically favoured interactions of Bakuchiol with BDNF-TrkB and acetylcholinesterase. Our current study shows that Bakuchiol at doses of 20 & 40 mg/kg dose dependently possess the potential to alleviate the neurological disorder in estrogen deficient chronic stress conditions.

artigos.titulo: Exposure, constraint, and repair: How child abuse pediatrics fellows navigate strain and restore purpose
artigos.autores: Benavides JL, Parmenter S, Nurre OM et al.
artigos.destaque: Fellows linked strain and restoration to exposure, supervision, and opportunities for recovery. Their accounts identify workload organization and supervisory support as areas for evaluation alongside individual coping.

resumo.texto: Child Abuse Pediatrics (CAP) fellows train in a subspecialty marked by repeated exposure to child maltreatment and high-stakes clinical and legal demands.
This qualitative study examined how CAP fellows describe and make meaning of emotional strain and restorative experiences during training.
Participants were 13 fellows enrolled in U.S. CAP fellowship programs, all practicing in urban settings.

Semi-structured interviews were conducted via Zoom between May and August 2024 and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Vicarious resilience sensitized the analysis to restorative experiences; the job demands-resources model informed interpretation after themes were constructed.

Three themes were constructed. Carrying What Cannot Be Left Behind described secondary traumatic stress as an accumulating presence that affected relationships and prompted protective silence. Procedural Continuity, Eroding Presence captured accounts of emotional numbing, constrained agency, and cumulative exposure that strained emotional presence even as fellows described continuing clinical tasks. When the Work Gives Back described how children's recovery, family recognition, and perceived accountability renewed meaning.

Fellows linked strain and restoration to exposure, supervision, and opportunities for recovery. Their accounts identify workload organization and supervisory support as areas for evaluation alongside individual coping.

artigos.titulo: Beyond diagnostics: a scoping review of generative artificial intelligence for clinical documentation and client communication in veterinary practice
artigos.autores: Bava R, Ruga S, Palma E et al.
artigos.destaque: GenAI demonstrates substantial technical promise for automating veterinary documentation and client communication tasks, yet the evidence base is characterized by a pronounced validation gap: operational and human-centric outcomes remain virtually unquantified.

resumo.texto: To systematically map the current landscape of generative AI (GenAI) and large language model applications for clinical documentation and client communication in veterinary medicine, critically appraise validation depth, and identify barriers to real-world adoption.

Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, CAB Abstracts, and IEEE Xplore were searched for original research published between January 2020 and June 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data using a 4-dimensional validation matrix (technical accuracy, clinical quality and safety, operational impact, and human-centric impact). Synthesis was conceptually grounded in the job demands-resources model.

10 studies met the inclusion criteria: 6 addressed clinical documentation (automated clinical coding, information extraction, and generation of subjective, objective, assessment, and plan [ie, SOAP] notes), and 4 addressed client communication (veterinary triage and automated query responses). While technical accuracy was frequently assessed, operational impact was evaluated in only 1 study, and no study employed validated psychometric instruments to measure burnout. Key barriers included clinical hallucinations, data privacy concerns, poor interoperability with practice information management systems, and absence of veterinary-specific fine-tuning.

GenAI demonstrates substantial technical promise for automating veterinary documentation and client communication tasks, yet the evidence base is characterized by a pronounced validation gap: operational and human-centric outcomes remain virtually unquantified.

Until rigorous evidence emerges, veterinarians should approach commercially available AI tools with cautious optimism. Future research must prioritize pragmatic, multicenter prospective trials employing multidimensional validation frameworks to generate evidence supporting safe clinical deployment.

artigos.titulo: Impact of Ambient Scribes on Primary Care Communication Pathways: Qualitative Observation and Interview Study
artigos.autores: Huang N, Jelich K, Truong K et al.
artigos.destaque: Integrating ambient scribes introduces a triadic interactional dynamic into traditionally dyadic patient consultations. Clinicians must continuously navigate the boundaries between patient-facing empathy and scribe-facing precision, deciding when to articulate clinical reasoning aloud and when to exercise verbal discretion regarding sensitive disclosures. While ambient scribes effectively reduce in-encounter computer screen time, they do not eliminate documentation overhead-they redistribute it from real-time typing to postencounter cognitive recall and verbal note curation. To prevent delayed cognitive fatigue from postencounter error verification, we suggest that future ambient scribes should move beyond passive transcription to incorporate interactive recall scaffolding and context-aware error prevention.

resumo.texto: The administrative burden of manual documentation has been a primary driver of physician burnout and a barrier to patient-centered care. Ambient scribes have emerged as a promising solution that uses passive audio capture and natural language processing to automate clinical note-taking. While their impact on clinical efficiency is frequently studied, there is a lack of research on how these tools have impacted interpersonal communication during clinical encounters.

This study investigates the communication pathways and interactional shifts that occur when ambient scribes are integrated into primary care, with a focus on how physicians adapt their behavior to accommodate an ambient digital listener.

We conducted a qualitative study with 17 licensed family practice physicians in the Greater Toronto Area who use ambient scribes in their daily practice. Data collection included observations from in-person clinical shadowing (n=5) and think-aloud walk-throughs (n=12), each followed by semistructured interviews; reported findings are predominantly drawn from interview data. We analyzed the combined dataset using iterative thematic analysis and open coding to identify affordances and constraints along 3 communication pathways: physician-to-patient, physician-to-patient-and-scribe, and physician-to-note.

Along the physician-to-patient pathway, participants reported that ambient scribes increased their capacity to demonstrate active listening, with some reporting greater attentiveness to nonverbal cues, yet introducing the technology to patients to obtain consent consumed limited consultation time, particularly when addressing sensitive health concerns. Along the physician-to-patient-and-scribe pathway, participants appreciated how ambient scribes acted as a forcing function for physicians to verbalize their clinical reasoning to enhance patient comprehension, as well as their scribes' ability to follow and organize nonlinear conversations. However, they reported that scribes frequently omitted implicit information (eg, deictic gestures) or created unintended documentation artifacts (eg, casual remarks about family members) that required post hoc corrections. Along the physician-to-note pathway, participants reported that scribes optimized their note-taking workflows and enabled note manipulation via spoken words for some physicians but recalling patient information to fix transcription errors and support patient follow-ups proved challenging.

Integrating ambient scribes introduces a triadic interactional dynamic into traditionally dyadic patient consultations. Clinicians must continuously navigate the boundaries between patient-facing empathy and scribe-facing precision, deciding when to articulate clinical reasoning aloud and when to exercise verbal discretion regarding sensitive disclosures. While ambient scribes effectively reduce in-encounter computer screen time, they do not eliminate documentation overhead-they redistribute it from real-time typing to postencounter cognitive recall and verbal note curation. To prevent delayed cognitive fatigue from postencounter error verification, we suggest that future ambient scribes should move beyond passive transcription to incorporate interactive recall scaffolding and context-aware error prevention.

artigos.titulo: Personality Traits and Professional Quality of Life in Volunteer Ski Patrollers
artigos.autores: Stubbers KM, Christiansen LR
artigos.destaque: Organizations could use this data to design tailored interventions to support ski patrollers in managing occupational trauma exposure. Individuals high in neuroticism endorsed more negative outcomes and could potentially benefit most from preventative measures and intervention compared to those high in extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness.

resumo.texto: IntroductionSki patrollers, as outdoor emergency first responders, face unique occupational trauma exposure that impacts their professional quality of life. Despite these exposures, this population has been largely understudied in trauma research. Personality traits have been associated with outcomes from occupational trauma exposure in other populations. This study investigates associations between personality traits and outcomes including compassion fatigue and satisfaction in volunteer ski patrollers.MethodsVolunteers from a ski patrol in the Pacific Northwest (n = 82) completed a cross-sectional online survey measuring trauma exposure, the 5-factor model personality traits (neuroticism, extraversion, agreeableness, openness, and conscientiousness), and professional quality of life variables of compassion fatigue (comprising burnout and secondary traumatic stress [STS]) and compassion satisfaction.ResultsThose who reported trauma exposure while patrolling endorsed higher compassion satisfaction and lower burnout. Extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness correlated negatively with burnout and positively with compassion satisfaction. Extraversion and conscientiousness negatively correlated with STS, while neuroticism positively correlated with burnout and STS but negatively correlated with compassion satisfaction.ConclusionsOur findings highlight the association between personality traits and professional quality of life outcomes. Organizations could use this data to design tailored interventions to support ski patrollers in managing occupational trauma exposure. Individuals high in neuroticism endorsed more negative outcomes and could potentially benefit most from preventative measures and intervention compared to those high in extraversion, agreeableness, and conscientiousness.

artigos.titulo: Effects of digital stress-management interventions in breast cancer patients 18 months after intervention access
artigos.autores: Svendsen K, Nes LS, Leithe S et al.
artigos.destaque: Neither CBI nor MBI showed statistically significant improvements at 18 months compared to controls. The results however suggest that long-term access to stress management interventions may help young women with breast cancer and those with high initial stress to reduce their stress levels.

resumo.texto: Digital stress-management tools show promise, but their long-term impact remains unclear. In the Coping After Breast Cancer (CABC) trial, the app-based stress-management program StressProffen, with either cognitive behavioral therapy intervention (CBI) or a mindfulness-based intervention (MBI), showed no advantage over usual care after six months of access. However, benefits may emerge gradually, as users need time not only to become familiar with the content and techniques, but also to internalize, apply and automatize their use in response to real-life stressors. The a priori defined aims of the current study were to examine; 1) whether extended (18 months) access to the digital stress-management interventions CBI and MBI were associated with changes in perceived stress (stress) (primary outcome), measures of health-related quality of life, mindfulness, fatigue, coping, anxiety, depression, and sleep (secondary outcomes), 2) association between app use and changes in stress level and investigate baseline characteristics as moderators of change in stress in the intervention groups, and 3) identify predictors of change in stress among patients with breast cancer.

Of 430 patients randomized to MBI, CBI, or usual care, 76% (n = 327) completed the 18-month survey. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess between-group differences in primary and secondary outcomes. Moderator analyses were performed to examine whether specific baseline characteristics modified the intervention effects on stress levels. Predictor analysis of change in stress was performed for the total sample.

At 18 months, all three groups showed stable trends over time, with no significant difference between either intervention group and controls. A larger stress reduction was observed among younger participants (≤50 years) in both CBI and MBI compared to controls. Higher baseline stress levels predicted significantly larger stress reductions in the total sample, but the moderator analysis showed that the effects were only significant in the CBI group.

Neither CBI nor MBI showed statistically significant improvements at 18 months compared to controls. The results however suggest that long-term access to stress management interventions may help young women with breast cancer and those with high initial stress to reduce their stress levels.
ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT04480203.

artigos.titulo: Burnout among urologists and urology trainees in Denmark
artigos.autores: Madsen MG, Tolouee S, Blichert-Refsgaard L et al.
artigos.destaque: Thirty-two percent of urologists and urology trainees in Denmark experience moderate to severe burnout, linked to psychosocial work conditions. These findings highlight the need to engage in dialogue around work-life expectations, workplace-focused prevention strategies to support career longevity, and ensure a stable workforce capable of delivering safe, high-quality patient care.

resumo.texto: Limited information exists on burnout among European urologists and urology trainees. This study aimed to explore prevalence of burnout and identify related workplace characteristics among practicing urologists and urology trainees in Denmark.

In April 2025, we conducted an anonymous nation-wide online survey of urologists and urology trainees working in a public healthcare department of Urology in Denmark. Burnout and psychosocial work environment factors were evaluated using validated assessment tools.

Of the 297 participants invited, 73% (n = 216) completed the survey. Respondents had a mean age of 45.8 years (standard deviation [SD] ± 10.8), 52% (n = 113) were women, and 70% (n = 152) were specialists. Personal burnout was the most prevalent domain, affecting 80.1% (n = 173) of respondents, including 47.7% (n = 103) with mild, 29.6% (n = 64) with moderate, and 2.8% (n = 6) with severe burnout. Personal burnout scores varied significantly by position (p = 0.035) and speciality tenure (p = 0.008). Psychosocial work environment factors differed across groups and departments. Strongest associations with burnout were observed for 'possibilities for performing work tasks', 'emotional demands', and 'unnecessary work tasks', with a notable link between work-related burnout and 'influence at work', alongside factors related to job demands and interpersonal relations. Female respondents reported higher personal (p = 0.003) and work-related (p = 0.011) burnout scores.

Thirty-two percent of urologists and urology trainees in Denmark experience moderate to severe burnout, linked to psychosocial work conditions. These findings highlight the need to engage in dialogue around work-life expectations, workplace-focused prevention strategies to support career longevity, and ensure a stable workforce capable of delivering safe, high-quality patient care.

artigos.titulo: Effects of Creative Arts Therapy on Psychological Outcomes and Stress-Related Physiological Markers in Children With Cancer: A Systematic Review
artigos.autores: Kristiawati K, Nursalam N, Qona'ah A et al.
artigos.destaque: A smaller subset of studies reported potential benefits for physiological markers, including heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, cortisol levels, hemodynamic status, and hematologic indicators. CAT may support psychological well-being, symptom relief, and stress regulation among children with cancer and may be a useful complement to supportive care in pediatric oncology, although further rigorous trials using standardized outcomes are needed.

resumo.texto: Children with cancer frequently experience psychological distress and symptom-related challenges during diagnosis, treatment, and hospitalization. Creative arts therapy (CAT) has been used as a complementary approach to support emotional expression, coping, and stress regulation; however, its effects on psychological outcomes and stress-related physiological markers remain unclear.
