artigos.titulo: Unleashing children's potential: An evidence-based narrative review of strategies to enhance cognitive function and intelligence in school-age children
artigos.autores: Al-Beltagi M
artigos.destaque: Finally, we propose priorities for multimodal, personalized, and scalable interventions, informed by perspectives from precision education, implementation science, and longitudinal research. By integrating neuroscientific, educational, and psychosocial insights, this review provides actionable recommendations for clinicians, educators, and policymakers to maximize children's cognitive potential, academic achievement, and long-term adaptive outcomes.

resumo.texto: School-age cognitive development (6-12 years) represents a critical window of neural plasticity, during which intelligence and executive function can be meaningfully enhanced. Once considered largely fixed, these cognitive capacities are now recognized as dynamic, multifactorial, and modifiable through environmental, nutritional, educational, and psychosocial interventions. This review synthesizes current evidence on strategies to optimize cognitive function in typically developing children as well as special populations, including those with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, learning disabilities, twice exceptional profiles, or socio-economic disadvantage. We examine the impact of macronutrient and micronutrient intake, gut-brain interactions, physical activity, sleep quality, parenting practices, stress regulation, educational curricula, digital learning tools, mindfulness, and social-emotional learning, highlighting mechanistic pathways, intervention effectiveness, and population-specific considerations. Methodological challenges, including heterogeneity, cultural bias, and translational gaps, are critically appraised. Finally, we propose priorities for multimodal, personalized, and scalable interventions, informed by perspectives from precision education, implementation science, and longitudinal research. By integrating neuroscientific, educational, and psychosocial insights, this review provides actionable recommendations for clinicians, educators, and policymakers to maximize children's cognitive potential, academic achievement, and long-term adaptive outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Brain and Cardiometabolic Effects of Major Weight Loss in People With Obesity: Preliminary Cohort Findings
artigos.autores: Gaggi NL, Hurwitz B, Bernal J et al.
artigos.destaque: Achieving ≥ 40% excess-weight loss was associated with improvements in metabolic health and brain structure, including favorable subcortical volume increases. These findings underscore the potential of sustained weight reduction to mitigate risks linked to metabolic syndromes and neurodegeneration. Longer-term follow-up is warranted to determine whether continued metabolic improvements lead to detectable cognitive gains and additional brain-health benefits beyond 1 year.

resumo.texto: Given the overlap between obesity-related metabolic and vascular abnormalities and Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk factors, it is critical to determine whether weight loss improves brain and cardiovascular health. This study examined whether ≥ 40% excess-weight loss is associated with improvements in cardiometabolic risk, brain structure, and cognition.

The study was a longitudinal study of individuals with obesity undergoing metabolic and bariatric surgery or medical/behavioral weight-loss treatment. Participants were classified at follow-up as weight-loss (WL; ≥ 40% excess-weight loss) or non-weight-loss (nWL; < 40%). All completed medical evaluations, structural MRI, and cognitive testing at baseline and 1 year.

At 1 year, the WL group exhibited improvements in BMI, HbA1C, inflammatory, metabolic, and lipid profiles. MRI-based volumetrics revealed increases in subcortical gray-matter volume and preservation of AD-vulnerable regions. Cognitive performance remained unchanged.

Achieving ≥ 40% excess-weight loss was associated with improvements in metabolic health and brain structure, including favorable subcortical volume increases. These findings underscore the potential of sustained weight reduction to mitigate risks linked to metabolic syndromes and neurodegeneration. Longer-term follow-up is warranted to determine whether continued metabolic improvements lead to detectable cognitive gains and additional brain-health benefits beyond 1 year.

artigos.titulo: Black Myrobalan (Terminalia chebula) as a potential multitarget neuroprotective agent: Translational insights and future directions in neurodegenerative diseases
artigos.autores: Ghiasvand K, Meftahi GH
artigos.destaque: T. chebula extracts and some isolated compounds have also been shown to improve cognitive function, reduce neuroinflammation, and protect dopaminergic neurons, and ameliorate neurotoxic effects of amyloid-β or α-synuclein through in vitro and in vivo animal studies. A review of the contributions from the phytochemistry, mechanism of action, preclinical, translational, and adjunctive applications of Terminalia chebula in neurodegenerative disease therapy is presented here.

resumo.texto: Myrobalan or Haritaki (Terminalia chebula Retz.) has been integrated into Ayurvedic, Unani, and even Tibetan medicine systems for over 2000 years. The "King of Medicines" has traditionally been used for diverse ailments such as digestive issues, wound healing, and general body strengthening. Now, modern medicine is focusing on the myrobalan's potential neuroprotective properties and its use in Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) neurodegenerative disorders. These ailments are characterized by some combination of enduring oxidative damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, irregular protein aggregation, and progressive neuron cell death. Most of the current treatment options revolve around addressing the symptoms of the diseases, which is insufficient as the underlying disease continues to progress. There is an urgent need to devise therapies that work simultaneously on multiple disease pathways. Some of the noted secondary metabolites in T. chebula include hydrolyzable tannins like chebulinic and chebulagic acid as well as corilagin. Others occur as phenolic acids such as gallic and ellagic acid and flavonoids quercetin and kaempferol. Moreover, glycosides, sterols, and a wide range of alkaloids are also present. A number of these compounds are known to possess multifunctional biological properties like scavenging ROS, activating Nrf2/ARE signaling, downregulating pro-inflammatory mediators through blockade of NF-κB, and exerting protective effects on the mitochondria, as well as modulating apoptosis via Bcl-2 and caspases. T. chebula extracts and some isolated compounds have also been shown to improve cognitive function, reduce neuroinflammation, and protect dopaminergic neurons, and ameliorate neurotoxic effects of amyloid-β or α-synuclein through in vitro and in vivo animal studies. A review of the contributions from the phytochemistry, mechanism of action, preclinical, translational, and adjunctive applications of Terminalia chebula in neurodegenerative disease therapy is presented here.

artigos.titulo: Chitosan nanoparticles functionalised with protocatechuic acid improve colon-targeted pazopanib delivery with multi-pathway therapeutic regulation and pharmacokinetic optimisation in colorectal cancer
artigos.autores: Maheshwari T, Bhattacharya S
artigos.destaque: Gut microbiota analysis involves fecal cultures on MacConkey, Lombard-Dowell, and anaerobic agar. Major outcomes include increased maximum concentration to 0.553 micrograms per milliliter, decreased time to maximum concentration to 0.5 hours, increased GPx-1 to 8.828 nanograms per milliliter, decreased LPO to 8.929 nanograms per milliliter, decreased IL-6 to 36.59 nanograms per milliliter, hemolysis remaining at 0.8 percent, and latency decreased to 58 seconds.

resumo.texto: Poor pharmacokinetics, insufficient tumor-selective drug accumulation, and systemic toxicity are often the main obstacles to colorectal cancer (CRC) treatment. Here, protocatechuic acid-functionalized chitosan nanoparticles (PAZ-CS-PCA-NPs) were designed to enhance the pharmacological efficacy of pazopanib via colon-targeted administration. Ionic gelation and EDC/NHS functionalization were used to create PAZ-CS-PCA-NPs, which were then assessed for hemocompatibility, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, therapeutic efficacy, gut microbiota regulation, cognitive function, and safety in a rat model of colorectal cancer induced by dimethylhydrazine. After five hours, PAZ-CS-PCA-NPs showed less than 0.8% haemolysis and kept platelet aggregation at about 20% as opposed to more than 90% in the positive Control. With improved colonic accumulation, as verified by fluorescence imaging, subsequent to intraperitoneal delivery, the nanoformulation significantly reduced the Tmax from 8.0 ± 0.5 h to 0.5 ± 0.1 h and elevated the Cmax from 0.377 ± 0.024 to 0.553 ± 0.020 μg mL⁻1. Treatment increased GPx-1 from 2.578 to 8.828 ng mL⁻1, decreased LPO from 26.874 to 8.929 ng mL⁻1, and lowered IL-6 from 472.6 to 36.59 ng mL⁻1. Furthermore, PAZ-CS-PCA-NPs revealed no significant treatment-related organ histopathological changes during acute toxicity assessment, reduced Morris water maze escape latency from 113.6 s to 58 s, altered the abundance of selected cultivable fecal bacterial populations under the tested culture conditions, and provided a translational nanotherapeutic approach for targeted CRC therapy.

This graphic summarizes the synthesis, characterization, targeted delivery, therapeutic efficacy, and major outcomes of PAZ-CS-PCA nanoparticles for colorectal cancer treatment in rats. The nanoparticles are synthesized by combining pazonanib, chitosan, and protocatechuic acid, forming chitosan nanoparticles with a PCA-grafted surface carrying pazonanib. Characterization includes a Morris water maze test showing escape latency reduced to 58 seconds with the nanoparticles, and hemocompatibility tests indicating reduced hemolysis and platelet aggregation. Targeted delivery is demonstrated by enhanced colonic uptake in Wister rats, with treatments showing reduced colorectal tumors, restored normal colon architecture, decreased tumor sizes on CT scans, suppressed disease-related anatomical distortion on radiography, and good acute tolerability. Therapeutic efficacy data show an increase in maximum concentration from 0.377 to 0.553 micrograms per milliliter. Gut microbiota analysis involves fecal cultures on MacConkey, Lombard-Dowell, and anaerobic agar. Major outcomes include increased maximum concentration to 0.553 micrograms per milliliter, decreased time to maximum concentration to 0.5 hours, increased GPx-1 to 8.828 nanograms per milliliter, decreased LPO to 8.929 nanograms per milliliter, decreased IL-6 to 36.59 nanograms per milliliter, hemolysis remaining at 0.8 percent, and latency decreased to 58 seconds.

artigos.titulo: A simple blood test could reveal Alzheimer’s risk 10 years before symptoms
artigos.destaque: A major international study found that a simple blood test could help predict Alzheimer’s-related cognitive decline years before symptoms appear, with the highest-risk individuals facing a 38% chance of impairment within five years and an estimated 78% chance within 10 years. Scientists believe the discovery could pave the way for earlier intervention and future treatments designed to prevent Alzheimer’s before memory problems begin.

artigos.titulo: Urological manifestations in obesity
artigos.autores: Jayapal B, Kapoor N
artigos.destaque: Obesity's urological effects are heterogeneous, paradoxical from pediatric to adults, mediated by insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, and hormonal dysregulation. Weight loss and the use of GLP-1 RA may offer a unique strategy for optimizing and treating urological conditions.

resumo.texto: The global prevalence of obesity continues to rise, with effects ranging across urology. This review summarizes recent evidence on obesity and its impact on various urological conditions, including malignancy, infections, stone disease, functional urology and male reproductive health, chronic kidney disease, and pediatric urology, to guide comprehensive management in this population.

Obesity has a paradoxical survival benefit in patients with renal cell carcinoma, while its impact drives aggressive prostate cancer. Obesity increases kidney stone risk, with sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists showing divergent effects on lithogenesis and urinary tract infections. It is a modifiable risk factor for overactive bladder and stress urinary incontinence, both of which improve with weight loss/ bariatric surgery. Robotic surgery mitigates obesity-related perioperative risk. Hypogonadism secondary to obesity is a major reversible cause of male infertility. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) reverse metabolic hypogonadism and helps in slowing chronic kidney progression. Maternal and childhood obesity may impair testicular descent and can also increase the risk of nocturnal enuresis.

Obesity's urological effects are heterogeneous, paradoxical from pediatric to adults, mediated by insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, and hormonal dysregulation. Weight loss and the use of GLP-1 RA may offer a unique strategy for optimizing and treating urological conditions.

artigos.titulo: Obesity and skeletal fragility: revisiting an old paradigm
artigos.autores: John R, Mithal A, Kapoor N
artigos.destaque: Comprehensive skeletal assessment, incorporation of lifestyle measures to preserve bone health, and appropriate osteoporosis therapy are essential. Future research should focus on obesity-specific fracture prediction tools, advanced imaging modalities, and dedicated clinical guidelines for the prevention, diagnosis, and management of osteoporosis in individuals with obesity.

resumo.texto: Obesity has traditionally been considered protective against osteoporosis because of its association with higher bone mineral density (BMD). However, emerging evidence demonstrates that individuals with obesity remain at increased risk of peripheral fractures despite preserved BMD. This review summarizes current evidence on the complex relationship between obesity and skeletal health, including underlying mechanisms, fracture patterns, assessment strategies, and management considerations.

Studies indicate that fracture risk in obesity is site-specific, with a greater propensity for peripheral fractures. Visceral adiposity, bone marrow adipose tissue, chronic low-grade inflammation, altered adipokine signaling, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and obesity-related comorbidities contribute to impaired bone quality and skeletal fragility. Conventional Dual Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA) may underestimate skeletal risk in obesity, while newer tools such as trabecular bone score (TBS) version 4.0, peripheral quantitative computerized tomography (pQCT) may improve risk assessment. Weight-loss interventions, including lifestyle modification, Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA), and bariatric surgery, provide substantial metabolic benefits but may increase fracture risk if skeletal health is not adequately addressed.

Obesity should no longer be regarded as protective for bone health. Although BMD is often normal or elevated, obesity is associated with alterations in bone quality and increased fracture susceptibility. Comprehensive skeletal assessment, incorporation of lifestyle measures to preserve bone health, and appropriate osteoporosis therapy are essential. Future research should focus on obesity-specific fracture prediction tools, advanced imaging modalities, and dedicated clinical guidelines for the prevention, diagnosis, and management of osteoporosis in individuals with obesity.

artigos.titulo: The pharmacist's role in enhancing adherence to GLP1 based anti-obesity medications through comprehensive side effect management
artigos.autores: Schwartzberg E, Azran C, Diker-Cohen T et al.
artigos.destaque: It provides side-effect incidence and management tables, possible lifestyle and treatment options in each phase, red-flag and referral criteria, strategies to prevent sarcopenia and nutrient deficiency. Implementing these pharmacist-driven interventions can significantly improve tolerability, adherence, and long-term clinical outcomes in obesity pharmacotherapy.

resumo.texto: The emergence of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP1) and GLP1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonists (hereinafter GLP1-RAs, GLP1-GIP-RAs) have transformed obesity treatment. These agents offer substantial weight loss and notable cardiometabolic and other health benefits. Yet, their success relies on long-term adherence and careful management of side effects. Common adverse events - especially gastrointestinal (GI) disturbances - often lead to treatment discontinuation, weight regain and reduced effectiveness. As healthcare providers with multiple patients' interactions, pharmacists provide continuous care throughout the entire treatment journey, from initiation through titration phase and long-term maintenance. The unique position of pharmacists' interactions with patients enables them to address the high rates of non-adherence commonly observed with GLP1 based medications, which often stem from GI side effects, medication complexity, and patient education gaps. Treatment persistence and patient outcomes can be significantly improved through structured, pharmacist-led strategies, including comprehensive patient education, lifestyle modifications, and judicious use of over-the-counter interventions and vitamin/mineral/supplement therapies. Critical emphasis is placed on the pharmacist's role in preventing and managing serious complications associated with rapid weight loss, particularly sarcopenia and nutrient deficiencies, while maintaining vigilance for "red flags" that signal serious complications requiring physician intervention. This manuscript delineates the rationale for pharmacist involvement through the phases of adherence: initiation, titration, persistence, and discontinuation. It provides side-effect incidence and management tables, possible lifestyle and treatment options in each phase, red-flag and referral criteria, strategies to prevent sarcopenia and nutrient deficiency. Implementing these pharmacist-driven interventions can significantly improve tolerability, adherence, and long-term clinical outcomes in obesity pharmacotherapy.

artigos.titulo: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
artigos.autores: Selvaganesan P, Karnib M, Helmy I et al.
artigos.destaque: Among patients with obese heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower incidence of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with alternative oral agents.

resumo.texto: To evaluate whether GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), compared with DPP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase-4) inhibitors or sulfonylureas, are associated with reduced all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalizations in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

PRAISE-HFpEF (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction) was a nationwide multicenter cohort study using a new-user, active-comparator design within the national Veterans Affairs Health System (170 US hospitals). Adults with type 2 diabetes between January 1, 2000 and December 31, 2021, were identified from centralized electronic health records. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 were selected using a validated diagnostic algorithm. Exposure was initiation of a GLP-1RA versus DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2021. The primary outcome was time to all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on the propensity score was used to balanced baseline characteristics.

Among 179 288 patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, 1024 GLP-1RA users and 796 DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea users met inclusion criteria. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.64-0.95], P=0.01). Weight loss was modestly greater with GLP-1RAs compared with DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea (-12.9% versus -10.1%).

Among patients with obese heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower incidence of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with alternative oral agents.

artigos.titulo: Rationale and Design of a Parallel Randomized Trial of a DASH-Enhanced Portfolio Diet With or Without Ultra-Processed Plant Proteins for Blood Pressure and Other Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Adults With Hypertension and Obesity: The Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention on Cardiometabolic Health Trial
artigos.autores: Houshialsadat Z, Viscardi G, Rossi AG et al.
artigos.destaque: Findings will provide high-quality evidence on the use of a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet and the role of nutrient-dense soy foods classified as UPFs within the combination of the 2 guideline-based dietary patterns to support dietary strategies for cardiometabolic risk reduction.

resumo.texto: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death and hospitalization globally. Clinical practice guidelines recommend various plant-based dietary patterns that target specific cardiometabolic risk factors, including the Dietary Approach to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet for blood pressure and the Portfolio diet for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Combining key elements of these patterns may enhance cardiovascular disease risk reduction. However, many soy-based products, a key Portfolio component, are classified as ultra-processed foods (UPFs). This trial will answer 2 questions: (1) Does a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet result in clinically meaningful reductions in blood pressure compared with standard of care and (2) Is a high-UPF noninferior to a low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet for blood pressure reduction?

The SWITCH (Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention for Cardiometabolic Health) trial is a parallel, randomized, 3-arm, open-label, superiority-noninferiority trial. Three hundred adults with hypertension and obesity, including 50% with type 2 diabetes, will be randomized to a high-UPF or low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet or standard of care for 12 weeks. The primary outcome is systolic blood pressure. Key secondary outcomes are non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and body weight. Other outcomes include cardiometabolic risk factors.

Findings will provide high-quality evidence on the use of a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet and the role of nutrient-dense soy foods classified as UPFs within the combination of the 2 guideline-based dietary patterns to support dietary strategies for cardiometabolic risk reduction.
URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/; Unique identifier: NCT06907862.

artigos.titulo: The metabolic-brain axis: GLP-1 signaling, insulin resistance, and obesity pharmacotherapy in neurodegeneration
artigos.autores: Santerre M, Shcherbik N, Sawaya BE
artigos.destaque: This review synthesizes current knowledge on brain insulin signaling, GLP-1 neurobiology, obesity-driven neuroinflammation, and the translational evidence for metabolic therapeutics in neurodegeneration, and uses the dissociation between mechanistic plausibility, epidemiological association, and null confirmatory trial results to identify critical knowledge gaps and translational barriers related to CNS target engagement, optimal dosing, and disease-modifying efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists. The review is organized into four major themes: brain insulin signaling, central GLP-1 biology, obesity-associated neuroinflammation, and the translational evidence supporting metabolic therapies for neurodegenerative disease.

resumo.texto: The intersection of metabolic disease and neurodegeneration represents one of the most consequential frontiers in translational neuroscience. Converging epidemiological, mechanistic, and pharmacological evidence supports a bidirectional metabolic-brain axis in which systemic insulin resistance, obesity, and chronic metabolic inflammation are associated with and may contribute to alterations in neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, and neuroimmune homeostasis. GLP-1 receptor agonists, originally developed for glycemic control and weight management, have therefore been investigated as potential disease-modifying therapies across Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and related neurodegenerative conditions through mechanisms including neuronal PKA activation, microglial NLRP3 suppression, mitochondrial biogenesis, and restoration of AQP4 perivascular localization that may contribute to glymphatic waste clearance. Direct human evidence for these CNS mechanisms remains limited or absent, with current support derived primarily from preclinical models and indirect human data, as detailed in Table 1, warranting dedicated investigation in the context of GLP-1 receptor agonism. Importantly, the two pivotal phase 3 programs designed to test this hypothesis in humans - EVOKE/EVOKE+ in early Alzheimer's disease and Exenatide-PD3 in Parkinson's disease - have both now reported, and neither demonstrated a statistically significant benefit on its primary clinical endpoint, despite favorable biomarker and epidemiological signals preceding these results. This review synthesizes current knowledge on brain insulin signaling, GLP-1 neurobiology, obesity-driven neuroinflammation, and the translational evidence for metabolic therapeutics in neurodegeneration, and uses the dissociation between mechanistic plausibility, epidemiological association, and null confirmatory trial results to identify critical knowledge gaps and translational barriers related to CNS target engagement, optimal dosing, and disease-modifying efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists. The review is organized into four major themes: brain insulin signaling, central GLP-1 biology, obesity-associated neuroinflammation, and the translational evidence supporting metabolic therapies for neurodegenerative disease.

artigos.titulo: Effects of Parent-Involved Digital Health Interventions on Adiposity-Related Outcomes and Behaviors in Children and Adolescents With Overweight or Obesity: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
artigos.autores: Zheng Y, Huang J, Peng Y et al.
artigos.destaque: Moderate-certainty evidence suggests that parent-involved DHIs may produce a small improvement in BMI-related outcomes among children and adolescents with overweight or obesity. However, evidence for improvements in adiposity-related behaviors remains limited, and neither the optimal digital delivery modality nor the most effective parent-involved strategy has been established. Future research should refine these interventions to identify optimal strategies and confirm their effectiveness.

resumo.texto: Parental involvement in obesity interventions is considered essential for sustainable behavior change in children and adolescents with overweight or obesity; yet, the effectiveness of parent-involved digital health interventions (DHIs) and the influence of different delivery modalities remain unclear.
This study aimed to synthesize the effects of parent-involved DHIs on adiposity-related outcomes and behaviors and explore potential moderators.

Nine databases were searched from inception to December 2025 to identify eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Primary outcomes were adiposity-related outcomes such as BMI; secondary outcomes were adiposity-related behaviors, including dietary behavior, physical activity, and sedentary behavior. Standardized mean differences (SMDs; Hedges g) on primary outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Prespecified subgroup analyses examined DHI delivery modalities and parent-involved strategies. Secondary outcomes were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2), and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation).

Twenty-nine RCTs (4156 participants) were included, of which 22 contributed to the meta-analysis. Parent-involved DHIs produced a small but statistically significant reduction in BMI-related outcomes compared with controls (SMD=-0.11, 95% CI -0.19 to -0.04; P=.004; I²=0%). When stratified by control type, the pooled effect remained significant in trials using inactive controls (SMD=-0.15, 95% CI -0.25 to -0.04; P=.006; I²=0%), but not in trials using active controls (SMD=-0.07, 95% CI -0.19 to 0.04; P=.20; I²=0%). Subgroup differences on DHI delivery modalities and parent-involved strategies were not statistically significant. For adiposity-related behaviors, significant improvements were reported in 5 of 16 trials for dietary behaviors, 2 of 17 for physical activity, and 2 of 12 for sedentary behavior. The risk of bias was generally low to some concerns, and the overall certainty of evidence for BMI-related outcomes was moderate.

Moderate-certainty evidence suggests that parent-involved DHIs may produce a small improvement in BMI-related outcomes among children and adolescents with overweight or obesity. However, evidence for improvements in adiposity-related behaviors remains limited, and neither the optimal digital delivery modality nor the most effective parent-involved strategy has been established. Future research should refine these interventions to identify optimal strategies and confirm their effectiveness.
PROSPERO CRD420251239829; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251239829.

artigos.titulo: High-intensity interval versus moderate-intensity continuous freestyle swimming in obese college students: A randomized controlled study protocol examining glycolipid and vascular endothelial responses
artigos.autores: Yang M, Wang J, Su X et al.
artigos.destaque: The findings may inform safe and more precise exercise prescriptions for young adults with obesity. The trial was prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2600121931) on April 7, 2026.

resumo.texto: Obesity among college students may be accompanied by early metabolic and endothelial abnormalities before overt cardiometabolic disease develops. Freestyle swimming combines whole-body energy expenditure with low weight-bearing load. This randomized controlled trial will compare high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) freestyle swimming and examine the relationships between changes in glycolipid markers and vascular endothelial markers.

A total of 108 obese college students will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to HIIT, MICT, or a usual-activity control group (36 participants per group). The exercise groups will complete supervised 30-min freestyle swimming sessions three times weekly for 6 months. Total cholesterol (TC) at 6 months, adjusted for baseline TC, will be the single primary outcome. Secondary glycolipid, endothelial, anthropometric, adherence, and safety outcomes will be assessed at baseline and at 2, 4, and 6 months. The primary comparison will use analysis of covariance under the intention-to-treat principle. Longitudinal mixed-effects models and multiple imputation sensitivity analyses will characterize outcome trajectories. Multivariable linear regression will examine the relationships between changes in individual glycolipid markers and changes in ET-1 and NO.

This trial will clarify whether HIIT and MICT freestyle swimming differ in their effects on TC and other glycolipid and endothelial outcomes in obese college students and whether improvements in glycolipid markers are accompanied by changes in ET-1 and NO. The findings may inform safe and more precise exercise prescriptions for young adults with obesity.
The trial was prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2600121931) on April 7, 2026.

artigos.titulo: Machine learning predicts weight change in a real-world digital health application
artigos.autores: Glasbrenner C, Lehmann M, Höchsmann C et al.
artigos.destaque: Predictive performance for weight-loss outcomes improved substantially when information from the first four weeks, particularly 4-week weight, was incorporated. Accordingly, the week 8 and week 12 models should be interpreted as predictions updated during treatment rather than predictions based solely on pretreatment characteristics. Weight-loss response and sustained intervention use were characterized by distinct predictive information and may require different forms of early, targeted support. These findings provide a basis for further research on the early identification of individuals at risk of suboptimal outcomes and the development of more personalized digital obesity care. External validation in independent, relevant cohorts is required before the models can be considered for clinical implementation.

resumo.texto: Digital health applications offer scalable support for weight loss, but individual outcomes and retention vary substantially. It remains unclear how predictive information evolves during treatment, whether app engagement adds predictive information beyond early weight response, and whether the same factors predict weight loss and retention.

Using real-world data from the 12-week digital health application Oviva Direkt for Obesity, we developed machine learning models to predict clinically meaningful weight loss, continuous relative weight change, and full app retention. Weight-change and full-retention analyses included 17,953 and 26,714 adults, respectively. Models evaluated baseline characteristics, 4-week weight, and weekly app engagement metrics separately and in combination to quantify their incremental predictive value and assess how performance changed when early-treatment information was added to pretreatment characteristics.

Baseline characteristics alone showed limited discrimination for clinically meaningful weight loss at weeks 8 and 12 (ROC AUC 0.54-0.58). Adding 4-week weight substantially improved performance (ROC AUC 0.86-0.92), whereas app engagement alone yielded modest improvements (ROC AUC 0.63-0.67). Adding app engagement to models including 4-week weight provided little further improvement (ROC AUC 0.87-0.92). A similar pattern was observed for continuous weight-change prediction. In contrast, full-retention prediction improved from ROC AUC 0.81 with baseline characteristics to 0.90 with app engagement, while 4-week weight provided no additional benefit. Weight-loss prediction was driven primarily by baseline weight, 4-week weight, and self-defined target weight, whereas engagement-related variables like goal setting and personalized logging recommendations were more influential for full retention.

Predictive performance for weight-loss outcomes improved substantially when information from the first four weeks, particularly 4-week weight, was incorporated. Accordingly, the week 8 and week 12 models should be interpreted as predictions updated during treatment rather than predictions based solely on pretreatment characteristics. Weight-loss response and sustained intervention use were characterized by distinct predictive information and may require different forms of early, targeted support. These findings provide a basis for further research on the early identification of individuals at risk of suboptimal outcomes and the development of more personalized digital obesity care. External validation in independent, relevant cohorts is required before the models can be considered for clinical implementation.

artigos.titulo: Bazi Bushen Attenuates Skeletal Muscle Decline Associated With Oestrogen Deficiency and Modulates FGFR1/ERK Signalling
artigos.autores: Huang D, Xu N, Chu Q et al.
artigos.destaque: Taken together, these findings suggest that FGFR1/ERK signalling may contribute to the protective effects of BZBS. Our findings provide evidence for the beneficial effects of BZBS on skeletal muscle deterioration associated with oestrogen deficiency.

resumo.texto: Postmenopausal oestrogen deficiency is associated with skeletal muscle loss and functional decline, thereby increasing the risk of sarcopenia in women. Considering the safety risks linked to hormone replacement therapy (HRT), alternative strategies are needed to attenuate skeletal muscle decline after menopause. A total of 24 female C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 6 per group): Sham-operated (SHAM), ovariectomized (OVX), OVX treated with estradiol valerate (OVX + E2) and OVX treated with Bazi Bushen (OVX + BZBS). Skeletal muscle mass and function were evaluated in four groups. RNA sequencing was applied to explore the molecular mechanisms and key signalling pathways underlying BZBS-induced muscle protection. We further examined the role of the FGFR1/ERK signalling pathway in mediating the effects of BZBS on myogenic differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts. The results showed that OVX mice had reduced grip strength and skeletal muscle mass, increased fat accumulation, reduced lean mass and impaired metabolic activity. These phenotypic alterations were accompanied by myofiber atrophy, increased collagen staining, endocrine perturbations and elevated expression of p16, p21, Atrogin-1 and MuRF1. BZBS ameliorated these abnormalities. RNA-seq suggested that FGF/MAPK signalling may be involved. In D-gal-treated C2C12 myoblasts, BZBS reduced Atrogin-1 and MuRF1 expression while restoring MYHC and MYOG expression. Mechanistically, BZBS suppressed FGFR1/ERK signalling activation and bFGF partially reversed the protective effects of BZBS. Taken together, these findings suggest that FGFR1/ERK signalling may contribute to the protective effects of BZBS. Our findings provide evidence for the beneficial effects of BZBS on skeletal muscle deterioration associated with oestrogen deficiency.

artigos.titulo: Associations of Coexisting Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sarcopenia-Related Abnormalities With Adverse Clinical Outcomes Across Obesity States
artigos.autores: Fan H, Mao X, Yan T et al.
artigos.destaque: Similar findings were observed in external validation analyses using the 2011-2018 US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort. Together, these observations inform risk stratification strategy and management of MASLD to include sarcopenia assessment.

resumo.texto: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with adverse liver and non-liver outcomes, but the impact of coexisting sarcopenia-related abnormalities (e.g., low muscle strength [MS], muscle mass, and physical performance) remains unclear. In a prospective UK Biobank cohort (n = 438,748), we evaluated their joint associations with incidence and risks of all-cause mortality, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), non-liver cancers, and obesity-related cancers across MASLD and sarcopenia-related abnormality status. Over a median follow-up of 13.8 years, 401 HCC, 1714 cirrhosis, 39,534 CVD, 19,637 CKD, 38,240 non-liver cancers, 12,536 obesity-related cancers, and 34,801 deaths occurred. A stepwise increase in both incidence and adjusted risk of liver and non-liver outcomes was observed across MASLD and sarcopenia strata. Within the coexistence group, the obesity (vs. non-obesity) subgroup generally had higher risks. For example, for cirrhosis, adjusted hazard ratios increased from 3.93 to 7.36 then 8.48 with MASLD alone, coexisting MASLD with low MS overall and coexisting MASLD, low MS and obesity, respectively. Similar findings were observed in external validation analyses using the 2011-2018 US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort. Together, these observations inform risk stratification strategy and management of MASLD to include sarcopenia assessment.

artigos.titulo: Impact of body composition on toxicity and response in patients with advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma treated with BV-AVD
artigos.autores: Stanchina MD, Kuker RA, Han S et al.
artigos.destaque: Stage IV disease and higher MTV were both associated with increased PN and may reflect the wider distribution of BV and an amplified inflammatory response. These findings demonstrate that body composition and PET-CT indices are relevant biomarkers in ASHL, and their integration with MTV may enhance risk stratification and deepen our understanding of toxicity risk.

resumo.texto: BV-AVD (brentuximab vedotin, doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine) has improved outcomes in advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma (ASHL); however, toxicity such as peripheral neuropathy (PN) remains a concern. Previous studies in oncology have demonstrated an association between sarcopenia and chemotoxicity. Therefore, we examined the effects of body composition parameters, including skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous fat (SF), and visceral fat (VF), along with quantitative biomarkers including metabolic tumor volume (MTV), on PN, treatment response, and progression-free survival. This study retrospectively reviewed the baseline, interim, and end-of-treatment (EOT) positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) for 39 patients with ASHL treated with BV-AVD and assessed changes in MTV and body composition. MTV declined significantly from baseline to interim PET and EOT PET-CT (EOT PET), with no significant difference between the latter time points, indicating an early treatment response. SM:VF and SF:VF ratios followed a similar pattern, suggesting that changes in body composition including SM loss (sarcopenia) and changes in fat distribution (SF:VF), occurred early during treatment. Patients with stable SM:VF ratios were more likely to achieve a complete response (CR), whereas larger changes in SM:VF and SF:VF ratios and an early increase in VF were associated with failure to achieve CR, possibly due to increased inflammation. Stage IV disease and higher MTV were both associated with increased PN and may reflect the wider distribution of BV and an amplified inflammatory response. These findings demonstrate that body composition and PET-CT indices are relevant biomarkers in ASHL, and their integration with MTV may enhance risk stratification and deepen our understanding of toxicity risk.

artigos.titulo: Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial
artigos.autores: Yokote K, Yamauchi T, Shingaki T et al.
artigos.destaque: In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists.

resumo.texto: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults.

ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed).

Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group).

In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists.
Eli Lilly and Company.
For the Japanese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

artigos.titulo: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Analog-Type Amyloidosis: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
artigos.autores: Loggie J, McKay RC, Nasr SH et al.
artigos.destaque: Only 3 cases of AGLP1-type amyloidosis have been previously reported. It is vital for clinicians and pathologists to be aware of AGLP1-type amyloidosis given the increasing worldwide use of GLP-1 agonists, as well as the potential for misdiagnosis of systemic amyloidosis, which has profound therapeutic and prognostic implications.

resumo.texto: Amyloidosis is a heterogeneous group of diseases characterized by extracellular deposition of insoluble proteins. Glucagon-like peptide-1 analog (AGLP1)-type amyloidosis is a rare iatrogenic form of amyloidosis localized to areas of glucagon-like peptide-1 analog injections. In this study, we describe a case of AGLP1-type amyloidosis presenting as a subcutaneous mass on the abdomen of a 71-year-old woman with a history of liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide use. Biopsy, including Congo red stain, was consistent with an amyloid deposit. Amyloid protein identification by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry showed a typical amyloid profile with low spectra for liraglutide. Immunohistochemistry, subsequently performed, showed that the amyloid deposits were positive for glucagon; there is an extensive peptide homology between liraglutide and glucagon. Only 3 cases of AGLP1-type amyloidosis have been previously reported. It is vital for clinicians and pathologists to be aware of AGLP1-type amyloidosis given the increasing worldwide use of GLP-1 agonists, as well as the potential for misdiagnosis of systemic amyloidosis, which has profound therapeutic and prognostic implications.

artigos.titulo: Combined time-restricted feeding and resistance training enhance tirzepatide-induced improvements in adiposity and whole-body insulin sensitivity in female mice
artigos.autores: Macêdo APA, da Conceição de Mattis LR, de Lima RD et al.
artigos.destaque: All interventions similarly reduced hepatic lipid accumulation and lipogenic gene expression. Tirzepatide-based therapies enhanced systemic metabolic health without additional hepatic benefits from combined interventions.

resumo.texto: Tirzepatide is a dual agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors with potent effects on body weight regulation, glucose homeostasis and metabolic health. However, its interaction with dietary and exercise interventions as well as its impact on obesity and hepatic metabolic pathways, particularly in females, remain unclear. Here, we tested whether tirzepatide, alone or combined with time-restricted feeding (TRF) or resistance training, modulates energy balance, strength performance, adipose tissue remodelling, insulin sensitivity and hepatic lipid accumulation in female mice. Female Swiss mice after 10 weeks of obesity induction were treated with tirzepatide, TRF or resistance training for 8 weeks. Tirzepatide was administered subcutaneously using a dose-escalation protocol. TRF consisted of a 12 h feeding window, and resistance training was performed as stair climbing on alternating days. Body weight, caloric intake and feed efficiency were monitored longitudinally. Glucose homeostasis was assessed by intraperitoneal glucose and insulin tolerance tests. Adipose depots, skeletal muscle and liver mass were quantified, and hepatic lipid accumulation was evaluated by histology and RT-qPCR of lipogenic metabolism genes. Tirzepatide reduced body weight gain and feed efficiency, consistent with a negative energy balance. When combined with TRF and resistance training, tirzepatide accelerated weight loss, and the addition of resistance training further enhanced this effect, bringing body weight close to control levels. These effects were associated with reduced adipose mass and adipocyte hypertrophy, indicating improved adipose tissue remodelling. Resistance training improved strength performance and increased skeletal muscle mass. Tirzepatide combined with TRF, with or without resistance training, improved glucose tolerance in female mice. All interventions reduced hepatic lipid accumulation. Collectively, tirzepatide, particularly in combination with TRF and resistance training, exerts enhanced metabolic benefits on obesity, insulin sensitivity and metabolic regulation in female mice. KEY POINTS: Tirzepatide combined with time-restricted feeding and resistance training produced greater reductions in body weight and adiposity in obese female mice. Combined interventions improved whole-body insulin sensitivity more effectively than isolated strategies. Resistance training preserved skeletal muscle mass during tirzepatide-induced weight loss. All interventions similarly reduced hepatic lipid accumulation and lipogenic gene expression. Tirzepatide-based therapies enhanced systemic metabolic health without additional hepatic benefits from combined interventions.

artigos.titulo: Neuropsychiatric Safety of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus or Obesity
artigos.autores: Jani HT, Levine H, Patel A et al.
artigos.destaque: Evidence does not support a clinically meaningful increase in neuropsychiatric harm with GLP-1 RAs or tirzepatide in the populations studied. Surveillance remains warranted for patients with substantial psychiatric morbidity, for obesity-only populations, and for long-term rare outcomes.

resumo.texto: Neuropsychiatric safety concerns about glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and tirzepatide prompted regulatory review by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA). We synthesized the contemporary evidence in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus or obesity, emphasizing study design, risk of bias, and the distinction between signal detection and causal inference.

The PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus databases were searched without a lower date limit through March 15, 2026 (English, adults ≥18 years). The review was reported with reference to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, and the PRISMA-S and PRISMA-Harms extensions. Evidence was grouped into prespecified categories: randomized syntheses, comparative observational studies and target-trial emulations, outlier non-active-comparator studies, pharmacovigilance analyses, and regulatory reviews. Risk of bias was appraised with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and with Risk of Bias in Non-randomised Studies of Interventions; certainty was summarized using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.

Twenty studies and two regulatory reviews met the inclusion criteria. Randomized evidence, including two large 2025 meta-analyses and post hoc pooled analyses of semaglutide and tirzepatide, showed no increased risk of suicidality, depression, or anxiety, though psychiatric exclusion criteria limited generalizability. Active-comparator cohorts from the United States, Scandinavia, and the United Kingdom likewise showed no clear increase after confounding control. Passive-comparator and disproportionality analyses generated signals but could not separate drug effects from baseline psychiatric risk, obesity-related distress, or reporting bias. The EMA and FDA conclusions do not support a causal class-wide association between GLP-1 RAs and suicidal ideation or behavior.

Evidence does not support a clinically meaningful increase in neuropsychiatric harm with GLP-1 RAs or tirzepatide in the populations studied. Surveillance remains warranted for patients with substantial psychiatric morbidity, for obesity-only populations, and for long-term rare outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Scientists discover why chronic back pain feels so personal
artigos.destaque: A surprising discovery at UC San Diego suggests that chronic lower back pain may become deeply embedded in the brain's sense of personal identity. Researchers found that movement-triggered pain activates a brain network associated with self-awareness and memories, even though ordinary acute pain typically shuts this network down. This unexpected difference could explain why conventional pain medications often provide limited relief and why fear, anticipation, and past experiences can intensify chronic pain.

artigos.titulo: Less than 42 minutes of bright daylight linked to higher dementia risk
artigos.destaque: Getting more daylight could be linked to a surprisingly powerful benefit for brain health. In a study of more than 87,000 adults, researchers found that higher daytime light exposure was associated with a 16% lower risk of dementia, with longer exposure to bright light linked to even greater reductions. Remarkably, getting less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily was a stronger predictor of dementia than six established risk factors.

artigos.titulo: Early Treatment Trajectory and Long-Term Persistence to Semaglutide for Obesity: A Population-Based Cohort Study
artigos.autores: Winter E, Wolff Sagy Y, Reges O et al.
artigos.destaque: Semaglutide discontinuation was common and associated with sociodemographic and early treatment characteristics. Day-90 dose and early weight-loss response may help identify discontinuation risk. Socioeconomic differences suggest inequalities in sustained obesity pharmacotherapy access.

resumo.texto: To assess semaglutide persistence in obesity management, identify factors associated with discontinuation and examine early tirzepatide adoption.

This retrospective cohort study used Clalit Health Services records of adults without diabetes initiating Wegovy between January and May 2025. Discontinuation was defined as a gap exceeding 60 days after medication coverage ended. Multivariable Cox models, including a Day-90 landmark analysis, assessed discontinuation. Tirzepatide adoption was evaluated following its December 2025 coverage introduction.

Among 34 309 participants (67.0% women; mean age 44.6 years), cumulative discontinuation reached 36.5% at 180 days and 67.6% at 365 days. Arab population sector (hazard ratio [HR] 1.65, 95% CI 1.59-1.72), low socioeconomic status (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.09-1.17) and current smoking (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.09-1.17) were associated with discontinuation. In the day-90 landmark cohort (n = 28 218), remaining on 0.25 versus 1.0 mg was associated with subsequent discontinuation (HR 1.88, 95% CI 1.72-2.06), substantially attenuated after adjustment for early refill adherence. Each percentage-point smaller BMI reduction was associated with 3% higher discontinuation hazard (HR 1.03, 95% CI 1.03-1.04). Following tirzepatide availability, 2908 of 33 936 eligible participants (8.6%) initiated treatment over a median 3.1-month observation period. Adoption was associated with higher socioeconomic status and baseline BMI.

Semaglutide discontinuation was common and associated with sociodemographic and early treatment characteristics. Day-90 dose and early weight-loss response may help identify discontinuation risk. Socioeconomic differences suggest inequalities in sustained obesity pharmacotherapy access.

artigos.titulo: Improving Materials for a Technology-Based Childhood Obesity Intervention for Hispanic/Latino Families in Rural Nebraska: Mixed Methods Usability Test
artigos.autores: Alves TF, Santos N, Rossi Squarcini CF et al.
artigos.destaque: The UT results, combined with systematic documentation using FRAME, allowed us to identify and prioritize the adaptations needed to improve the intervention materials. These refinements will prepare the HFC intervention for implementation in a subsequent feasibility study.

resumo.texto: Childhood obesity remains a public health concern in the United States, disproportionately affecting Hispanic/Latino and rural populations. Despite this disparity, there is a lack of culturally relevant programs specifically designed to reach this population. To address this gap, our team culturally adapted a technology-based childhood obesity intervention, Hispanic Family Connections (HFC), targeting Hispanic/Latino families living in rural areas. The intervention comprises 2 main components: interactive voice response (IVR) calls and a workbook with at-home activities to promote family engagement.

The objectives were to (1) evaluate the usability of the IVR calls and workbook included in the HFC intervention and (2) document and plan adaptations to these components using the FRAME (Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications-Enhanced).

We conducted 5 mixed methods, task-based usability tests (UTs) using the think-aloud procedure. All 5 participants were women, self-identified as Hispanic/Latino, and were Spanish literate. Each participant completed 3 think-aloud tasks designed to evaluate the usability of the IVR calls and workbook chapters. Usability was assessed using the After-Scenario Questionnaire (ASQ) at the end of each task and the System Usability Scale (SUS) at the end of the UT session. All sessions were recorded, and data were organized into two primary categories: (1) quantitative results (ASQ and SUS) and (2) qualitative data (participants' comments and researchers' observations). Findings were compiled and analyzed following the 8 main domains of FRAME.

For the workbook, ASQ scores showed a high level of ease in task completion (mean 1.1, SD 0.32), satisfaction with completion time (mean 1.0, SD 0.00), and satisfaction with support information (mean 1.5, SD 0.97). For the IVR calls, participants reported a higher level of ease in task completion (mean 1.0, SD 0.00), satisfaction with completion time (mean 1.0, SD 0.00), and satisfaction with support information (mean 1.2, SD 0.45). SUS results were positive for 80% (4/5) of participants, with an average usability score above the benchmark (mean 75.5, SD 15.04). Using FRAME, we identified and documented 30 suggestions for adaptations and improvements to the workbook and IVR calls. The majority of suggestions were content-related (n=26, 86.67%), with most focusing on tailoring/tweaking, or refining existing materials.

The UT results, combined with systematic documentation using FRAME, allowed us to identify and prioritize the adaptations needed to improve the intervention materials. These refinements will prepare the HFC intervention for implementation in a subsequent feasibility study.

artigos.titulo: Changes in obstructive sleep apnea severity, upper-airway findings, and health-related quality of life after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a prospective before-and-after study
artigos.autores: Bonilla LFS, Díaz JDR, Peñaranda D et al.
artigos.destaque: Among participants with complete follow-up, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass was followed by lower OSA severity and favorable secondary outcomes, but complete remission was uncommon. Continued postoperative sleep reassessment remains important.

resumo.texto: To evaluate changes in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, upper-airway findings, daytime sleepiness, and health-related quality of life approximately 6 months after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass in adults with obesity.

We conducted a prospective single-group before-and-after study at Hospital de San José, Bogotá, Colombia. Adults with OSA undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass as routine care had pre- and postoperative polysomnography, anthropometric and otolaryngologic assessment, nasofibrolaryngoscopy, and patient-reported measures. Study eligibility required preoperative AHI > 5 events/h. Paired outcomes were analyzed with paired t, Wilcoxon signed-rank, or exact McNemar tests as appropriate.

Of 33 patients assessed, 30 underwent surgery and 18 completed both objective evaluations. Mean weight decreased from 104.4 ± 12.6 to 68.5 ± 8.9 kg, BMI from 38.77 ± 4.94 to 25.82 ± 4.28 kg/m², and AHI from 23.70 ± 8.67 to 8.74 ± 4.35 events/h; mean AHI change was - 14.96 events/h (95% CI - 18.69 to - 11.22; p < 0.001). Residual OSA (AHI ≥ 5 events/h) persisted in 15/18 participants (83.3%; exact 95% CI 58.6-96.4%). Several upper-airway, sleepiness, and quality-of-life measures also changed favorably.

Among participants with complete follow-up, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass was followed by lower OSA severity and favorable secondary outcomes, but complete remission was uncommon. Continued postoperative sleep reassessment remains important.
Not applicable. This is an observational beforeandafter cohort study no health intervention was prospectively assigned for research purposes.

artigos.titulo: OBESI-NET: an Italian network proposal for AI-supported obesity monitoring and precision medicine
artigos.autores: Gambino O, Savesvki V, Manco M et al.
artigos.destaque: It also emphasizes longitudinal real-world data collection, multimodal data integration, and privacy-preserving approaches, such as federated learning. If implemented and validated, OBESI-NET could provide a framework for epidemiological monitoring, clinical research, treatment stratification, and public health planning in obesity care.Level of Evidence: Level V, expert opinion and conceptual project proposal.

resumo.texto: Obesity requires structured and coordinated surveillance, because clinical, anthropometric, behavioural, technological, and epidemiological information is often collected in fragmented systems. In Italy, data on obesity and its comorbidities are distributed across registries, observational studies, and local institutional initiatives. This fragmentation limits longitudinal monitoring, national comparability, and the development of data-driven tools for prevention, diagnosis, and clinical management. This paper presents the conceptual proposal of OBESI-NET (Osservatorio Basato su Ecosistema Sanitario Digitale di Intelligenza Artificiale per l'Obesità-NETwork Nazionale). OBESI-NET is proposed as a national software ecosystem intended to connect Italian Society of Obesity clinical centers, healthcare professionals, and artificial intelligence engineering groups. The proposed infrastructure would support the standardized collection, secure integration, and analysis of heterogeneous data. These data include clinical, behavioural, anthropometric, imaging, wearable sensor, and, in future developments, multi-omics data. The expected contribution of OBESI-NET is not the presentation of an already implemented system, but the definition of a national model for obesity-centerd digital surveillance and AI (Artificial Intelligence)-supported precision medicine. Compared with existing digital obesity projects and registries, the proposal emphasizes integration within routine clinical practice and coordination through SIO (Società italiana dell'Obesità) centers. It also emphasizes longitudinal real-world data collection, multimodal data integration, and privacy-preserving approaches, such as federated learning. If implemented and validated, OBESI-NET could provide a framework for epidemiological monitoring, clinical research, treatment stratification, and public health planning in obesity care.Level of Evidence: Level V, expert opinion and conceptual project proposal.

artigos.titulo: Comparative Effects of Pharmacological Treatment on Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
artigos.autores: Zhang J, Wang Y, Li J et al.
artigos.destaque: No significant differences among the individual SGLT-2I, GLP-1RA, nsMRA, and sGC drugs were found in risks of CV death, all-cause mortality or SAEs in patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Further evidence is needed to support these comparative effects and update guidance on medication choice for HFmrEF/HFpEF.

resumo.texto: The comparative efficacy and safety of the new drugs (including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors [SGLT-2Is], glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists [GLP-1RAs], non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists [nsMRAs], and soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators [sGCs]) for heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved (HFmrEF/HFpEF) ejection fraction remains largely unclear. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis to evaluate their comparative effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF, aiming to provide evidence-based guidance for treatment selection.

MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were comprehensively searched. We included randomized controlled trials that compared nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA with placebo for patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Primary efficacy outcomes were cardiovascular (CV) death, hospitalization for heart failure (HF hospitalization), and all-cause mortality, while primary safety outcomes were adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs). The main analysis was conducted to compare the effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF between individual drugs. A frequentist network meta-analysis with random-effects models was used to calculate risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes.

A total of 20 randomized controlled trials (RCTs, including 10 drugs from 35 publications) were included for analyses, but none provided head-to-head direct comparisons. No significant differences among all the individual drugs were found in risks of CV death or all-cause mortality. Compared with exenatide, low or moderate certainty evidence showed that dapagliflozin (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.36-0.91), empagliflozin (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.34-0.86), and semaglutide (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.20-0.91) were related to decreased risk of HF hospitalization. No significant differences in the risk of SAEs were found among the individual drugs. Compared with empagliflozin, very low certainty evidence showed that tirzepatide (RR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32) was related to increased risk of AEs. When comparing the four drug classes (nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA), no significant differences in efficacy outcomes were found, while SGLT-2I (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78-0.96) was associated with a decreased risk of AEs compared with GLP-1RA.

No significant differences among the individual SGLT-2I, GLP-1RA, nsMRA, and sGC drugs were found in risks of CV death, all-cause mortality or SAEs in patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Further evidence is needed to support these comparative effects and update guidance on medication choice for HFmrEF/HFpEF.
PROSPERO identifier number CRD420251143542.

artigos.titulo: Comparative adverse-event reporting patterns of semaglutide and tirzepatide: a disproportionality analysis of FAERS
artigos.autores: Arslan T
artigos.destaque: Semaglutide and tirzepatide exhibited distinct post-marketing reporting patterns. The erectile-dysfunction finding was exploratory and hypothesis-generating. All findings reflect spontaneous reporting rather than comparative clinical risk or causality and require confirmation in population-based studies.

resumo.texto: Semaglutide and tirzepatide are widely used for type 2 diabetes and obesity, but comparative post-marketing safety data remain limited.

To compare adverse-event reporting patterns for semaglutide and tirzepatide in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), focusing on gastrointestinal, renal and ocular events, alopecia, serious outcomes, mortality, and reporting chronology.

This retrospective pharmacovigilance study analyzed FAERS reports submitted from January 2022 through June 2026. After deduplication, 215,337 unique reports remained; predefined exposure criteria identified 60,423 semaglutide-only reports, 143,126 tirzepatide-only reports, and 853 reports listing both drugs without additional suspect active ingredients. Disproportionality was assessed using reporting odds ratios (RORs) with 95% confidence intervals. Multivariable logistic regression, false discovery rate adjustment, and reporting-latency analyses were also performed.

Semaglutide showed higher reporting odds than tirzepatide for impaired gastric emptying (ROR 6.39), intestinal obstruction/ileus (ROR 4.56), acute kidney injury (ROR 2.51), pancreatitis (ROR 2.18), vomiting (ROR 2.11), and optic ischaemic neuropathy (ROR 15.77). Alopecia was relatively more frequently reported with tirzepatide (ROR 0.74). Semaglutide reports had higher adjusted reporting odds of hospitalization (aOR 2.80) and death (aOR 1.21). In an exploratory analysis restricted to male reports, erectile dysfunction was reported in 92 of 16,673 semaglutide reports and 46 of 27,321 tirzepatide reports (ROR 3.29, 95% CI 2.31-4.69; q < 0.001).

Semaglutide and tirzepatide exhibited distinct post-marketing reporting patterns. The erectile-dysfunction finding was exploratory and hypothesis-generating. All findings reflect spontaneous reporting rather than comparative clinical risk or causality and require confirmation in population-based studies.

artigos.titulo: Switching between semaglutide and tirzepatide in obesity management: an expert-consensus framework for approximate clinical efficacy-matched switching doses
artigos.autores: Schwartzberg E, Berman E, Shani S et al.
artigos.destaque: Estimation of clinical efficacy-matched switching doses is more practical than mandatory lowest-dose initiation, which naturally risks a 'therapeutic gap' and subsequent weight regain. Until prospective switching trials validate exact conversions, clinicians should utilize the proposed equivalence bands and the five-step clinical decision algorithm to guide seamless transitions, titrating doses every 4-8 weeks based on individual tolerability and metabolic outcomes.

resumo.texto: Currently, there are no available guidelines for switching from semaglutide to tirzepatide, since the mechanisms of action and pharmacokinetics differ, thus posing a challenge for continuous treatment of obesity.

A narrative review of PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov (to May 2026) evaluated trials and cohorts comparing semaglutide (0.25-7.2 mg) and tirzepatide (2.5-15 mg). We synthesized indirect treatment comparisons to outline dose-response relationships and develop approximate efficacy‑matched switching dose bands.

Estimation of clinical efficacy-matched switching doses is more practical than mandatory lowest-dose initiation, which naturally risks a 'therapeutic gap' and subsequent weight regain. Until prospective switching trials validate exact conversions, clinicians should utilize the proposed equivalence bands and the five-step clinical decision algorithm to guide seamless transitions, titrating doses every 4-8 weeks based on individual tolerability and metabolic outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Lower and earlier diurnal cortisol signatures of psychological trauma versus comparable physiological stress: one day post-exposure
artigos.autores: Huang J, Liu Y, Wang Y et al.
artigos.destaque: Stillbirth was also exhibited associated with an earlier acrophase. Compared with comparable physiological delivery stress, stillbirth is linked to reduced total cortisol secretion, lower mean levels, and an advanced circadian phase in the acute postpartum period, suggesting that the psychological trauma of stillbirth may involve alterations in hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis regulatory patterns and providing preliminary evidence for future work on early biological markers and supportive interventions.

resumo.texto: Traumatic events engage stress physiology, with the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and cortisol central to adaptation. In naturalistic trauma, physical injury and psychological distress often co-occur, complicating interpretation of acute cortisol changes. Stillbirth offers a natural contrast: it is physiologically similar to live birth but constitutes traumatic bereavement. This study tested whether psychological trauma elicited by stillbirth is associated with acute alterations in diurnal cortisol rhythm versus comparable physiological delivery stress. Fifty-seven postpartum women were included (stillbirth, 24; live birth, 33). Saliva samples were collected at seven fixed time points across the day following childbirth. Cosinor curve fitting yielded the midline estimating statistic of rhythm, amplitude, and acrophase. Traditional indices included area under the curve with respect to ground, area under the curve with respect to increase, and the cortisol awakening response. Group differences were tested using analyzes of variance. Both groups showed a coherent diurnal pattern. Compared with live birth, stillbirth was associated with a lower area under the curve with respect to ground, a lower area under the curve with respect to increase, and a lower midline estimating statistic of rhythm. Stillbirth was also exhibited associated with an earlier acrophase. Compared with comparable physiological delivery stress, stillbirth is linked to reduced total cortisol secretion, lower mean levels, and an advanced circadian phase in the acute postpartum period, suggesting that the psychological trauma of stillbirth may involve alterations in hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis regulatory patterns and providing preliminary evidence for future work on early biological markers and supportive interventions.

artigos.titulo: Academic Stress and Depressive Symptoms in High School Students: A Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model and Cross-Lagged Panel Network Analysis
artigos.autores: Ji T, Xu T, Zhang X et al.
artigos.destaque: Early drivers included 'I thought my life had been a failure' and 'I felt that people dislike me', whereas over time 'I was unhappy' and 'I felt hopeless about the future' gained predictive importance. The study revealed temporal relationships between academic stress and depressive symptoms and identified potential targets, providing evidence and implications for prevention and intervention.

resumo.texto: Despite evidence linking academic stress and depressive symptoms, cross-sectional designs cannot reveal their developmental dynamics, and total-scale scores obscure symptom-level complexity and intervention targets. We applied the random intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) and cross-lagged panel network (CLPN) analysis to 307 Chinese adolescents (58.63% female) to examine the relationship between academic stress and depressive symptoms from the aggregate to the symptom level and to identify key nodes. Results from the RI-CLPM indicated a positive association between academic stress and depressive symptoms at the between-person level. At the within-person level, Time-1 academic stress predicted a reduction in Time-2 depressive symptoms. CLPN results revealed complex reciprocal influences: 'People were unfriendly' and 'I felt hopeless about the future' were initially vulnerable and later progressed to 'I felt sad' and 'I thought my life had been a failure'. Early drivers included 'I thought my life had been a failure' and 'I felt that people dislike me', whereas over time 'I was unhappy' and 'I felt hopeless about the future' gained predictive importance. The study revealed temporal relationships between academic stress and depressive symptoms and identified potential targets, providing evidence and implications for prevention and intervention.

artigos.titulo: Ethical Reflections on Co‑Authoring With People With Lived Experience Across Health, Education and Community Settings
artigos.autores: Moss H, Fitzpatrick K, O'Shea P et al.
artigos.destaque: Co-authoring with participants with lived experience is not only feasible but vital. PLA reversals support meaningful, ethical and impactful collaboration.

resumo.texto: Co‑authoring with people who have lived experience is increasingly recognised as essential to meaningful patient and public involvement (PPI) (Involve 2012). Yet genuine power‑sharing in academic writing remains rare, particularly in music and health research. Traditional research models position participants as 'informants', while academic authors retain interpretive authority. Participatory Learning and Action (PLA) offers principles and methods to shift research from extractive, top-down models towards collaborative knowledge creation.

This viewpoint argues that co‑authoring with lived‑experience contributors is not merely a methodological choice but an ethical stance requiring time, humility and structural disruption. Drawing on the experience of co‑editing a book with 11 lived‑experience authors, this article briefly examines the ethical, relational and practical challenges of co‑authorship through the lens of PLA reversals.
Nine themes are presented and discussed based on the authors reflections of co-authoring a book with participants with lived experience.
Co-authoring with participants with lived experience is not only feasible but vital. PLA reversals support meaningful, ethical and impactful collaboration.
