artigos.titulo: Accuracy, Quality and Readability of Knee Osteoarthritis Information on Social Media (Instagram e TikTok) and Search Platforms (Google e YouTube): A Cross-Sectional Study
artigos.autores: Castro RQ, Ferreira de Oliveira G, Marques MN et al.
artigos.destaque: As digital platforms have become a widely used source of health information, our findings raise concerns about the potential for misinformation to delay effective treatment and perpetuate low-value care.

resumo.texto: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a chronic condition with a high global prevalence, often resulting in functional decline. Faced with this, many people turn to the internet to find information about the disease and available treatments. Besides the amount of content available online, it does not ensure its accuracy, quality and readability. This study aims to evaluate the accuracy, quality and readability of KOA-related information available on Instagram, TikTok, Google and YouTube in Brazilian Portuguese.

Google and YouTube searches were performed using 'Tratamento de osteoartrite de joelho', 'Tratamento de artrose no joelho' and 'Tratamento de artrite no joelho'. For each term, the first 20 results were selected. Searches on Instagram and TikTok were conducted using the hashtags: #artrosenojoelho, #artrosedojoelho, and #artrosedejoelho, selecting the first 100 posts for each term. All the research was done on June 19, 2024. Content accuracy was assessed against a reference resource on knee osteoarthritis, information quality was assessed using DISCERN, and the readability of Google content was evaluated using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level scale.

We found that the information about medical management was the most classified as inaccurate. The overall DISCERN score indicated low quality (2.3 ± 0.7) and 78% of Google texts required at least 14 years of schooling to read.

As digital platforms have become a widely used source of health information, our findings raise concerns about the potential for misinformation to delay effective treatment and perpetuate low-value care.

artigos.titulo: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Medicaid: Insights From Policy and Prescription Data
artigos.autores: Fung RYL, Tonti L, Pesko MF
artigos.destaque: GLP-1 prescriptions were more common in managed care than fee-for-service plans. GLP-1 prescribing varies substantially across state Medicaid coverage environments, underscoring the importance of monitoring how utilization evolves as state coverage policies change.

resumo.texto: State Medicaid programs vary in whether they cover glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1s) for obesity treatment, creating an opportunity to examine how utilization differs across coverage environments. We combined 2024 KFF Medicaid coverage data with Medicaid State Drug Utilization Data from 2015 to 2024 across all 50 states and Washington, D.C. As of August 2024, 13 states covered GLP-1s for obesity, and prescriptions were concentrated in those states, reaching 16.2 per 1,000 Medicaid beneficiaries in Q4 2024. Prescription rates for obesity-indicated GLP-1s were higher in states with coverage and showed no consistent patterns across states with different utilization management requirements. GLP-1 prescriptions were more common in managed care than fee-for-service plans. GLP-1 prescribing varies substantially across state Medicaid coverage environments, underscoring the importance of monitoring how utilization evolves as state coverage policies change.

artigos.titulo: Beyond treatment: Reinvigorating prevention in Canadian obesity and chronic disease policy
artigos.autores: Kirk SFL, Anderson LN, Conklin AI et al.
artigos.destaque: We outline five priorities for renewed action in Canada: improving food environments, promoting healthy built environments, addressing income and social inequities, creating healthier digital environments, and strengthening early-life environments. Reinvigorating prevention alongside equitable access to evidence-based treatment is necessary to achieve a comprehensive, equitable, and sustainable approach to obesity and chronic disease prevention.

resumo.texto: Over the past 15 years, obesity discourse in Canada has undergone substantial transformation. Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic disease; weight bias and stigma are increasingly considered; and effective pharmacological and surgical therapies have expanded treatment options for people living with obesity. These developments represent important advances in obesity care and challenge longstanding narratives that frame obesity as a matter of personal responsibility. Despite this progress, gaps remain in the implementation of evidence-informed prevention policies in Canada. As attention to obesity treatment continues to expand, a renewed focus is needed to ensure that prevention remains an integral component of obesity and chronic disease policy. Population health policies address the upstream social, economic, and environmental conditions that shape obesity risk and can complement clinical approaches to care. This commentary urges us to ensure that population-level prevention policies in Canada are reinvigorated alongside advances in treatment. We outline five priorities for renewed action in Canada: improving food environments, promoting healthy built environments, addressing income and social inequities, creating healthier digital environments, and strengthening early-life environments. Reinvigorating prevention alongside equitable access to evidence-based treatment is necessary to achieve a comprehensive, equitable, and sustainable approach to obesity and chronic disease prevention.

artigos.titulo: Ginsenoside Rg2 attenuates TGF-β1/Smad-mediated fibrotic remodeling in aged male mice with sarcopenia
artigos.autores: Liu Y, Zou Y, Chen H et al.
artigos.destaque: Our findings suggest that ginsenoside Rg2 alleviates TGF-β1/Smad-mediated fibrotic remodeling and improves the aging-related inflammatory-fibrotic microenvironment during skeletal muscle aging.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is an age-related degenerative disease often accompanied by chronic low-grade inflammation and fibrotic remodeling, yet its specific underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the potential mechanism by which ginsenoside Rg2 ameliorates aging-related sarcopenia, with particular attention to TGF-β1/Smad-mediated fibrosis.

Using single-cell sequencing, transcriptomic analysis, and Mendelian randomization (MR), we identified a causal relationship between transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-mediated fibrosis and the progression of sarcopenia. We employed siRNA-mediated gene knockdown, real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), grip strength testing, western blotting, histological staining, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) assays to evaluate the effects and potential mechanisms of Rg2 in aged male mice and C2C12 cell models.

Single-cell sequencing and MR analyses revealed that aging was associated with depletion of muscle satellite cells and skeletal muscle cells, together with increased neutrophils and fibroblasts. TGF-β1-related signaling showed a genetically supported association with sarcopenia-related traits and was closely associated with fibrotic remodeling in aged skeletal muscle. Rg2 treatment significantly mitigated age-associated weight gain while improving muscle mass, strength, and exercise endurance. Mechanistically, Rg2 interacted with TGF-β1 and attenuated downstream Smad2/3 phosphorylation in vitro and in vivo, thereby modulating inflammatory and fibrosis-related markers and partially reversing muscle tissue and cellular senescence.
Our findings suggest that ginsenoside Rg2 alleviates TGF-β1/Smad-mediated fibrotic remodeling and improves the aging-related inflammatory-fibrotic microenvironment during skeletal muscle aging.

artigos.titulo: Tirzepatide Use Resulted in Clinically Meaningful Weight Reduction in Individuals With Obesity or Overweight: 12-Month Real-World Results
artigos.autores: Chinthammit C, Gibble TH, Dehghan M et al.
artigos.destaque: After 12 months of persistent tirzepatide use, individuals experienced clinically meaningful weight reduction, comparable to outcomes reported in clinical trials. These real-world findings were observed both in GLP-1 RA-naïve and experienced individuals.

resumo.texto: This study assessed the real-world effectiveness of tirzepatide in commercially insured individuals without diabetes, eligible for obesity medications (OMs), including glucagon like-peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA)-naïve individuals (i.e., no GLP-1 RA prescription during the 12-month pre-index period) and GLP-1 RA-experienced individuals.

This retrospective, observational cohort study used Optum's de-identified Market Clarity Data (Optum Market Clarity). Adults with ≥ 1 prescription claim for tirzepatide between November 2023 and March 2024, with continuous medical/pharmacy enrollment for ≥ 12 months pre-index and post-index and available pre- and post-index data were included. Baseline demographics, clinical characteristics, and treatment effectiveness (change from baseline in weight, body mass index, and cardiometabolic risk factors) were assessed among OM-eligible individuals who were persistent on tirzepatide for ≥ 12 months.

The GLP-1 RA-naïve and experienced cohorts included 230 individuals (mean age: 49.5 years, 72.2% female) and 123 individuals (mean age: 48.9 years, 81.3% female), respectively, who were persistent on tirzepatide for 12 months with documented pre- and post-index weight measurements. At baseline, more than 85% of individuals in each cohort had ≥ 1 obesity-related complication, most commonly dyslipidemia, hypertension, and prediabetes. At 12 months post-index, the GLP-1 RA-naïve cohort achieved a mean weight reduction of 19.3%, while the GLP-1 RA-experienced cohort achieved a mean weight reduction of 13.1%.

After 12 months of persistent tirzepatide use, individuals experienced clinically meaningful weight reduction, comparable to outcomes reported in clinical trials. These real-world findings were observed both in GLP-1 RA-naïve and experienced individuals.

artigos.titulo: GLP-1-Based Therapy in Type 1 Diabetes: Balancing Efficacy, Safety, and Patient Selection
artigos.autores: Rossatto T, de Andrade Oliveira R, Cardoso AM
artigos.destaque: Current evidence supports a phenotype-directed approach centred primarily on adults with T1D and obesity, accompanied by careful patient selection, individualised insulin adjustment, glucose and ketone monitoring, and structured patient education. The clinical question has shifted from whether GLP-1-based therapies are effective in T1D to which patients are most likely to achieve a favourable benefit-risk balance and how these therapies can be used safely.

resumo.texto: To critically examine the evolving evidence on glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide as adjuncts to insulin therapy in type 1 diabetes (T1D), with particular emphasis on their benefit-risk balance in individuals with overweight or obesity.

This narrative review examines evidence on liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide in T1D, focusing on effects on body weight and insulin requirements, alongside hypoglycaemia, ketosis, diabetic ketoacidosis and gastrointestinal tolerability.

Early trials with liraglutide demonstrated reductions in body weight and insulin requirements but raised concerns regarding hypoglycaemia and ketosis. More recently, semaglutide and tirzepatide have renewed interest in incretin-based therapy in T1D, particularly among individuals with obesity. Their greater effects on weight and insulin requirements introduce a clinically important safety challenge: insulin must be reduced sufficiently to prevent hypoglycaemia while maintaining adequate insulinization to suppress lipolysis and ketogenesis. Gastrointestinal adverse events may further destabilize this balance through reduced carbohydrate intake and dehydration.

Current evidence supports a phenotype-directed approach centred primarily on adults with T1D and obesity, accompanied by careful patient selection, individualised insulin adjustment, glucose and ketone monitoring, and structured patient education. The clinical question has shifted from whether GLP-1-based therapies are effective in T1D to which patients are most likely to achieve a favourable benefit-risk balance and how these therapies can be used safely.

artigos.titulo: Interpreting Diabetic Retinal Outcomes After GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and Tirzepatide Initiation: Clinical Evidence and Its Limits
artigos.autores: Wu B, He BS
artigos.destaque: Current guidance supports establishing retinal status and coordinating diabetes and eye care during treatment intensification. The implications differ between patients with recent screening and no known retinopathy, established non-proliferative disease, and active sight-threatening disease or recent retinal treatment. No universal safe rate of glycated haemoglobin decline or retinal-protective titration regimen has been established. Future studies should align eligibility and treatment initiation, distinguish incident disease from progression, and use scheduled retinal assessments. A comparison between two specific medicines can inform treatment choice but cannot exclude risks shared by both.

resumo.texto: Reports of diabetic retinopathy after potent glucose-lowering treatment create uncertainty for clinicians, particularly when studies measure different outcomes in patients with different baseline retinal disease. This review examines diabetic retinal outcomes after glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide initiation.
This critical narrative review uses targeted, non-systematic study selection. It distinguishes disease onset or progression from detection, treatment use and subsequent visual function.

The SUSTAIN-6 retinopathy-complication signal remains clinically relevant; post hoc associations with early glycated haemoglobin reduction do not establish causal mediation. Contemporary cohorts report differing associations across baseline retinal strata, comparators and endpoints. Positive signals should be presented alongside their absolute event proportions and limitations, rather than dismissed because observational adjustment is imperfect. Conversely, non-significant results do not establish equivalence or class-wide safety.

Current guidance supports establishing retinal status and coordinating diabetes and eye care during treatment intensification. The implications differ between patients with recent screening and no known retinopathy, established non-proliferative disease, and active sight-threatening disease or recent retinal treatment. No universal safe rate of glycated haemoglobin decline or retinal-protective titration regimen has been established. Future studies should align eligibility and treatment initiation, distinguish incident disease from progression, and use scheduled retinal assessments. A comparison between two specific medicines can inform treatment choice but cannot exclude risks shared by both.

artigos.titulo: The Impact of Incretin-Based Therapies on Anthropometric and Metabolic Parameters in Women with Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome
artigos.autores: Koceva A, Janež A, Jensterle M
artigos.destaque: Interpretation of the available evidence is limited by the predominance of short-term trials at sub-obesity doses, frequent co-administration with metformin, and the absence of phenotype-stratified data, leaving the full metabolic potential of these agents in PMOS incompletely defined. Larger, longer, and higher-dose trials are needed to fully characterize the anthropometric and metabolic potential of these agents in PMOS.

resumo.texto: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recently renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), affects 170 million women globally and is often accompanied by obesity and various levels of insulin resistance. Incretin-based therapies, including the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists liraglutide and semaglutide, and the dual GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) agonist tirzepatide, offer a biologically plausible mechanism for targeting metabolic dysfunction in PMOS. This review examines clinical trial evidence on the anthropometric and metabolic effects of incretin-based therapies in this population, including a focus on women of reproductive age, who face distinct challenges related to preconception planning, treatment duration, and post-discontinuation metabolic and weight management. Available literature shows that liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide produce clinically meaningful reductions in body weight, body mass index (BMI), and waist circumference, with some studies also confirming preferential effects on visceral and ectopic fat compartments. Glycaemic and insulin resistance outcomes vary across studies, while lipid and blood pressure effects remain incompletely characterized. Although emerging data suggest that higher-potency agents may yield more consistent weight-loss benefits, available PMOS-specific evidence does not establish comparative metabolic superiority among agents. Interpretation of the available evidence is limited by the predominance of short-term trials at sub-obesity doses, frequent co-administration with metformin, and the absence of phenotype-stratified data, leaving the full metabolic potential of these agents in PMOS incompletely defined. Larger, longer, and higher-dose trials are needed to fully characterize the anthropometric and metabolic potential of these agents in PMOS.

artigos.titulo: Pancreatic and Gallbladder Adverse Events Associated with Tirzepatide in Obesity Management: A Scoping Review
artigos.autores: Kutsyba T, Raj S, van der Berg M
artigos.destaque: Pancreatic and gallbladder AEs were reported across clinical trials, observational studies, case reports, and pharmacovigilance databases. RCTs generally reported low frequencies of pancreatobiliary AEs, whereas pharmacovigilance databases captured a broader spectrum of reported events. Variability in study populations, comorbidity profiles, reporting methods, and the absence of exposure denominators limited direct comparison across evidence sources. Vigilant monitoring and standardized AE reporting are needed to further characterize the pancreatobiliary safety profile of tirzepatide.

resumo.texto: Obesity is a chronic and relapsing condition that affects all demographics and results in comorbidities, rising healthcare costs, and social challenges. Tirzepatide, a novel dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, has emerged as a promising therapy offering significant weight reduction. However, uncertainty remains regarding its pancreatic and gallbladder safety profile across different populations and evidence sources.

To systematically map existing evidence on the safety of tirzepatide in obesity management, with an emphasis on pancreatic- and gallbladder-related adverse events (AEs) across randomized controlled trials (RCTs), observational studies, case reports, and pharmacovigilance evidence.

Following the methodological framework of Arksey and O'Malley (2005), expanded with Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, this scoping review included RCTs, observational studies, and post-marketing safety reports identified between December 2019 and September 2025. The searches were conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, and the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), with additional evidence identified through gray literature, targeted journal searches, and published pharmacovigilance studies based on the EudraVigilance database. ClinicalTrials.gov was subsequently searched as an additional source to identify relevant clinical trials. Studies were eligible if they examined pancreatic or gallbladder AEs in the context of tirzepatide exposure among individuals with obesity. The review included 11 RCTs, 5 observational studies, 4 case reports, 1 EudraVigilance pharmacovigilance analysis, and 575 FAERS reports. Pancreatic and gallbladder AEs were systematically extracted and coded using MedDRA version 28.1, following the predetermined hierarchy. Findings were mapped descriptively across data sources without formal comparative statistical testing.

Pancreatic and gallbladder AEs were reported infrequently in RCTs. Pancreatitis was reported in 11 participants across five RCTs, with study-specific frequencies ranging from 0.2% (3 of 1,896) to 3.7% (1 of 27), while cholelithiasis was reported in 73 participants across 11 RCTs, with frequencies ranging from 0.3% (1 of 335 and 1 of 364) to 3.7% (1 of 27). Among observational studies, pancreatitis was reported in three studies, with proportions of 0.6% (63/10,002), 0.9% (1/110), and 2.1% (5,882/280,094). One retrospective cohort study reported an incidence rate of 3.84 events per 1,000 person-years among 9,193 participants, while cholelithiasis was reported at 11.89 events per 1,000 person-years in the same cohort. In the EudraVigilance pharmacovigilance analysis, pancreatitis represented 363 reported AEs (6.3% of all AEs and 19.4% of gastrointestinal AEs). In the FAERS database, pancreatitis accounted for 155/288 pancreatic-related reports [53.8%] and cholelithiasis for 143/249 gallbladder-related reports [57.4%]. Four case reports described six distinct AEs: edematous pancreatitis, acute pancreatitis, pancreatitis necrotizing, acalculous cholecystitis, gallstones, and gallbladder wall thickening, each reported once. Female participants, White participants, adults aged 18-64 years, and participants from the United States (US) predominated among reported demographic characteristics; however, demographic characteristics and comorbidity profiles were inconsistently reported and varied across studies.

Pancreatic and gallbladder AEs were reported across clinical trials, observational studies, case reports, and pharmacovigilance databases. RCTs generally reported low frequencies of pancreatobiliary AEs, whereas pharmacovigilance databases captured a broader spectrum of reported events. Variability in study populations, comorbidity profiles, reporting methods, and the absence of exposure denominators limited direct comparison across evidence sources. Vigilant monitoring and standardized AE reporting are needed to further characterize the pancreatobiliary safety profile of tirzepatide.

artigos.titulo: Beyond reproduction: the emerging role of FSH in postmenopausal aging
artigos.autores: Vallejo MS, Paradas A, Neira H
artigos.destaque: Experimental studies indicate that reducing FSH may benefit bone and adiposity, while preliminary clinical evidence regarding cognition remains inconclusive. Thus, FSH may represent not only a marker of menopause, but also a potential marker of risk and, ultimately, a therapeutic target.

resumo.texto: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is traditionally regarded as a biochemical marker of menopause and declining ovarian function. However, emerging evidence suggests that its role may extend beyond reproductive physiology. During the menopause transition, FSH concentrations rise progressively, initially due to declining inhibin B and later to loss of ovarian estradiol and inhibin production. Evidence of FSH effects in bone, adipose tissue, the cardiovascular system and brain has raised the possibility of broader physiological actions. Higher FSH levels have been associated with bone loss and hip fracture risk, adverse cardiometabolic and vascular changes, and cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease. Although these associations do not establish causality, they suggest that FSH may contribute to some consequences of reproductive aging rather than simply reflect ovarian failure. Experimental studies indicate that reducing FSH may benefit bone and adiposity, while preliminary clinical evidence regarding cognition remains inconclusive. Thus, FSH may represent not only a marker of menopause, but also a potential marker of risk and, ultimately, a therapeutic target.

artigos.titulo: Association of conventional and non-conventional lipid profile with cognitive impairment among type 2 diabetic patients
artigos.autores: Esmaeili B, Hesari E, Khalaji K et al.
artigos.destaque: Among conventional lipid profiles, only the HDL-C levels were related to cognitive dysfunction and no relationship was observed between cognitive impairment and non-conventional lipids.

resumo.texto: To explore the connection between atherogenic index of plasma, non-HDL-C, as well as conventional lipid profiles in relation to cognition dysfunction among the diabetic participants aged over 60 years.

The data of this cross-sectional research study came from the Bushehr Elderly Health (BEH) Program (Phase II) carried on the participants aged 60 and above. The functional status of the participants was assessed using the Functional Assessment Staging tool (FAST) and Category Fluency Test (CFT). After the measurement of lipid parameters, we used multiple logistic regression to analyze their relationship with cognitive impairment (CI) among the participants.

There were 836 participants in this cross-sectional study. Of them, 339 had cognitive decline. The average age of the subjects was 68.6 ± 5.7 years. There was no relationship between lipid parameters and cognition dysfunction with the exception of HDL-C. A higher amount of HDL-C had a protective role. While older age (OR = 1.05, 95% CI = 1.01-1.08, P = 0.002) and higher education (OR = 1.08, 95% CI = 1.04-1.12, P < 0.001) were positively related to cognitive impairment, male gender (OR = 0.41, 95% CI = 0.27-0.62, P < 0.001) was associated with 59% reduced odds of cognition impairment.
Among conventional lipid profiles, only the HDL-C levels were related to cognitive dysfunction and no relationship was observed between cognitive impairment and non-conventional lipids.

artigos.titulo: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
artigos.destaque: A new clinical trial suggests that a simple daily fiber supplement could significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis pain, improve muscle strength, and make the body less sensitive to pain. Researchers discovered that the benefits may be linked to changes in gut bacteria and the hormone GLP-1, revealing a promising new approach to arthritis relief.

artigos.titulo: Scientists discover a surprising clue to why some brains resist Alzheimer’s
artigos.destaque: Why do some people stay mentally sharp even when their brains show signs of Alzheimer’s disease? Scientists in the Netherlands may have uncovered an important clue hidden in a rare group of immature brain cells. Researchers discovered that these cells remain present even in people over 80, but their behavior differs dramatically between those who develop dementia and those who remain cognitively healthy.

artigos.titulo: Pediatric obesity pharmacotherapy: a practical guide for general pediatricians
artigos.autores: Mulvihill H, Pliskin L, Ponery N et al.
artigos.destaque: Readiness to prescribe these medications is influenced by physician comfort, practice infrastructure, and access-related barriers. Specialty training (i.e., endocrinology, gastroenterology, obesity medicine) does not have to be a requirement for managing obesity.

resumo.texto: Multimodal treatment approaches to pediatric obesity, including pharmacotherapy, are now recommended as part of an early intervention strategy to improve long-term health outcomes. However, barriers to prescribing obesity medications limit patient access to them. This review summarizes practical approaches to pediatric obesity pharmacotherapy tailored for the general pediatrician, based on evidence and expert opinion.

The American Academy of Pediatrics clinical practice guideline for the evaluation and management of pediatric obesity calls for early, individualized intervention, including consideration of pharmacotherapy. Available obesity medications include those that are Federal Drug Administration (FDA)-approved for this indication and those that are used "off-label" with FDA approval for other indications.

Obesity pharmacotherapy should be considered an adjunct to lifestyle interventions for pediatric obesity. Readiness to prescribe these medications is influenced by physician comfort, practice infrastructure, and access-related barriers. Specialty training (i.e., endocrinology, gastroenterology, obesity medicine) does not have to be a requirement for managing obesity.

artigos.titulo: Association between anesthetic fresh gas flow and postoperative inflammatory response in laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: A retrospective cohort study
artigos.autores: Çitilcioğlu US, Özdoğan HK
artigos.destaque: Low-flow sevoflurane anesthesia was associated with smaller postoperative increases in RDW and CRP compared with standard-flow anesthesia in obese patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. These findings suggest an association between fresh gas flow strategy and selected postoperative inflammatory marker changes during bariatric surgery.

resumo.texto: Perioperative inflammation is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes, and anesthetic management may modulate this response. However, the influence of fresh gas flow strategies during volatile anesthesia on perioperative inflammatory responses has not been adequately characterized. Evidence in obese surgical patients remains particularly limited despite the chronic low-grade inflammatory state and exaggerated responses to surgical stress associated with obesity. In this retrospective cohort study, 155 obese adult patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy under sevoflurane anesthesia were evaluated. Patients received either low-flow (1 L/min, n = 76) or standard-flow (4 L/min, n = 79) anesthesia. Perioperative changes (Δ = postoperative - preoperative) in red cell distribution width (RDW), C-reactive protein (CRP), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) were assessed using preoperative and 24-hour postoperative values. Between-group changes in these 3 designated primary outcomes were compared, and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed as adjusted supportive analyses. Intraoperative hemodynamic and oxygenation parameters and postoperative hospital length of stay were evaluated as exploratory secondary outcomes. ΔRDW and ΔCRP were greater in the standard-flow group than in the low-flow group (both P < .001) and remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (α = 0.0167), whereas no statistically significant between-group difference was observed for ΔNLR (P = .902). After adjustment for the measured covariates and calendar period, standard-flow anesthesia remained associated with greater ΔRDW and ΔCRP. No statistically detectable between-group differences were observed in the longitudinal hemodynamic and oxygenation outcomes or postoperative hospital length of stay. Low-flow sevoflurane anesthesia was associated with smaller postoperative increases in RDW and CRP compared with standard-flow anesthesia in obese patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. These findings suggest an association between fresh gas flow strategy and selected postoperative inflammatory marker changes during bariatric surgery.

artigos.titulo: Frailty Rather Than Sonographic Muscle Measurement Predicts Outcome in Liver Cirrhosis
artigos.autores: Kremer WM, Schwarz A, Dumont MC et al.
artigos.destaque: CFS is robustly associated with poorer prognosis in patients with liver cirrhosis and seems to be superior to sonographic muscle thickness measurement of the thigh.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia and frailty are frequent in patients with liver cirrhosis and are associated with morbidity and mortality. Given the limitations of computed tomography (CT) for routine assessment of muscle loss and the need for practical bedside assessment, we aimed to compare sonographic muscle thickness measurement and the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) for their prognostic value in patients with liver cirrhosis.

In this study, data of prospectively recruited patients with liver cirrhosis (both in- and outpatients) treated at a tertiary care centre were retrospectively analysed. Sonographic muscle thickness measurement was used to calculate the feather thigh muscle thickness index (fTMTI) and the compression thigh muscle thickness index (cTMTI). Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale. Patients were followed for liver transplantation or death.

In total, 153 patients were included with a median Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) of 18 (Interquartile range (IQR) 10; 24). Ninety-five patients (62.0%) were male, and 70 patients (46%) were recruited in the outpatient setting. During the 90-day follow-up period, 71 patients (46.4%) either died or underwent liver transplantation. Outpatients had more muscle mass than inpatients and a lower CFS (fTMTI 19.1 mm/m vs. 12.1 mm/m, p < 0.001 and CFS 3 vs. 5, p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox-regression models adjusted for age and MELD score, a higher CFS remained independently associated with mortality and liver transplantation (LT) (HR 1.25 (1.14; 1.63), p < 0.001), whereas fTMTI and cTMTI were not consistently associated with a poorer prognosis (fTMTI HR 1.52 (0.68; 3.42), p = 0.300; cTMTI HR 1.01 (0.61; 1.68), p > 0.9). Subgroup analyses in men confirmed a superior prognostic value of CFS (HR 1.51 (1.17; 1.94), p = 0.001) over sonographic muscle thickness measurement (cTMTI HR 0.94 (0.84; 1.04), p = 0.200; fTMTI HR 0.93 (0.88; 1.00), p = 0.039).
CFS is robustly associated with poorer prognosis in patients with liver cirrhosis and seems to be superior to sonographic muscle thickness measurement of the thigh.

artigos.titulo: Aquaporin-4 Orchestrates Muscle Cell Differentiation and Satellite Cell Preservation: A Novel Target in Age-Related Muscle Decline
artigos.autores: Girón MD, Manzano M, Pereira SL et al.
artigos.destaque: Reduced AQP4 expression is associated with impaired muscle regeneration and functional decline in aged skeletal muscle. Experimental AQP4 loss disrupts myogenic signalling, membrane organization and increases progression to senescence, whereas AQP4 restoration rescues these defects. These findings identify AQP4 as a biologically plausible therapeutic target for strategies aimed at preserving or restoring muscle health and regenerative capacity in ageing-associated muscle dysfunction.

resumo.texto: Impaired muscle regeneration is a key contributor to age-related muscle decline, yet the molecular mechanisms linking muscle water homeostasis to regenerative failure remain incompletely understood. Aquaporin-4 (AQP4), a major skeletal muscle water channel, may have functions beyond water transport that are relevant to muscle maintenance and repair. We investigated whether altered AQP4 expression contributes to age-related defects in skeletal muscle regeneration and whether AQP4 may represent a targetable pathway for muscle dysfunction associated with ageing.

Skeletal muscle from young adult (25-week; n = 9) and aged (85-week; n = 8) rats was analysed for extracellular and intracellular water content by bioimpedance. AQP4, AQP1 and myogenic markers were measured by Western blot. Satellite cells isolated from skeletal muscle were assessed for proliferation, differentiation and expression of differentiation markers. To define the mechanistic role of AQP4 in myogenesis, CRISPR-generated AQP4-silenced L6 rat myoblasts were evaluated for proliferation, differentiation, senescence and Akt/PKB signalling. Rescue experiments were performed by restoring AQP4 expression in silenced cells. Data are reported as mean ± SEM.

Compared with young rats, aged rats showed an altered intracellular water-to-lean mass ratio (0.94 vs. 0.62, p < 0.05), a 33% reduction in AQP4 expression (p < 0.05) and reduced muscle strength (3.1 vs. 2.6, p < 0.05), with AQP4 levels correlating with muscle performance. Satellite cells from aged muscle exhibited 29% lower AQP4 expression and 39% lower Pax7 expression (both p < 0.05), together with reduced myogenic differentiation (30% decrease, p < 0.05). In L6 myoblasts, AQP4 silencing reduced proliferation (20% decrease, p < 0.05), impaired myotube differentiation (50% decrease, p < 0.05), increased senescence (30% increase, p < 0.05) and decreased Akt/PKB signalling by 42% (p < 0.05). AQP4 silencing was also associated with decreased dystrophin localization at the plasma membrane (50%, p < 0.05). Re-expression of AQP4 reversed these abnormalities and restored the phenotype toward wild-type levels (all p < 0.05).

Reduced AQP4 expression is associated with impaired muscle regeneration and functional decline in aged skeletal muscle. Experimental AQP4 loss disrupts myogenic signalling, membrane organization and increases progression to senescence, whereas AQP4 restoration rescues these defects. These findings identify AQP4 as a biologically plausible therapeutic target for strategies aimed at preserving or restoring muscle health and regenerative capacity in ageing-associated muscle dysfunction.

artigos.titulo: Oral Health-Related Adverse Events of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists
artigos.autores: Massarotto FC, Mahmoud AH, Watson GE et al.
artigos.destaque: This analysis highlights emerging safety signals in oral health and underscores the need for heightened clinical awareness and prospective studies to characterize the incidence, timing, and mechanisms of oral AEs associated with GLP-1 RA therapy.Knowledge Transfer Statement:Understanding the oral adverse effects associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists allows clinicians and dental providers to more effectively counsel patients initiating or continuing these medications. By recognizing early symptoms such as dry mouth, dysgeusia, and reflux-related irritation, providers can implement targeted preventive strategies-including hydration guidance, salivary substitutes, dietary modifications, and closer oral health monitoring-to reduce complications and improve patient comfort, adherence, and overall treatment outcomes. This knowledge enhances interdisciplinary management of individuals using GLP-1 RAs.

resumo.texto: As the clinical use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) continues to grow for the management of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular and renal protection, noncirrhotic fatty liver disease, and weight management, their potential implications for oral health need to be considered.
This study examined oral health-related adverse events (AEs) associated with GLP-1 RAs using postmarketing data from the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).

FAERS reports for available GLP-1 RAs, exenatide, liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide, and tirzepatide, were screened from their initial market introduction through December 2025, identifying 364,274 total AE reports, of which 31,195 (8.6%) involved oral, craniofacial, or dental manifestations.

Tirzepatide, despite being one of the most recently approved GLP-1 RAs, accounted for the highest overall AE volume, and semaglutide demonstrated the largest proportion of oral health-related AEs. A disproportionality analysis revealed a significant drug-specific signal for dry mouth of semaglutide, while vomiting, regurgitation, and reflux-related events produced a significant signal across all 5 drugs. Sensory disorders, including dysgeusia and taste disturbances, also demonstrated significant proportional reporting ratios (PRRs) and reporting odds ratios (RORs) for several GLP-1 RAs. Association analysis of AEs showed significant associations between vomiting and taste disturbances, as well as between dry mouth and dysgeusia, particularly with semaglutide and dulaglutide.

This analysis highlights emerging safety signals in oral health and underscores the need for heightened clinical awareness and prospective studies to characterize the incidence, timing, and mechanisms of oral AEs associated with GLP-1 RA therapy.Knowledge Transfer Statement:Understanding the oral adverse effects associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists allows clinicians and dental providers to more effectively counsel patients initiating or continuing these medications. By recognizing early symptoms such as dry mouth, dysgeusia, and reflux-related irritation, providers can implement targeted preventive strategies-including hydration guidance, salivary substitutes, dietary modifications, and closer oral health monitoring-to reduce complications and improve patient comfort, adherence, and overall treatment outcomes. This knowledge enhances interdisciplinary management of individuals using GLP-1 RAs.

artigos.titulo: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Transplant Recipients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Study
artigos.autores: Blazquez-Bermejo Z, Enríquez-Vázquez D, García-Romero E et al.
artigos.destaque: In HT recipients with T2DM, GLP-1 RAs were associated with improved glycemic and cardiometabolic parameters and were generally well tolerated. These findings support the use of GLP-1 RAs as a valuable therapeutic strategy for the management of T2DM after HT.

resumo.texto: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequent after heart transplantation (HT) and is exacerbated by immunosuppressive therapy. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) may improve metabolic control, but data in HT recipients are limited.

We performed a retrospective, multicenter study including HT recipients with T2DM from 14 Spanish centers. In patients treated with GLP-1 RAs, we assessed antidiabetic and immunosuppressive therapies, adverse events, and changes in metabolic parameters, insulin dose, and immunosuppressant trough levels during the first year after GLP-1 RA initiation.

Among 734 HT recipients with T2DM (2011-2021), 108 (14.7%) received GLP-1 RAs (mean age 55.4 ± 9.0 y; 79.6% male), initiated 4.0 ± 3.1 y post-HT. At baseline, 64.8% had obesity. Semaglutide was used in 59%, dulaglutide in 27%, liraglutide in 13%, and tirzepatide in 1%; 41.7% achieved the maximum therapeutic dose. After 1 y, significant reductions were observed in body weight (-6.2 kg; 95% confidence interval [CI], -7.7 to -4.5 kg), fasting glucose (-27 mg/dL; 95% CI, -41 to -7 mg/dL), glycated hemoglobin (-0.74%; 95% CI, -1.12% to -0.35%), total cholesterol (-12 mg/dL; 95% CI, -19 to -6 mg/dL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (-8 mg/dL; 95% CI, -14 to -2 mg/dL), triglycerides (-29 mg/dL; 95% CI, -53 to -5 mg/dL), and systolic blood pressure (-3.6 mm Hg; 95% CI, -6.4 to -0.9 mm Hg). Tacrolimus trough levels decreased modestly (-0.7 ng/mL; 95% CI, -1.4 to -0.1 ng/mL; P = 0.025), without episodes of acute rejection. Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in 12.0%, leading to discontinuation in 3.7%.

In HT recipients with T2DM, GLP-1 RAs were associated with improved glycemic and cardiometabolic parameters and were generally well tolerated. These findings support the use of GLP-1 RAs as a valuable therapeutic strategy for the management of T2DM after HT.

artigos.titulo: Disaster exposure and women's mental and general health: evidence from longitudinal data
artigos.autores: Seema M, Afoakwah C, Byrnes J
artigos.destaque: Reported disaster exposure was associated with modest within-person declines in women's mental and general health, while evidence for psychological distress was less conclusive. The findings support consideration of women's health in disaster preparedness and recovery planning.

resumo.texto: Disasters can have important consequences for health, yet much evidence is cross-sectional and cannot account for time-invariant individual heterogeneity.
To examine the association between reported disaster exposure and women's mental health, psychological distress, and general health using longitudinal Australian data.

Data from women aged ≥ 15 years participating in Waves 9-22 of the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia Survey were analysed. Individual and survey-wave fixed-effects models examined within-person associations between disaster exposure and mental health (MHI-5), psychological distress (Kessler-10), and SF-36 General Health. Sensitivity analyses considered long-term illness and single exposure. Dynamic associations were examined using the Callaway-Sant'Anna multiple-period difference-in-differences estimator with formal pre-trend tests.

Reported disaster exposure was associated with modest declines in mental health (β = -0.86, 95% CI - 1.51 to -0.20) and general health (β = -0.83, 95% CI - 1.44 to -0.22). Psychological distress was higher but not statistically significant in the primary model (β = 0.33, 95% CI - 0.04 to 0.70). Sensitivity analyses generally supported the mental and general health findings. Event-study analyses showed no consistent evidence of persistent post-exposure deterioration; however, the MHI-5 joint pre-trend test indicated differential pre-exposure patterns, limiting causal interpretation.

Reported disaster exposure was associated with modest within-person declines in women's mental and general health, while evidence for psychological distress was less conclusive. The findings support consideration of women's health in disaster preparedness and recovery planning.

artigos.titulo: Regular napping mitigates the onset of cognitive fatigue and protects against stress-inflammatory responses to real-world sleep debt
artigos.autores: Belhout S, Poudevigne L, Mouton L et al.
artigos.destaque: Chronic sleep debt increased attentional fatigability without exacerbating executive decline, an effect that may be driven by neuro-inflammatory processes and effectively alleviated by regular daytime napping. Importantly, these findings indicate that chronic afternoon napping may confer protective and long-lasting restorative benefits observable in morning assessments, reflecting effects that persist over a 24-h period.

resumo.texto: Chronic sleep debt impairs cognitive processes, stress regulation, and immune homeostasis, while sustained cognitive engagement induces mental fatigue. However, it remains unclear how chronically insufficient sleep in real-life conditions accelerates the onset of mental fatigue during prolonged cognitive activity-and whether daytime napping can buffer these effects. This study investigated the combined effects of chronic sleep debt and extended cognitive engagement on cognitive fatigue and salivary neuro-immune and neurotrophic markers in an ecologically valid context. Compared with controls, participants with chronic sleep debt showed pronounced declines in Psychomotor Vigilance Task performance (reaction time and number of lapses) across both time-on-task and time-on-week and showed higher commission rates in the executive Go-NoGo task. These morning impairments were partially attenuated in the participants who practiced afternoon chronic naps, and the reduction in lapses was correlated with nap frequency. Biologically, chronic sleep debt was associated with a blunted morning cortisol response, an increase in IL-1β and IL-6, and a reduction in BDNF levels, but not observed in either the Control or Sleep-Debt + Nap groups. In the Sleep-Debt group, IL-1β levels were positively correlated with sustained attention deficits. Chronic sleep debt increased attentional fatigability without exacerbating executive decline, an effect that may be driven by neuro-inflammatory processes and effectively alleviated by regular daytime napping. Importantly, these findings indicate that chronic afternoon napping may confer protective and long-lasting restorative benefits observable in morning assessments, reflecting effects that persist over a 24-h period.

artigos.titulo: Communication breakdown: Impaired pericyte KATP channels in a model of Alzheimer's disease
artigos.autores: Jackson WF
artigos.destaque: These novel findings present new therapeutic targets to slow or possibly prevent the reduced cerebral blood flow in Alzheimer's disease, perhaps delaying or preventing cognitive decline. Like all scientific advances, they also open the door for new areas of research.

resumo.texto: The brain requires a continuous supply of blood in proportion to its metabolic activity, a process that is disrupted in Alzheimer's disease. However, the mechanisms responsible for altered brain blood flow regulation in Alzheimer's disease remain poorly defined. In an earlier issue of JGP, Hariharan et al. (https://doi.org/10.1085/jgp.202614014) significantly add to our understanding of this pathology by showing that ATP-Sensitive K+ (KATP) channels in thin strand pericytes on cerebral capillaries are compromised at 6-8 weeks in the 5X-FAD mouse model of Alzheimer's disease. They also confirmed that cerebral capillary endothelial inward rectifier K+ (KIR) channels are crippled and importantly show that this defect occurs at 2-4 months, before significant cognitive defects have been reported. Combined, these channelopathies severely attenuate electrical communication along cerebral capillaries, dampening blood flow regulation. These novel findings present new therapeutic targets to slow or possibly prevent the reduced cerebral blood flow in Alzheimer's disease, perhaps delaying or preventing cognitive decline. Like all scientific advances, they also open the door for new areas of research.

artigos.titulo: Neurotropic herpesviruses as accelerators of brain aging: The role of latency and reactivation in neurodegeneration
artigos.autores: Nadholta P, Volety I, Shukla D
artigos.destaque: Clinical neurodegeneration emerges when the cumulative burden of lifelong viral reactivation exceeds the aging brain's capacity to maintain homeostasis. Recognizing herpesviruses as modifiable drivers of brain aging identifies subclinical viral reactivation as a key therapeutic target for preventing cognitive decline.

resumo.texto: Neurotropic herpesviruses establish lifelong latency within the human nervous system. Traditionally viewed as either harmless latent infections or rare causes of acute encephalitis, growing evidence suggests these viruses undergo recurrent, subclinical reactivations throughout life. This review summarizes recent advances and introduces the multiple-hit viral reactivation model, proposing that repeated silent reactivation events act as cumulative biological stressors that accelerate brain aging. We describe a self-reinforcing cycle in which age-related immunosenescence impairs control of viral latency, leading to recurrent subclinical reactivation, chronic neuroinflammation, cellular senescence, and progressive disruption of central nervous system homeostasis. Rather than directly causing neurodegenerative disease, recurrent host-virus interactions gradually diminish brain resilience and promote the accumulation of pathogenic protein aggregates, including amyloid-β, tau, α-synuclein, and TDP-43. Clinical neurodegeneration emerges when the cumulative burden of lifelong viral reactivation exceeds the aging brain's capacity to maintain homeostasis. Recognizing herpesviruses as modifiable drivers of brain aging identifies subclinical viral reactivation as a key therapeutic target for preventing cognitive decline.

artigos.titulo: Neuroprotective roles of Klotho signaling in Huntington's disease: From molecular insights to clinical translation
artigos.autores: Gupta V, Kumar D, Begam M et al.
artigos.destaque: Such a structure encourages Klotho-based interventions as a new, mechanism-based approach to HD. Further experimental studies are required to determine whether modulation of Klotho signaling could influence disease progression in HD.

resumo.texto: Huntington's Disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by CAG repeat expansion in the HTT gene, producing toxic mutant huntingtin (mHTT) protein. This leads to progressive motor dysfunction, cognitive decline, and psychiatric disturbances. Despite advances in understanding mHTT toxicity, potentially disease-modifying therapies remain scarce, underscoring the need for novel approaches targeting core pathophysiological mechanisms. Klotho, a multifunctional anti-aging protein, regulates several pathways relevant to neuronal survival and may have relevance to HD pathophysiology. Klotho is a co-receptor with a membrane and is a soluble co-receptor that regulates synaptic and metabolic homeostasis. Although direct experimental evidence in HD remains limited, emerging findings from aging and neurodegeneration research suggest that Klotho-mediated pathways may influence mechanisms relevant to HD pathogenesis. It suppresses fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) signaling and major pathways such as PI3K/Akt-FOXO, Wnt/ -catenin and insulin/IGF-1 pathways, which oppose the hallmarks of HD, namely excitotoxicity, calcium dysregulation, impaired neuroprotection, and peripheral neuroinflammation. There is growing evidence of the involvement of Klotho in mitochondrial health and biogenesis, mitophagy coordination, and oxidative stress resistance - direct mitigating cellular toxicity caused by mHTT. These mechanistic overlaps suggest that Klotho signaling may represent a potential area for investigation in HD. It deals with oxidative stress, excitotoxicity, inflammation, and metabolic dysregulation, and compares it to other diseases of the neurodegenerative type in which Klotho deficits contribute to pathology. Such a structure encourages Klotho-based interventions as a new, mechanism-based approach to HD. Further experimental studies are required to determine whether modulation of Klotho signaling could influence disease progression in HD.

artigos.titulo: Metacognitive Prediction of Creative Performance in Divergent Thinking
artigos.autores: Sun T, Xie X, Sun Y et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings suggest that individuals can prospectively monitor aspects of divergent thinking supported by semantic accessibility and category-based search, but may have difficulty anticipating originality, which may depend more strongly on remote association and representational transformation. The study contributes to research on creative metacognition by showing that metacognitive prediction accuracy in divergent thinking is dimension-specific rather than uniformly accurate or inaccurate.

resumo.texto: Understanding how individuals monitor and predict their own creative performance is essential for advancing theories of creative metacognition. Despite extensive research on metacognitive predictions in memory and problem solving, little is known about whether people can accurately anticipate their performance in divergent thinking tasks. The present study examined prospective metacognitive prediction accuracy in the Alternative Uses Task (AUT), focusing on fluency, flexibility, and originality. Thirty-two participants first ranked 10 everyday objects according to how well they believed they would perform on each AUT item and subsequently completed a verbal AUT for the same objects. Creative performance was independently scored by trained raters, and prediction accuracy was quantified using Gamma correlations between predicted and actual performance rankings. Results showed above-chance prediction accuracy for fluency and flexibility, but not for originality. These findings suggest that individuals can prospectively monitor aspects of divergent thinking supported by semantic accessibility and category-based search, but may have difficulty anticipating originality, which may depend more strongly on remote association and representational transformation. The study contributes to research on creative metacognition by showing that metacognitive prediction accuracy in divergent thinking is dimension-specific rather than uniformly accurate or inaccurate.

artigos.titulo: Contralateral delay activity during dynamic spatial updates in working memory
artigos.autores: Chernik C, van den Berg R, Lundqvist M
artigos.destaque: The control task suggested this was partially but not fully explained by visual attention demands. Thus, the spatial location of activity related to both attention and WM was updated to meet behavioral demands as the spatial location of remembered objects changed.

resumo.texto: Working memory (WM) enables us to maintain and directly manipulate mental representations, yet we know little about the neural implementation of this privileged online format. We recorded electroencephalography data as human subjects engaged in a task requiring continuous updates to the locations of objects retained in WM as well as in a visually identical task with WM demands removed. Analysis of neural data suggested WM-related contralateral delay activity reversed polarity as objects held in WM moved to the opposite hemifield. The control task suggested this was partially but not fully explained by visual attention demands. Thus, the spatial location of activity related to both attention and WM was updated to meet behavioral demands as the spatial location of remembered objects changed.

artigos.titulo: Challenges in obese liver transplant recipients
artigos.autores: Surendran S, Bharathan VK, Varghese CT
artigos.destaque: Individualized recipient assessment, coordinated perioperative optimization, and long-term metabolic surveillance are essential to improve outcomes. Future research should refine obesity assessment beyond BMI and clarify the optimal integration of pharmacologic and surgical weight-loss strategies in liver transplantation candidates before and after transplantation.

resumo.texto: The global obesity epidemic has significantly altered the epidemiology of chronic liver disease and liver transplantation, with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis emerging as a rapidly increasing indication for liver transplantation worldwide. Obesity in liver transplantation candidates is frequently accompanied by sarcopenia, frailty, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic comorbidities, creating complex perioperative and long-term management challenges. This review summarizes contemporary evidence regarding assessment, pretransplant preparation, perioperative management, and long-term outcomes of obese liver transplant recipients, while highlighting evolving therapeutic strategies and unresolved clinical questions.

Recent literature emphasizes that BMI alone inadequately characterizes obesity in cirrhosis, with body composition, sarcopenic obesity, visceral adiposity, and frailty emerging as important prognostic factors. Structured prehabilitation, lifestyle modification, incretin-based pharmacotherapy, and selective metabolic bariatric surgery have shown promising results in carefully selected patients. Although obesity increases perioperative complexity and postoperative complications, carefully selected obese recipients can achieve graft and patient survival comparable to nonobese recipients.

Obesity should not be considered a contraindication to liver transplantation. Individualized recipient assessment, coordinated perioperative optimization, and long-term metabolic surveillance are essential to improve outcomes. Future research should refine obesity assessment beyond BMI and clarify the optimal integration of pharmacologic and surgical weight-loss strategies in liver transplantation candidates before and after transplantation.

artigos.titulo: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery for Treatment of Obesity and Related Diseases
artigos.autores: Wilson RL, McClinton A
artigos.destaque: Careful preoperative planning, multidisciplinary evaluation, and proper procedure selection are essential for optimal outcomes. Advances in laparoscopic and robotic techniques, along with adherence to sound surgical principles, help minimize complications and improve patient safety and long-term success.

resumo.texto: Metabolic surgery has emerged as the most effective long-term treatment for obesity, a global health epidemic associated with serious conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, and sleep apnea. Updated 2022 guidelines have expanded eligibility, allowing more patients to benefit from surgical intervention. Modern procedures-including sleeve gastrectomy, SADI-S, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, and duodenal switch-are now safer, with low morbidity and mortality rates. Careful preoperative planning, multidisciplinary evaluation, and proper procedure selection are essential for optimal outcomes. Advances in laparoscopic and robotic techniques, along with adherence to sound surgical principles, help minimize complications and improve patient safety and long-term success.

artigos.titulo: Strategies for Managing Obesity and Cardiometabolic Risk in Young Children: Current Evidence and Future Directions
artigos.autores: Salama M, Kumar S
artigos.destaque: Bariatric surgery provides durable weight loss and cardiometabolic benefit and adolescents with severe obesity, though data and younger children are sparse. Available interventions may improve cardiometabolic risk profiles when appropriately applied early in life, but high-quality long-term data and preadolescent children are needed.

resumo.texto: Early-onset obesity is associated with adverse cardiometabolic risk factors and early vascular changes linked to atherosclerosis, yet evidence-based treatment options for young children remain limited. The purpose of the review is to examine current evidence for lifestyle, pharmacologic, and surgical interventions for obesity management in preadolescent children, with emphasis on cardiometabolic and atherosclerotic risk.

Lifestyle and familybased behavioral interventions remain first line therapy but often produce modest and variable weight reduction. Pharmacologic options for children younger than 12 years are limited, emerging data suggest selected agents, including topiramate, lisdexamfetamine, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and metformin can improve weight status and cardiometabolic risk factors in carefully selected patients. Bariatric surgery provides durable weight loss and cardiometabolic benefit and adolescents with severe obesity, though data and younger children are sparse. Available interventions may improve cardiometabolic risk profiles when appropriately applied early in life, but high-quality long-term data and preadolescent children are needed.

artigos.titulo: Midlife time-restricted feeding preserves skeletal muscle insulin responsiveness and function during aging
artigos.autores: Ben-David R, Sarvin N, Carmeli E et al.
artigos.destaque: These physiological benefits were accompanied by greater membrane abundance of selected components of the insulin receptor-plakoglobin-DGC signaling assembly and enhanced postprandial AKT signaling. The data reveal an age-sensitive response to nutritional timing but do not establish a causal connection between preservation of this assembly and the physiological improvements.

resumo.texto: Primary sarcopenia, the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function during aging, is partly driven by anabolic resistance, a reduced ability of aged muscle to activate protein synthesis in response to nutrients and hormones. We compared 12-wk time-restricted feeding (TRF) and alternate-day fasting (ADF) interventions initiated at 3, 12, 15, or 18 mo of age in male C57BL/6J mice (analyzed at 6, 15, 18, or 21 mo, respectively). The effects of intermittent fasting on skeletal muscle were strongly age-dependent. Midlife (15 mo of age) TRF preserved lean mass, improved glucose tolerance, and increased insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in isolated muscle, whereas ADF induced broader metabolic remodeling but was associated with lean-tissue loss when initiated later in life. Muscle aging was accompanied by reduced membrane abundance of insulin receptor-plakoglobin-dystrophin glycoprotein complex (DGC) signaling assembly. However, midlife TRF was associated with greater abundance of these protein modules and enhanced postprandial AKT signaling. These findings identify midlife as a responsive window for nutritional timing interventions and link improved muscle insulin responsiveness and maintenance with diet-associated differences in sarcolemmal protein abundance and organization, although targeted perturbation studies are required to establish causality.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Midlife time-restricted feeding preserved lean mass, muscle performance, glucose tolerance, and insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in male mice. These physiological benefits were accompanied by greater membrane abundance of selected components of the insulin receptor-plakoglobin-DGC signaling assembly and enhanced postprandial AKT signaling. The data reveal an age-sensitive response to nutritional timing but do not establish a causal connection between preservation of this assembly and the physiological improvements.

artigos.titulo: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Risk of Arrhythmias: A Network Meta-Analysis
artigos.autores: Barbosa LM, Rodrigues Oliveira VM, Ruelas MG et al.
artigos.destaque: Among GLP-1 RAs and co-agonists, subcutaneous semaglutide is highlighted as the most effective intervention for reducing the risk of AF. Further studies focusing on arrhythmic outcomes are needed to confirm these findings.

resumo.texto: Arrhythmias are often associated with comorbidities such as diabetes and obesity, which significantly influence their onset and progression. In this context, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have garnered attention for their potential benefits, with emerging evidence indicating that GLP-1 receptor activation might offer antiarrhythmic effects.
This study aimed to evaluate the impact of all GLP-1 RAs and co-agonists on the incidence of new-onset arrhythmias, particularly atrial fibrillation (AF).

A comprehensive search of databases was conducted from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) focusing on patients with diabetes or obesity receiving GLP-1 RAs or co-agonists. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. Interventions were ranked using the p-score cumulative rank, ranging from 0 (worst) to 1 (best).

A total of 94 RCTs involving 155,989 patients were included, comparing 12 GLP-1 RAs and co-agonists. Subcutaneous semaglutide emerged as the most effective intervention, significantly reducing AF incidence compared with placebo (RR 0.82; 95% CI: 0.68 to 0.99), and compared with tirzepatide (RR 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37 to 0.88). In contrast, dulaglutide was associated with an increased risk of AF, while lixisenatide was associated with a decreased risk in atrioventricular blocks. For AF, semaglutide presented a p-score of 0.7885, while tirzepatide and dulaglutide scored 0.1830 and 0.1750, respectively.

Among GLP-1 RAs and co-agonists, subcutaneous semaglutide is highlighted as the most effective intervention for reducing the risk of AF. Further studies focusing on arrhythmic outcomes are needed to confirm these findings.

artigos.titulo: GLP-1 receptor agonist-associated weight loss in breast cancer patients receiving concurrent endocrine therapy: a retrospective cohort analysis
artigos.autores: Cronin KM, Tiersten A
artigos.destaque: GLP-1 RAs produce statistically significant but substantially attenuated weight loss in breast cancer patients on concurrent endocrine therapy. GLP-1 agent selection significantly influences outcomes. Given emerging evidence of oncologic benefit, prospective trials are needed.

resumo.texto: Endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer is associated with adverse metabolic effects - including increased fat mass, decreased lean muscle mass, and insulin resistance - that may attenuate the efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs). This study evaluated GLP-1 RA-associated weight loss outcomes in breast cancer patients receiving concurrent endocrine therapy.

We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 269 breast cancer patients at a single academic center receiving concurrent GLP-1 RA and adjuvant endocrine therapy. GLP-1 RA and endocrine therapy data were obtained from electronic medication reconciliation lists and pharmacy dispense reports. Patients were required to have initiated GLP-1 therapy during the study period and to have received concurrent GLP-1 RA and endocrine therapy for at least one year. The primary outcome was percentage weight change from GLP-1 initiation to 12 months (± 2 months). Secondary outcomes included proportions achieving ≥ 5%, ≥ 10%, and ≥ 15% weight loss.

Mean one-year percentage weight loss was - 4.5% (95% CI: -6.0% to - 3.0%; -3.9 kg; 95% CI: -4.96 to - 2.93 kg), significantly below the 10-20% observed in postmenopausal subgroups of GLP-1 randomized trials (all p < 0.001). Only 21.3% achieved ≥ 10% and 10.4% achieved ≥ 15% weight loss. Weight loss differed significantly by GLP-1 agent (p = 0.003); semaglutide (- 5.8%) and tirzepatide (- 4.7%) outperformed dulaglutide (+ 0.1%), which is approved for type 2 diabetes only. Higher baseline weight was associated with greater absolute loss (r = - 0.19, p = 0.002), though percentage weight loss did not differ significantly by baseline BMI category (p = 0.303). PR-negative patients lost more than PR-positive patients (- 8.2% vs. -4.2%; p = 0.021, d = 0.46). Type 2 diabetes was present in 70.6% of patients; T2DM status was not significantly associated with weight loss on t-test (p = 0.288), though patients without T2DM were numerically more likely to achieve ≥ 15% loss (21.5% vs. 5.8%).

GLP-1 RAs produce statistically significant but substantially attenuated weight loss in breast cancer patients on concurrent endocrine therapy. GLP-1 agent selection significantly influences outcomes. Given emerging evidence of oncologic benefit, prospective trials are needed.

artigos.titulo: Characteristics and Treatment Utilisation Patterns of Individuals Using Tirzepatide for Type 2 Diabetes in Germany
artigos.autores: Füchtenbusch M, Kraus M, Heitmann E et al.
artigos.destaque: This first comprehensive real-world study of tirzepatide use in Germany showed tirzepatide initiation primarily after GLP-1 RA and/or insulin therapy. Most individuals remained on 5.0 mg, with a notable proportion escalating to 10.0 mg. Cohort characteristics were generally similar to those in the SURPASS trials, supporting the relevance of trial findings to clinical practice.

resumo.texto: This study describes real-world characteristics and utilisation patterns of tirzepatide among adults with type 2 diabetes in German office-based practice.

This retrospective observational study analysed data from the CompuGroup Medical Healthcare Database. Cohort 1 initiated tirzepatide between 1 December 2023 and 31 March 2024 and cohort 2 between 1 July and 30 September 2024. A subgroup of cohort 1 with ≥ 6 months' follow-up data and uninterrupted tirzepatide use (cohort 1a) was also analysed. Descriptive statistics summarised baseline characteristics, prior therapy, and dosing patterns.

Cohort 1 included 1223 individuals and cohort 2 included 2300; mean (± standard deviation) age was 59 ± 12 and 60 ± 12 years, respectively, and approximately 54% were male. Comorbidities, especially hypertension and dyslipidaemia, were frequent. Most individuals had prior insulin and/or glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) treatment (cohort 1, 72.1%; cohort 2, 59.6%). A total of 458 individuals had 6 months' follow-up (cohort 1a). The most common starting dose was 2.5 mg (71.2%). Use of higher doses gradually increased over time, with 5.0 mg becoming the most prevalent; at 6 months, 35.9% of individuals received 5.0 mg and 18.6% received 10.0 mg.

This first comprehensive real-world study of tirzepatide use in Germany showed tirzepatide initiation primarily after GLP-1 RA and/or insulin therapy. Most individuals remained on 5.0 mg, with a notable proportion escalating to 10.0 mg. Cohort characteristics were generally similar to those in the SURPASS trials, supporting the relevance of trial findings to clinical practice.

artigos.titulo: Intensive Care Unit Delirium in Critically Ill Adults: Evidence-Based Approaches to Prevention and Management
artigos.revista: Crit Care Nurs Clin North Am
artigos.autores: Ahrens E, Pandharipande PP, Cordoza ML
artigos.destaque: Emphasis is placed on validated screening tools, light sedation practices, sleep promotion, and multicomponent care bundles. Empowering nurses with knowledge, autonomy, and interdisciplinary collaboration is essential to improving delirium-related outcomes.

resumo.texto: Intensive care unit (ICU) delirium affects up to 80% of critically ill adults and is associated with increased mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and long-term cognitive decline. Despite strong evidence supporting strategies for delirium management, adherence to best practices is inconsistent, and traditional practices often override their implementation. This clinical review highlights opportunities for deimplementation of outdated practices and adoption of evidence-based strategies to detect, prevent, and manage ICU delirium. Emphasis is placed on validated screening tools, light sedation practices, sleep promotion, and multicomponent care bundles. Empowering nurses with knowledge, autonomy, and interdisciplinary collaboration is essential to improving delirium-related outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Intensive Care Unit Liberation: Transforming Critical Care Through the ABCDEF Bundle
artigos.revista: Crit Care Nurs Clin North Am
artigos.autores: Gregory S, Ratliff E
artigos.destaque: Critical care nurses play a central role in driving bundle adherence. Successful implementation requires interdisciplinary teamwork, leadership support, education, and integration into practice standards.

resumo.texto: This article highlights the shift from traditional intensive care unit practices, including deep sedation, immobility, and restricted visitation, to evidence-based, patient-centered care. These outdated methods, once considered protective, are now known to increase delirium, muscle weakness, cognitive decline, and health care costs. Implementing the ABCDEF bundle (eg, pain management, awakening and breathing trials, sedation choice, delirium management, early mobility, and family engagement) is a proven evidence-based framework that improves patient outcomes. Critical care nurses play a central role in driving bundle adherence. Successful implementation requires interdisciplinary teamwork, leadership support, education, and integration into practice standards.

artigos.titulo: How adverse childhood experiences affect the association between chronic condition progression and subjective or objective cognitive function among rural older adults?
artigos.autores: Luo J, Zhang Y, Zhou C
artigos.destaque: ACEs amplified this association among older adults with multimorbidity, particularly among males. Incorporating subjective cognitive screening into chronic disease management, with attention to childhood adversity, may help identify older adults earlier in rural settings.

resumo.texto: Objectives: Little is known regarding the association between chronic condition progression and subjective or objective cognitive function, and whether adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) moderate this association. This study aimed to explore the association between chronic condition progression and subjective or objective cognition, and to determine whether ACEs moderate this relationship.Methods: This study used two waves of follow-up surveys (2020 and 2022) conducted by the Shandong Rural Elderly Health Cohort (SREHC), including 2,607 older adults aged 60 years or above. Chronic condition progression was defined as the change in the number of 12 chronic conditions across waves. Subjective and objective cognitive function were measured by the Subjective Cognitive Decline Questionnaire 9 and Mini Mental State Examination, respectively. ACEs were measured by seven items of childhood adversity before age 17. Generalized linear mixed models with random intercepts were used to estimate our hypothetical models.Results: Chronic condition progression was significantly associated with subjective cognitive decline (β ranging from 0.428 to 0.869, all p < .05) but not with objective cognitive function. The moderating effect of ACEs was only on subjective, but not objective, cognitive function. ACEs exacerbated this association among rural older adults with multimorbidity, whether unchanged (unchanged multimorbidity × ACEs: β = 0.406, p = .026) or progressive (no chronic condition to emerging multimorbidity × ACEs: β = 0.990, p = .023; one chronic condition to emerging multimorbidity × ACEs: β = 0.456, p = .043; progressive multimorbidity × ACEs: β = 0.696, p = .001). This moderating effect was significant among males but not females.Conclusions: Chronic condition progression was associated with subjective cognitive decline but not objective cognitive function. ACEs amplified this association among older adults with multimorbidity, particularly among males. Incorporating subjective cognitive screening into chronic disease management, with attention to childhood adversity, may help identify older adults earlier in rural settings.

artigos.titulo: The memory of the tumor microenvironment: epigenetic scarring and the hysteretic logic of therapeutic relapse
artigos.autores: Kokkanti RR, Biswas S, Parida N et al.
artigos.destaque: Finally, we discuss the experimental and clinical strategies required to identify memory-rich tumors, develop biomarkers of historical imprinting, and design memory-aware therapeutic interventions. By integrating diverse forms of adaptive persistence within a unified history-dependent framework, TME memory provides a conceptual foundation for investigating tumor evolution, therapeutic resistance, and future precision oncology strategies.

resumo.texto: Tumor progression and therapeutic failure are classically interpreted through the lenses of genetic evolution and ongoing signaling dynamics. However, increasing evidence suggests that tumors are also shaped by durable imprints of prior microenvironmental exposures. These prior exposures can leave persistent epigenetic and structural imprints that progressively stabilize adaptive cellular states, allowing transient responses to become durable regulatory programs. Chronic inflammation, metabolic stress, therapeutic pressure, and extracellular matrix remodeling induce persistent molecular states across cancer cells and stromal compartments, generating history-dependent phenotypes that influence future biological responses. Building on these observations, we propose that these adaptive processes collectively constitute a distributed tumor microenvironment (TME) memory encoded across cancer cells, fibroblasts, immune cells, endothelial cells, and the extracellular matrix (ECM), rather than representing isolated mechanisms of adaptation. We examine how TME memory contributes to therapy resistance, immune dysfunction, cancer-cell dormancy, minimal residual disease, and tumor recurrence, and discuss the molecular mechanisms underlying memory encoding, persistence, and recall. Finally, we discuss the experimental and clinical strategies required to identify memory-rich tumors, develop biomarkers of historical imprinting, and design memory-aware therapeutic interventions.
