By integrating diverse forms of adaptive persistence within a unified history-dependent framework, TME memory provides a conceptual foundation for investigating tumor evolution, therapeutic resistance, and future precision oncology strategies.

artigos.titulo: Mesenchymal stromal cell-based therapies for obesity-associated metabolic complications: Mechanistic insights, translational evidence, and future perspectives
artigos.autores: Zeng X, Cao J, Xin W et al.
artigos.destaque: In this review, we summarize current mechanistic insights, preclinical findings, and clinical data on MSC-based interventions for obesity-associated metabolic disorders, while critically discussing key biological, manufacturing, and regulatory challenges. Finally, we define the prerequisites for rational translation - standardized potency assays, obesity-specific early-phase trials with active comparators, objective body-composition endpoints, hemocompatibility testing, and long-term surveillance.

resumo.texto: Obesity is a major global health challenge and a key driver of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic syndrome. Although pharmacological therapies and bariatric surgery have improved both short- and long-term outcomes, with GLP-1 receptor agonists now demonstrating cardiovascular and heart-failure benefits beyond weight reduction (SELECT, SUMMIT), durable and broadly applicable treatments for all patients remain limited. In this context, mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-based therapies, particularly adipose-derived MSCs, have gained increasing attention due to their immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory properties demonstrated in preclinical models. Experimental studies suggest that MSCs influence adipose tissue remodeling, immune cell polarization, insulin sensitivity, and energy homeostasis predominantly through paracrine mechanisms, including the release of cytokines and extracellular vesicles, rather than long-term engraftment or differentiation. However, accumulating evidence indicates that obesity itself profoundly impairs endogenous MSC function through oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and epigenetic alterations, raising important concerns regarding the feasibility of autologous MSC-based approaches in obese individuals. Critically, no randomized controlled trial has evaluated MSC therapy for obesity with weight loss, body composition, or obesity-related clinical outcomes as primary endpoints; the available human evidence addresses glycemic control in type 2 diabetes and metabolic complications. In this review, we summarize current mechanistic insights, preclinical findings, and clinical data on MSC-based interventions for obesity-associated metabolic disorders, while critically discussing key biological, manufacturing, and regulatory challenges. Finally, we define the prerequisites for rational translation - standardized potency assays, obesity-specific early-phase trials with active comparators, objective body-composition endpoints, hemocompatibility testing, and long-term surveillance.

artigos.titulo: Identification of TAS2R-targeting bioactive compounds against metabolic decline: A novel ex vivo methodology based on enteroendocrine and inflammatory readouts
artigos.autores: Vilalta A, Descamps-Solà M, Feliu-Villarò F et al.
artigos.destaque: This study establishes an ex vivo platform for profiling intestinal TAS2R agonists, revealing subtype-specific effects on enterohormonal and inflammatory responses. This framework supports the identification of receptor-selective agonists to modulate gut homeostasis in obesity and ageing.

resumo.texto: Obesity and ageing disrupt intestinal homeostasis. Bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) regulate gut hormone secretion and inflammatory responses. This study aimed to identify intestinal TAS2Rs most affected by obesity and ageing and characterise their receptor-specific responses in ex vivo intestinal explants from Wistar rats. We have integrated previously published transcriptomic and metabolic datasets to identify intestinal TAS2R subtypes differentially modulated by obesity, ageing, and the combination of obesity and ageing. Receptor selection was based on associations with inflammatory, metabolic and enteroendocrine readouts. Subtype-selective agonists were identified through ligand affinity databases and literature screening, and their functional effects were characterised ex vivo in jejunal and ileal explants from Wistar rats. Enterohormone assays revealed receptor- and dose-dependent effects on GLP-1, GIP and CCK secretion, including both stimulatory and inhibitory responses. In Dextran Sulphate Sodium (DSS)-inflamed tissue, bitter agonists exerted divergent immunomodulatory effects on TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-18. Overall, rTas2r108, rTas2r119, rTas2r140 and rTas2r143, activated by amarogentin, costunolide, resveratrol and ethylpyrazine, respectively, emerged as functionally relevant targets. This study establishes an ex vivo platform for profiling intestinal TAS2R agonists, revealing subtype-specific effects on enterohormonal and inflammatory responses. This framework supports the identification of receptor-selective agonists to modulate gut homeostasis in obesity and ageing.

artigos.titulo: TREM2/IGF-1 signaling axis-induced microglial senescence underlies benzo[a]pyrene-associated Parkinson's disease-like lesions
artigos.autores: Wu Y, Shi Y, Xiao F et al.
artigos.destaque: Subsequent experiments further validated that insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), as a direct downstream effector regulated by TREM2, is functionally required for B[a]P-triggered microglial senescence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that B[a]P exposure can induce PD-like lesions and microglial senescence, and which is primarily mediated via the TREM2/IGF-1 signaling axis.

resumo.texto: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder worldwide. Accumulating evidence has linked environmental polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), with benzo[a]pyrene (B[a]P) as a representative ubiquitous member, to elevated PD risk and disease pathogenesis. The present study aimed to investigate whether B[a]P can trigger typical PD-like lesions in mice, and further dissects the functional role of microglial senescence as well as its underlying regulatory mechanism, using complementary systems in vivo mouse model and in vitro BV2 microglia cell. Behavioral assessments revealed that B[a]P exposure induced significant, dose-dependent impairments in motor coordination and cognitive function compared with the control group. Moreover, the degree of functional impairments measured in the high-dose B[a]P group was comparable to that observed in the MPTP positive-control group. Following B[a]P treatment, brain-resident microglia cells exhibited signs of cell senescence, as evidenced by typical ultrastructural alterations, increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) activity, and elevated expression of the core senescence markers p16, p21, and p53 proteins. Consistent with these in vivo observations, B[a]P was confirmed to also induce cell cycle arrest in cultured BV2 microglia cells. This pro-senescent effect was significnatly attenuated by Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) overexpression, whereas it was markedly exacerbated following TREM2 knockout. Subsequent experiments further validated that insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), as a direct downstream effector regulated by TREM2, is functionally required for B[a]P-triggered microglial senescence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that B[a]P exposure can induce PD-like lesions and microglial senescence, and which is primarily mediated via the TREM2/IGF-1 signaling axis.

artigos.titulo: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
artigos.destaque: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia. Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect. The discovery suggests that genetics could help explain why some people benefit while others do not.

artigos.titulo: Research progress in neural regulatory mechanisms and targeted therapy of obesity (Review)
artigos.autores: Kang D, Li X, Zhang Y et al.
artigos.destaque: The present study further addresses multimodal combined interventions and balanced pros‑and‑cons of neuromodulation techniques. This multi‑system overview provided theoretical support for developing novel precision anti‑obesity strategies.

resumo.texto: Obesity is a multifactorial chronic metabolic disease driven by disrupted energy homeostasis and excessive adipose tissue (AT) deposition under genetic, environmental and central neural regulation. Sustained energy surplus triggers AT hypertrophy, endocrine dysfunction and low‑grade inflammation, elevating risks of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular diseases and multiple cancers while impairing physical‑mental well‑being. Hypothalamic central neural circuits integrate peripheral metabolic signals to govern feeding and systemic energy balance and serve as core pathological drivers of obesity. Conventional interventions including bariatric surgery, calorie restriction and exercise yield only transient weight loss with poor long‑term outcomes, as they fail to reverse obesity‑related neural‑circuit dysfunction and thus produce high weight‑regain rates. Translational obstacles remain for neuromodulatory therapies, including poorly defined cell‑type‑specific neural control and limited blood‑brain barrier penetration of candidate agents. The present review systematically outlined obesity‑associated hierarchical neural networks centered on hypothalamic arcuate nucleus pro‑opiomelanocortin and agouti‑related peptide neurons and the leptin‑melanocortin axis. The present review summarized recent progress in hypothalamic neurons, key neuro‑transmitters and downstream cascades controlling energy metabolism; characterized gut‑microbiota‑vagus‑nerve gut‑brain signaling and dual appetite‑regulatory roles of short‑chain fatty acids; and delineated pathological links between gut dysbiosis and hypothalamic pro‑opiomelanocortin neuronal injury, distinguishing confirmed mechanisms from unvalidated hypotheses. Three neural‑targeted anti‑obesity modalities (GLP‑1R agonists, MC4R agonists and NMU‑R2 small‑molecule candidates) are comparatively assessed, covering preclinical evidence for NMU‑R2, adverse‑effect profiles, target populations and animal‑to‑human translational gaps. The present study further addresses multimodal combined interventions and balanced pros‑and‑cons of neuromodulation techniques. This multi‑system overview provided theoretical support for developing novel precision anti‑obesity strategies.

artigos.titulo: Taiwan GEST-TASL-TMASO Joint Position Statement in Managing Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Obesity
artigos.autores: Cheng PN, Lu CW, Lin CL et al.
artigos.destaque: Risk stratification using noninvasive tools such as Fibrosis-4 and vibration-controlled transient elastography effectively guides referral and management. A multidisciplinary, precision-based approach, integrating lifestyle modification, pharmacotherapy, surgical options, and risk stratification, is essential for effective MASLD management in patients with obesity, while research into artificial intelligence-driven biomarkers, gut microbiota modulation, and genetic factors represents future directions.

resumo.texto: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and obesity share common pathogenesis and are increasingly relevant in clinical care. This joint statement addresses the need for comprehensive guidance in Taiwan for MASLD patients with obesity. The Gastroenterological Society of Taiwan, the Taiwan Association for the Study of the Liver, and the Taiwan Medical Association for the Study of Obesity conducted an evidence-based review, integrating epidemiological data, clinical trial outcomes, and expert consensus to develop position statements covering diagnosis, disease burden, pathogenesis, surveillance, and therapeutic strategies. MASLD prevalence in Taiwanese adults is 30%-45%, reaching 60%-70% in individuals with obesity, with similar high prevalence in children and adolescents. Obesity accelerates hepatic and extrahepatic disease progression, including cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and cardiovascular complications. Lifestyle interventions, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, resmetirom, and bariatric surgery demonstrate efficacy in improving hepatic and metabolic outcomes. Risk stratification using noninvasive tools such as Fibrosis-4 and vibration-controlled transient elastography effectively guides referral and management. A multidisciplinary, precision-based approach, integrating lifestyle modification, pharmacotherapy, surgical options, and risk stratification, is essential for effective MASLD management in patients with obesity, while research into artificial intelligence-driven biomarkers, gut microbiota modulation, and genetic factors represents future directions.

artigos.titulo: The Dual Reality of Psychological Outcomes and Mental Health Trajectories After Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: A Scoping Review of Desirable and Less Desirable Experiences
artigos.autores: El Ansari W, El-Ansari K, Hany M
artigos.destaque: The psychological aftermath of MBS is a dual reality rather than a uniformly positive or negative one. Reframing psychological success as the net balance between the two trajectories supports biopsychosocial, multidisciplinary, long-term care, and points to a research agenda built on within-cohort, dual-outcome longitudinal designs.

resumo.texto: To map, within a single integrated framework, the full spectrum of desirable ('feel-good') and less desirable ('feel-bad') psychological outcomes and mental health trajectories after metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS), and to identify the knowledge gaps that emerge only when both sides are viewed together.

Across 251 included studies, the desirable arm comprised four interconnected domains: improved mental health (depression, anxiety, mood, eating disorders); enhanced physical-health domains supporting psychological well-being; improved body image, self-esteem and relational functioning; and gains in occupational, educational and economic participation. The less desirable arm comprised three themes: a spectrum of adverse outcomes; the negotiation of self and existential tensions; and a 'lonely struggle' against insufficient support, encompassing the most serious outcomes of suicide, self-harm and alcohol-use disorder. Thirty-seven studies contributed to both arms, and benefits and burdens frequently coexisted within the same patient over time. Recent studies show that these gains are smaller and less durable than group averages suggest. Improvements in depressive and anxiety symptoms are largest in the first year and smaller thereafter or partly reversed; symptoms persist or worsen in a subset of patients; relationship, work, body-image, and weight-stigma outcomes run in both directions; and the benefits differ by sex, ethnicity, age group, and pre-surgical psychiatric history. The psychological aftermath of MBS is a dual reality rather than a uniformly positive or negative one. Reframing psychological success as the net balance between the two trajectories supports biopsychosocial, multidisciplinary, long-term care, and points to a research agenda built on within-cohort, dual-outcome longitudinal designs.

artigos.titulo: Bioactive shape-memory biodegradable biliary stent functionalized with dHAM-Curcumin for improved biliary repair and microenvironment modulation
artigos.autores: Dai C, Zhang H, Bai Y et al.
artigos.destaque: The PCT/BaSO4@dHAM-Cur composite demonstrated local anti-inflammatory and anti-adhesion effects in preclinical models, along with favorable biocompatibility and anti-restenotic potential. This system holds promise as a therapeutic platform for the clinical management of biliodigestive anastomoses.

resumo.texto: Anastomotic stricture after biliodigestive reconstruction remains a clinical challenge leading to recurrent cholangitis, jaundice, and secondary biliary cirrhosis. Conventional plastic stents provide temporary support but are prone to biofilm formation and biliary sludge accumulation and require secondary removal procedures. There is a need for biodegradable biliary stents that provide sufficient mechanical support while actively modulating the local microenvironment. A biodegradable shape-memory biliary stent composed of a poly(CL-co-TOSUO)/BaSO4 (PCT/BaSO4) composite core coated with a decellularized human amniotic membrane-curcumin (dHAM-Cur) hydrogel was developed. In vivo performance was assessed in rat subcutaneous and duodenal implantation models and in a rabbit orthotopic common bile duct stenting model. Gut microbiota and bile metabolomic changes were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS). The PCT/BaSO4 stent exhibited suitable mechanical properties, radiopacity, and shape memory functionality, with a degradation profile that matched the expected biliary healing period. The dHAM-Cur coating increased surface hydrophilicity and supported sustained curcumin release. The functionalized stent reduced inflammatory cell infiltration, fibrous capsule formation, and bile duct fibrosis, and preserved biliary patency compared with plastic and PCL/BaSO4 controls in vivo. Multi-omics analyses suggested that the stent subtly reshaped gut microbial composition and modulated bile acid-related metabolic pathways. The PCT/BaSO4@dHAM-Cur composite demonstrated local anti-inflammatory and anti-adhesion effects in preclinical models, along with favorable biocompatibility and anti-restenotic potential. This system holds promise as a therapeutic platform for the clinical management of biliodigestive anastomoses.

artigos.titulo: Integrated assessment of driving performance, eye movements, and cognitive function in obstructive sleep apnea: A pilot study
artigos.autores: Tateishi T, Tamaoka M, Takagi S et al.
artigos.destaque: Basic psychomotor speed was associated with OSA severity and improved following CPAP therapy, suggesting within-subject improvement of vigilance-dependent processes. In contrast, integrated oculomotor and executive function measures were more closely linked to complex driving performance, indicating that multidomain assessment may better characterize driving-related impairment in OSA. These findings provide preliminary evidence to guide future hypothesis-driven studies.

resumo.texto: Motor vehicle accident (MVA) risk is greater in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), yet the functional domains most closely linked to driving-related impairment remain incompletely understood. This exploratory pilot study aimed to perform an integrated assessment of driving performance, eye movements, vigilance, and cognitive function in OSA and to examine their relationships with disease severity and treatment response.

Adult drivers with suspected OSA underwent assessment using a driving simulator, Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT), eye-tracking, and the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB). Participants with moderate-to-severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥20) who initiated continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy underwent re-evaluation after 6-12 months.

At baseline, single-task reaction time in the driving simulator was positively correlated with apnea severity. In contrast, response accuracy under multitask plus steering conditions was associated with nocturnal hypoxemia (T90), suggesting differential contributions of apnea frequency and oxygen desaturation to driving performance. Eye-tracking parameters, including saccade amplitude and fixation duration, were significantly correlated with both driving performance and spatial working memory error scores. Following CPAP therapy, simple reaction times improved in both the driving simulator and PVT, whereas changes in multitasking performance and CANTAB measures were not statistically significant.

Basic psychomotor speed was associated with OSA severity and improved following CPAP therapy, suggesting within-subject improvement of vigilance-dependent processes. In contrast, integrated oculomotor and executive function measures were more closely linked to complex driving performance, indicating that multidomain assessment may better characterize driving-related impairment in OSA. These findings provide preliminary evidence to guide future hypothesis-driven studies.

artigos.titulo: Overcoming the efficacy-safety dilemma of cytokine therapy for tissue-resident memory T cells in cancer immunotherapy: Intrinsic sensitization and extrinsic optimization
artigos.autores: Xiao Y, Li ZZ, Sun ZJ
artigos.destaque: Complementing this, extrinsic optimization minimizes risks through targeted delivery systems, tumor microenvironment (TME) modulation for endogenous release, rational cytokine combination, and protein engineering coupled with rational selection. Collectively, this roadmap outlines how to harness cytokine networks safely and effectively, enabling precision TRM-based antitumor immunotherapy.

resumo.texto: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells are important contributors to immune checkpoint blockade therapy response in several cancers, yet their therapeutic potential remains underutilized. The cytokine-mediated enhancement of TRM cells represents a promising strategy to amplify antitumor immunity. However, clinical translation is hindered by an efficacy-safety dilemma. Potent cytokines such as IL-12 and IL-15 induce severe systemic toxicity; other potent cytokines such as TGF-β and IL-1 carry inherent immunosuppressive risks. To overcome this barrier, a dual-strategy framework is proposed. Intrinsic sensitization involves the use of multidimensional regulatory networks such as those involving transcription factors, metabolic pathways, hypoxia signaling, and host aging to enhance TRM responsiveness to cytokines rather than increasing the dose. Complementing this, extrinsic optimization minimizes risks through targeted delivery systems, tumor microenvironment (TME) modulation for endogenous release, rational cytokine combination, and protein engineering coupled with rational selection. Collectively, this roadmap outlines how to harness cytokine networks safely and effectively, enabling precision TRM-based antitumor immunotherapy.

artigos.titulo: Protopanaxadiol-type ginsenosides ameliorate PTSD-like memory impairment and neuroinflammation in rats via suppression of TLR4/NF-κB signaling
artigos.autores: Lee B
artigos.destaque: By contrast, PT treatment did not produce meaningful changes in memory performance or inflammatory markers. These findings suggest that the beneficial effects of PD are associated with anti-inflammatory activity that may involve modulation of the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway.

resumo.texto: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a serious psychiatric condition that develops after exposure to intense or traumatic stress. Ginsenosides, the primary bioactive compounds of ginseng, have been reported to enhance cognitive performance. Protopanaxadiol (PD) and protopanaxatriol (PT) are two major classes of triterpenoid saponins. In the present study, a PTSD-like rat model was established using the single prolonged stress (SPS) paradigm, and the effects of PD and PT on memory dysfunction were evaluated. After SPS exposure, male rats received daily intraperitoneal administration of PD (10 or 20 mg/kg) or PT (10 and 20 mg/kg) for 14 days. PD treatment significantly improved both spatial and cognitive memory compared with PT treatment. PD also suppressed the elevation of pro-inflammatory cytokines in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus, and mitigated the reduction in brain-derived neurotrophic factor mRNA expression in the hippocampus. In addition, PD attenuated the upregulation of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and nuclear factor (NF)-κB protein expression in the hippocampus. By contrast, PT treatment did not produce meaningful changes in memory performance or inflammatory markers. These findings suggest that the beneficial effects of PD are associated with anti-inflammatory activity that may involve modulation of the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway.

artigos.titulo: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
artigos.destaque: Scientists have uncovered a surprising new clue to why the Mediterranean diet is so good for the heart, brain, and healthy aging. Researchers at USC found that older adults who closely followed the diet had higher levels of two tiny proteins, humanin and SHMOOSE, produced by the mitochondria, the energy-producing structures inside cells. These proteins have been linked to protection against heart disease, Alzheimer's disease, and age-related damage.

artigos.titulo: Scientists discover a hidden switch that burns fat and blocks new fat cells
artigos.destaque: Scientists have discovered that switching off a protein called Mitch makes human cells burn more fat and prevents new fat cells from developing. The breakthrough builds on experiments in mice that showed remarkable resistance to obesity and improved muscular endurance, raising hopes for a new approach to weight-loss treatment.

artigos.titulo: Skeletal effects of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in adults with overweight or obesity: a systematic review
artigos.autores: Lai CH, Li YT, Wu TS et al.
artigos.destaque: The randomized evidence is too sparse and too clinically heterogeneous to determine the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in adults with overweight or obesity. Each agent has been evaluated in at most five small trials, most conducted in adults with type 2 diabetes rather than in adults with obesity alone. The two trials producing the largest weight loss, one of semaglutide and one of liraglutide 3.0 mg, both reported reduced lumbar spine and total hip BMD at closely similar magnitudes of weight loss, and the semaglutide trial additionally reported increased bone resorption. This convergence warrants dedicated evaluation rather than extrapolation across the drug class. Adequately powered, agent-specific trials with fracture endpoints are required.

resumo.texto: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain unclear. This systematic review of eight randomized controlled trials (n = 493) evaluating dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived bone mineral density reports findings separately for each agent, without pooling, because the trials evaluated four pharmacologically distinct agents differing markedly in weight-lowering potency. The evidence is sparse for every agent and is insufficient to establish the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in this population.

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed the randomized evidence on bone mineral density (BMD) and bone turnover markers in adults with overweight or obesity, reporting findings separately for each individual agent.

This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review (INPLASY202630076) searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (January 2015 to July 2026). Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolled adults aged ≥18 years with mean baseline body mass index (BMI) > 25 kg/m², compared a GLP-1 RA with placebo or another antidiabetic therapy for ≥12 weeks, and reported BMD assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Because the included trials evaluated pharmacologically distinct agents that differ substantially in weight-lowering potency, results were synthesized narratively and reported separately by agent; no meta-analysis was performed.

Eight RCTs (n = 493) were included. Three trials were at low risk of bias (Eriksson 2019; Hygum 2020; Hansen 2024) and five raised some concerns, principally regarding the randomization process and selective reporting; no agent is supported by more than one trial at low risk of bias. (Cai 2021 contributes two treatment arms assessed separately, giving nine comparisons in the risk-of-bias assessment.) Evidence was unevenly distributed across agents: semaglutide and dulaglutide were each evaluated in one trial, liraglutide in two, and exenatide in five. Five of the eight trials enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes, including all four that randomized an insulin comparator arm; three enrolled adults without diabetes, of which one was defined by obesity alone. By study-level mean baseline BMI, five trials lay in the obese range ( ≥ 30 kg/m²) and three in the overweight range (25 to <30 kg/m²). The single semaglutide trial (Hansen 2024; n = 64; low risk of bias), which produced the largest weight loss of any trial (estimated treatment difference [ETD] -6.8 kg vs placebo), reported reduced lumbar spine BMD (ETD - 0.018 g/cm², p = 0.007), reduced whole-body BMD (mean difference [MD] -0.02 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.03 to -0.01), and increased C-terminal telopeptide (CTX; MD 166.50 pg/mL; 95% CI 66.60 to 266.40). Liraglutide was evaluated at two doses with divergent results. At the weight-management dose of 3.0 mg daily, in the only trial conducted in adults with obesity and without diabetes (Jensen 2024; ETD - 6.7 kg vs placebo), lumbar spine BMD (MD - 0.019 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.034 to -0.004) and total hip BMD (MD - 0.013 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.024 to -0.002) were reduced. At the diabetes dose of 1.8 mg daily (Hygum 2020; -3.8 kg), no site changed materially (lumbar spine MD 0.00 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.01 to 0.01). Exenatide trials were inconsistent, ranging from 0.03 g/cm² (95% CI 0.02 to 0.03) at the lumbar spine (Renyuan 2015) to -0.04 g/cm² (95% CI - 0.15 to 0.07; Akyay 2023). Certainty of evidence was very low for every agent.

The randomized evidence is too sparse and too clinically heterogeneous to determine the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in adults with overweight or obesity. Each agent has been evaluated in at most five small trials, most conducted in adults with type 2 diabetes rather than in adults with obesity alone. The two trials producing the largest weight loss, one of semaglutide and one of liraglutide 3.0 mg, both reported reduced lumbar spine and total hip BMD at closely similar magnitudes of weight loss, and the semaglutide trial additionally reported increased bone resorption. This convergence warrants dedicated evaluation rather than extrapolation across the drug class. Adequately powered, agent-specific trials with fracture endpoints are required.
