artigos.titulo: Associations of critical consciousness and positive youth development among Taiwanese indigenous early adolescents
artigos.autores: Yang PJ, Zheng Y
artigos.destaque: Furthermore, PYD may potentially serve as a foundation for the development of critical consciousness. This study offers preliminary empirical support for a social justice-oriented extension of the PYD framework.

resumo.texto: This study investigates the longitudinal associations among components of critical consciousness (i.e., perceived inequality, egalitarian beliefs, and critical motivation) and the role of these components within the PYD framework in a sample of Indigenous early adolescents in Taiwan. Each critical consciousness component was examined in association with PYD and, secondarily, as a corroborating outcome, with internalizing symptoms. Ethnic-racial discrimination was included as a contextual variable to examine its potential adverse effects. A total of 358 adolescents (Mage = 12 years, 48% female) were followed across three waves at 6-month intervals. The results suggest that, although early components of critical consciousness may not yet show clear interrelated patterns, egalitarian beliefs, and critical motivation were associated with lower levels of internalizing symptoms. Furthermore, PYD may potentially serve as a foundation for the development of critical consciousness. This study offers preliminary empirical support for a social justice-oriented extension of the PYD framework.

artigos.titulo: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial
artigos.destaque: A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission. Researchers believe the technology could transform PTSD care and pave the way for more precise treatments for other mental health conditions.

artigos.titulo: Scientists discover a surprising double benefit of exercise for Parkinson’s
artigos.destaque: A seven-year study found that people with Parkinson’s disease who were more physically active experienced slower declines in memory, thinking, and movement abilities. Those exercising more than eight hours per week showed almost no average cognitive decline, suggesting that staying active may offer important benefits as the disease progresses.

artigos.titulo: Gut virome remodeling after fecal microbiota transplantation is associated with virus-bacteria co-variation and metabolic response in obesity and type 2 diabetes
artigos.autores: Jiang H, Peng Y, Lam B et al.
artigos.destaque: FMT-responsive viral contigs that were shared between the two FMT groups were predicted to infect Roseburia and Bifidobacterium, while contigs associated with clinical responses were predicted to infect Escherichia, Roseburia, Blautia, and Enterococcus. These findings suggest that the gut virome is a complementary ecological component associated with FMT responses and metabolic outcomes in ObT2.

resumo.texto: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) modifies gut bacterial composition and improves metabolic outcomes in subjects with obesity and type 2 diabetes (ObT2), but bacterial changes alone do not fully explain the heterogeneity in clinical response. We performed virus-like particle (VLP)-enriched metagenomic sequencing coupled with bulk-DNA metagenomic sequencing on longitudinal fecal samples from a randomized controlled FMT trial in ObT2. Using random forest classification, post-FMT virome changes showed accuracy comparable to bacteriome changes (84.8% vs 81.4%) in distinguishing LDL responders from non-responders. Donor-derived viral contig engraftment was detected in 64.7% (11/17) of recipients receiving FMT alone and 58.8% (10/17) receiving FMT with lifestyle intervention (LSI), versus 5.6% (1/18) in the sham with LSI group. FMT was associated with increased virome diversity, compositional shifts toward the donor virome, and coordinated virus-bacteria associations, with most responsive viral contigs classified as Caudoviricetes. FMT-responsive viral contigs that were shared between the two FMT groups were predicted to infect Roseburia and Bifidobacterium, while contigs associated with clinical responses were predicted to infect Escherichia, Roseburia, Blautia, and Enterococcus. These findings suggest that the gut virome is a complementary ecological component associated with FMT responses and metabolic outcomes in ObT2.

artigos.titulo: New Horizons for Incretin-Based Therapeutics
artigos.autores: Liskiewicz D, Liskiewicz A, Müller TD
artigos.destaque: Concurrently, research is heavily focused on identifying the biological drivers of weight regain, such as altered neuroregulation, metabolic adaptation, and adipose tissue remodeling. This review examines the current landscape, limitations, and emerging strategies of obesity pharmacotherapy.

resumo.texto: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies marked a major breakthrough in obesity pharmacotherapy, while subsequent advancements targeting multiple entero-pancreatic hormones now deliver weight loss previously achievable only with bariatric surgery, alongside improvements in obesity-related complications. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including reduced efficacy in diabetic populations, gastrointestinal adverse effects, and high costs that drive a real-world adherence gap. Consequently, next-generation therapies, including receptor polyagonists, oral formulations, and small-molecule incretin mimetics with optimized pharmacokinetic profiles, are being developed to enhance efficacy, tolerability, and accessibility while maintaining safety. However, weight regain after treatment cessation remains a critical hurdle. Growing evidence underscores the importance of sustained lifestyle interventions and muscle mass preservation to facilitate weight stabilization. Concurrently, research is heavily focused on identifying the biological drivers of weight regain, such as altered neuroregulation, metabolic adaptation, and adipose tissue remodeling. This review examines the current landscape, limitations, and emerging strategies of obesity pharmacotherapy.

artigos.titulo: Hyperglycemia-induced metabolic rewiring is associated with skeletal muscle loss in a fructose-streptozotocin-induced diabetic rat model
artigos.autores: Moreira-Pais A, Oliveira-Brás F, Moreira RJ et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings demonstrate an association between hyperglycemia and muscle loss, with muscle loss being associated with metabolic reprogramming toward the preferential utilization of non-glucose substrates, possibly to preserve energy homeostasis at the expense of protein maintenance.

resumo.texto: This study investigated the impact of hyperglycemia on systemic and skeletal muscle metabolite profiles.
Serum and gastrocnemius metabolites of fructose-fed, streptozotocin-injected rats (T2D) were analyzed by 1H NMR and related to markers of energy metabolism and mitochondrial remodeling.

T2D rats exhibited hyperglycemia and impaired insulin secretion without obesity or dyslipidemia. Hyperglycemia induced a generalized catabolic state, reflected by reduced body weight and relative gastrocnemius mass. T2D rats presented increased phosphorylated AMP-activated protein kinase (pAMPK) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) muscle levels and pAMPK/AMPK ratio, which correlated with muscle mass loss, indicating AMPK signaling and fatty acid oxidation activation. 1H NMR results suggested muscle proteolysis, with elevated serum levels of isoleucine, alanine, glycine, and threonine in T2D rats. Reduced muscle levels of all three branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) were also detected in T2D rats, suggesting enhanced BCAA oxidation/impaired uptake. T2D rats also exhibited elevated 3-hydroxybutyrate and acetate serum levels. No changes were observed in glucose, glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4), and 6-phosphofructokinase muscle type (PFKM) muscle levels, or ATP synthase activity.

These findings demonstrate an association between hyperglycemia and muscle loss, with muscle loss being associated with metabolic reprogramming toward the preferential utilization of non-glucose substrates, possibly to preserve energy homeostasis at the expense of protein maintenance.

artigos.titulo: Modern antidiabetic therapy in older adults with type 2 diabetes: evidence, best practice and a clinical pharmacist's framework
artigos.autores: Martinc B, Šabovič M, Janić M et al.
artigos.destaque: A structured medication review should integrate patient priorities, nutrition, physical performance, renal function, and hypoglycemia risk, followed by explicit monitoring and communication across care transitions. Prospective validation of this integrated framework in the oldest and most vulnerable populations is needed.

resumo.texto: Older adults with type 2 diabetes require treatment that balances cardiovascular and kidney protection against hypoglycemia, treatment burden, undernutrition, and functional vulnerability.

This narrative review considers PubMed-indexed literature and ClinicalTrials.gov records covering January 2010-October 2026, with targeted updating on 12 October 2026. It examines sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, tirzepatide, and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors. Age-stratified outcome evidence is distinguished from whole-trial results and the limited evidence in adults aged 80 years or older. Body-composition findings, neurodegenerative outcomes, kidney-protective treatment, and pharmacist-supported regimen modification are critically appraised.

Organ protection and glycemic simplification should be considered separately. Frailty is not synonymous with kidney impairment, and reductions in lean mass do not establish treatment-induced sarcopenia. Weight-neutral therapy remains useful when weight loss is undesirable. A structured medication review should integrate patient priorities, nutrition, physical performance, renal function, and hypoglycemia risk, followed by explicit monitoring and communication across care transitions. Prospective validation of this integrated framework in the oldest and most vulnerable populations is needed.

artigos.titulo: 12-month weight-loss trajectories and predictors of response to tirzepatide under individualized dosing: A multicenter real-world study
artigos.autores: Angelopoulos N, Fousteris E, Zianni D et al.
artigos.destaque: In a fully self-funded real-world setting, tirzepatide was associated with substantial weight loss and high documented treatment persistence over 12 months. Six-month weight-loss response was associated with the likelihood of achieving ≥20% weight loss at 12 months. These findings do not establish long-term weight maintenance beyond the observation period.

resumo.texto: Real-world evidence on 12-month treatment effectiveness and persistence with tirzepatide remains limited, particularly under individualized dosing and self-funded treatment conditions. We evaluated 12-month tirzepatide outcomes in routine clinical practice.

This was a multicenter, retrospective, observational real-world study including 249 adults with overweight or obesity treated with tirzepatide across 13 obesity practices in Greece. Treatment was entirely self-funded, and dose escalation was individualized rather than protocol driven. Treatment persistence, reasons for discontinuation, weight loss, dose trajectories, metabolic outcomes, and predictors of 12-month response were evaluated.

At 12 months, 170/249 patients (68.3%) remained on treatment, 64 (25.7%) had confirmed discontinuation, and 15 (6.0%) were lost to follow-up. Among patients with available weight measurements, mean weight loss was 19.9 ± 8.6% at 12 months, with 88.9%, 50.0%, and 27.2% achieving ≥10%, ≥20%, and ≥25% weight loss, respectively. Mean tirzepatide dose at 12 months was 9.71 mg. Among 179 patients assessed at both 6 and 12 months, 70.4% experienced >2% additional weight loss during the second 6 months, whereas 10.1% experienced >2% weight regain. Six-month percentage weight loss was not significantly associated with additional weight loss between months 6 and 12 after multivariable adjustment (β = -0.110, P = 0.135). Among 139 participants who had not achieved ≥20% weight loss at month 6, early response demonstrated moderate discrimination for achieving this cumulative threshold at month 12 (AUC 0.760, 95% bootstrap CI 0.675-0.837), with an adjusted OR of 1.34 per additional percentage point of 6-month weight loss (P < 0.001).

In a fully self-funded real-world setting, tirzepatide was associated with substantial weight loss and high documented treatment persistence over 12 months. Six-month weight-loss response was associated with the likelihood of achieving ≥20% weight loss at 12 months. These findings do not establish long-term weight maintenance beyond the observation period.

artigos.titulo: GLP-1-based therapies in cardiovascular disease: outcomes, mechanisms, and emerging clinical applications
artigos.autores: Jang R, Jang M, Ruan X et al.
artigos.destaque: Growing clinical evidence supports the use of GLP-1-based therapies beyond diabetes management, particularly in patients with cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, or obesity-related heart failure. Further studies will be needed to understand their mechanisms better, long-term safety, and optimal use in clinical practice.

resumo.texto: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have shown cardiovascular benefits beyond their established role in treating type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This review evaluates recent clinical evidence, potential mechanisms, and the expanding use of GLP-1-based therapies in cardiovascular disease.
We reviewed major randomized clinical trials assessing cardiovascular, kidney, and heart failure outcomes, along with related mechanistic studies and clinical guidelines published through July 2026.

Early trials, including LEADER, SUSTAIN-6, and REWIND, reported 12%-26% reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with T2DM. More recent trials have extended these findings to other populations. SELECT showed a 20% reduction in MACE among individuals with obesity and established cardiovascular disease but without diabetes, while FLOW demonstrated a 24% reduction in its primary kidney composite outcome. SOUL reported a 14% reduction in MACE with oral semaglutide, and SUMMIT showed a 38% reduction in cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure with tirzepatide. SURPASS-CVOT found tirzepatide to be noninferior, but not superior, to dulaglutide for MACE. These benefits likely involve several mechanisms beyond glucose lowering and weight loss, although gastrointestinal adverse effects still remain a concern.

Growing clinical evidence supports the use of GLP-1-based therapies beyond diabetes management, particularly in patients with cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, or obesity-related heart failure. Further studies will be needed to understand their mechanisms better, long-term safety, and optimal use in clinical practice.

artigos.titulo: Beyond LDL-C: A case-based review of complex Dyslipidemia
artigos.autores: Fanaropoulou NM, Varghese RT
artigos.destaque: The third demonstrates genetically confirmed familial hypercholesterolemia due to a pathogenic LDLR variant despite absent classic physical stigmata. Together, these cases support a phenotype-driven approach that integrates LDL-C, ApoB or LDL particle number, diet response, metabolic context, imaging, medication tolerance, and selective genetic testing to individualize dyslipidemia risk assessment and treatment.

resumo.texto: Dyslipidemia is clinically heterogeneous, and LDL-C alone may not fully capture atherogenic particle burden, metabolic risk, treatment response, or inherited disease. This case-based review presents three dyslipidemia phenotypes that illustrate common diagnostic and management challenges. The first case describes diet-sensitive LDL particle and lipoprotein insulin resistance changes despite LDL-C values near conventional targets in a patient with subclinical coronary atherosclerosis. The second highlights persistent low HDL-C and HDL particle number despite substantial LDL-C reduction with non-statin and incretin-era therapies in the setting of obesity and strong family history. The third demonstrates genetically confirmed familial hypercholesterolemia due to a pathogenic LDLR variant despite absent classic physical stigmata. Together, these cases support a phenotype-driven approach that integrates LDL-C, ApoB or LDL particle number, diet response, metabolic context, imaging, medication tolerance, and selective genetic testing to individualize dyslipidemia risk assessment and treatment.

artigos.titulo: How Well Are We Measuring Nausea? A Narrative Review of Patient-Reported Outcome Gaps in GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Obesity Trials
artigos.autores: Oria L, Darkhabani M
artigos.destaque: This observation gains further importance when considered alongside a second, less widely recognized fact: these same trial programmes devoted substantial methodological effort to developing and implementing a rigorous, quality of life measure specifically for obesity, the Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite Clinical Trials Version in addition to the Short Form-36 and EuroQol-5D. We argue that this asymmetry, more than any single mismeasurement, helps explain why real-world persistence with these agents falls so far short of what trial-reported tolerability figures would predict, and we outline what a fit-for-purpose metabolic nausea instrument would need to capture that adverse-event surveillance cannot.

resumo.texto: Across the full spectrum of major clinical trials evaluating glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) for obesity management, nausea consistently emerges as the most documented adverse effect, yet the methods used to capture it have received little scrutiny relative to their clinical importance. This narrative review traces how nausea was actually measured across the pivotal liraglutide (SCALE), semaglutide (STEP) and tirzepatide (SURMOUNT) obesity trial programmes, and situates those methods against the standards set out in the Consensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN) and the United States Food and Drug Administration's Patient-Focused Drug Development guidance. Across all three drug classes, nausea was ascertained through investigator-recorded, spontaneously reported adverse events coded to the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA), a pharmacovigilance framework built for a different purpose than symptom characterization, rather than through any validated, symptom-specific patient-reported outcome instrument. This observation gains further importance when considered alongside a second, less widely recognized fact: these same trial programmes devoted substantial methodological effort to developing and implementing a rigorous, quality of life measure specifically for obesity, the Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite Clinical Trials Version in addition to the Short Form-36 and EuroQol-5D. We argue that this asymmetry, more than any single mismeasurement, helps explain why real-world persistence with these agents falls so far short of what trial-reported tolerability figures would predict, and we outline what a fit-for-purpose metabolic nausea instrument would need to capture that adverse-event surveillance cannot.

artigos.titulo: Maternal mental health and its intergenerational transmission in-utero: a scoping review
artigos.autores: Seema M, Afoakwah C, Byrnes J
artigos.destaque: However, heterogeneity in exposure measurement, outcome definitions, and follow-up periods limited comparability and causal interpretation.Maternal mental health during pregnancy may be an important early-life and intergenerational exposure associated with offspring developmental trajectories, but observational evidence does not establish causal in-utero transmission. Stronger causal inference, longitudinal data linkage, and incorporation of economic and policy-relevant outcomes are priorities for future research.

resumo.texto: Maternal mental health during pregnancy is important for maternal wellbeing and offspring development. Prenatal depression, anxiety, stress, and psychological distress have been associated with offspring emotional, behavioural, cognitive, and mental health outcomes, but evidence remains dispersed across conditions, outcomes, and proposed mechanisms. This scoping review synthesises empirical evidence on maternal mental health during pregnancy as a potential intergenerational exposure, including potential in-utero pathways.Five databases (MEDLINE, Scopus, PsycInfo, CINAHL, and Embase) were searched from 1995 to 24 February 2026, following PRISMA-ScR guidance. Eligible sources of evidence examined maternal mental health during pregnancy in relation to postnatal offspring outcomes. Data were extracted using a structured framework and synthesised narratively. Twenty sources of evidence met the inclusion criteria. Across diverse designs and populations, prenatal depression, anxiety, stress, and psychological distress were commonly associated with adverse offspring outcomes, including emotional and behavioural difficulties, neurocognitive impairments, and increased risk of psychiatric conditions from childhood to adulthood. Several primary studies reported associations independent of traditional birth outcomes, consistent with potential in-utero pathways. Plausible mechanisms included stress-related neuroendocrine processes, inflammation, and epigenetic regulation. However, heterogeneity in exposure measurement, outcome definitions, and follow-up periods limited comparability and causal interpretation.Maternal mental health during pregnancy may be an important early-life and intergenerational exposure associated with offspring developmental trajectories, but observational evidence does not establish causal in-utero transmission. Stronger causal inference, longitudinal data linkage, and incorporation of economic and policy-relevant outcomes are priorities for future research.

artigos.titulo: When words reveal risk: a mixed-method study on autobiographical narratives of breast biopsy results disclosure as early markers of psychological distress
artigos.autores: Fortin J, Paquin A, Leblanc R et al.
artigos.destaque: In terms of form, all three dimensions were significantly associated to PTSS, while frequency and emotional intensity were significantly associated with non-specific distress. Early narrative markers following breast biopsy result disclosure were associated with psychological distress one month later.Conclusions: These findings highlight how memory processes associated with medical stressors can shape psychological outcomes and support their potential as screening tools for early identification of at-risk individuals.

resumo.texto: Background: Autobiographical memory theory suggests that how stressful events are encoded and recalled, particularly in terms of centrality to identity, emotional intensity, and retrieval frequency, can influence mental health. In breast cancer care, the disclosure of biopsy results may represent a psychologically impactful moment, regardless of diagnosis type.Objectives: This mixed-method study aimed to determine whether and how narrative features of breast biopsy result disclosure, analysed by both content (what was said) and form (how it was said), are associated with psychological distress one month later.Method: Sixty-eight participants were interviewed ≥7 days after receiving a breast biopsy result. Psychological distress was assessed one month later using the Distress Thermometer (non-specific distress) and the Impact of Event Scale-Revised (post-traumatic stress symptoms; PTSS). Narratives were coded using a theory-driven framework assessing centrality, emotional intensity, and recall frequency, applied separately to content and form.Results: While controlling for self-reported dissociation, linear regressions showed that for content, centrality and emotional intensity were significantly associated with PTSS, whereas only emotional intensity was significantly associated with non-specific distress. No substantial evidence of an association was found between frequency and any psychological outcome. In terms of form, all three dimensions were significantly associated to PTSS, while frequency and emotional intensity were significantly associated with non-specific distress. Early narrative markers following breast biopsy result disclosure were associated with psychological distress one month later.Conclusions: These findings highlight how memory processes associated with medical stressors can shape psychological outcomes and support their potential as screening tools for early identification of at-risk individuals.

artigos.titulo: Photography training and inhibitory control: ERP correlates and dissociable patterns from athletic training
artigos.autores: Guo C, Zhang Z, Deng Y et al.
artigos.destaque: Photography training was associated with a shift in the speed-accuracy trade‑off toward a greater emphasis on accuracy, as well as motor preparation and conflict monitoring-two core subprocesses of inhibitory control. Moreover, photographers and athletes showed improvements in inhibitory control through different neurocognitive pathways: while both groups showed enhanced motor preparation and conflict monitoring, athletes additionally exhibited enhanced cognitive preparation compared with photographers. This differential pattern may reflect athletes' need to respond to unpredictable, real‑time emergencies during competition.

resumo.texto: Long‑term engagement in professional behavioral training and the resulting behavioral changes are known to influence human cognition. The present study investigates whether and how photography training is associated with individuals' inhibitory control.
Fifteen photographers, 15 athletes, and 15 controls were recruited to complete a Go/Nogo task with concurrent electroencephalogram recording.

Behavioral results showed slower response times and fewer commission errors for both photographers and athletes compared with controls, with no significant difference between the two training groups. Event‑related potential analyses revealed more negative Bereitschaftspotential amplitudes and more positive N2 amplitudes for photographers and athletes than for controls, again with no significant difference between photographers and athletes. Furthermore, a more negative prefrontal negativity amplitude was observed for athletes than for both photographers and controls, whereas no significant difference was found between photographers and controls.

Photography training was associated with a shift in the speed-accuracy trade‑off toward a greater emphasis on accuracy, as well as motor preparation and conflict monitoring-two core subprocesses of inhibitory control. Moreover, photographers and athletes showed improvements in inhibitory control through different neurocognitive pathways: while both groups showed enhanced motor preparation and conflict monitoring, athletes additionally exhibited enhanced cognitive preparation compared with photographers. This differential pattern may reflect athletes' need to respond to unpredictable, real‑time emergencies during competition.

artigos.titulo: The role of polysomnography in Parkinson's disease: objective sleep assessment and clinical indications
artigos.autores: Zanatta A, de Almeida CMO, Della Coletta MV et al.
artigos.destaque: While home sleep apnea testing (HSAT, type 3) may be useful for selected cases with high suspicion of OSA, comprehensive in-laboratory (type 1) PSG provides superior diagnostic accuracy, particularly in patients with complex or overlapping sleep disturbances. Integrating objective sleep evaluation into routine PD management is crucial to identify treatable comorbidities, improve prognostic stratification, and optimize motor and non-motor outcomes.

resumo.texto: Sleep disorders (SDs) are highly prevalent in Parkinson's disease (PD), affecting up to 80% of patients during the disease and significantly contributing to impaired quality of life, cognitive decline, motor worsening, fall risk, and increased caregiver burden. Polysomnography (PSG) remains the gold standard for objective sleep assessment in PD and plays a central role in differential diagnosis and therapeutic planning. This review examines the spectrum of SDs identifiable by PSG, including rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD), obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), periodic limb movements in sleep, and alterations in sleep architecture. Video-polysomnography (v-PSG) is essential for confirming REM sleep without atonia (RWA), which is the electrophysiological hallmark of RBD and a recognized prodromal marker of synucleinopathies. Also, PSG quantifies the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), oxygen desaturation burden, and sleep fragmentation, parameters associated with cognitive impairment and disease progression. While home sleep apnea testing (HSAT, type 3) may be useful for selected cases with high suspicion of OSA, comprehensive in-laboratory (type 1) PSG provides superior diagnostic accuracy, particularly in patients with complex or overlapping sleep disturbances. Integrating objective sleep evaluation into routine PD management is crucial to identify treatable comorbidities, improve prognostic stratification, and optimize motor and non-motor outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Polysaccharide-based ionically active biomaterials for neuromorphic electronics: Molecular design, ion transport, and biointegrated memory functions
artigos.autores: Zaman W, Amin A, Raza MA
artigos.destaque: The resulting framework emphasizes carbohydrate chemistry while treating device metrics and environmental lifetime as linked design outcomes. Finally, this review outlines a prioritized set of experiments designed to determine if molecular descriptors can predict ionic relaxation and device behavior under matched fabrication and measurement conditions.

resumo.texto: Neuromorphic electronics integrate state storage with signal transformation; nevertheless, a device that exhibits resistive switching is not inherently a neuromorphic element, necessitating a thorough investigation into how specific material structures dictate these functions. In this context, cellulose, chitosan, pectin, and starch are chemically distinct polysaccharides characterized by functional groups (hydroxyl, amino, and carboxyl), chain organization, counterions, and water content that can influence ion transport and electrode reactions. This review examines evidence from glycan chemistry and hydration to ion transport, switching mechanisms, and measured memory or synaptic responses. We compare two-terminal cells with electrolyte-gated devices and distinguish direct experimental demonstrations from unproven mechanistic interpretations. We also identify cases where reported values are not comparable because of differences in polymer composition, electrodes, humidity, and pulse protocols. The resulting framework emphasizes carbohydrate chemistry while treating device metrics and environmental lifetime as linked design outcomes. Finally, this review outlines a prioritized set of experiments designed to determine if molecular descriptors can predict ionic relaxation and device behavior under matched fabrication and measurement conditions.

artigos.titulo: Imagination and Its Disorders in Mental State Examination
artigos.autores: Delcourt F, Nilsson LS, Rasmussen AR
artigos.destaque: Imagination is part of ordinary psychic life, but, in somewhat distorted forms, also an aspect of different key psychopathological concepts and hence of immediate clinical importance. In this review, we present principal findings from clinical psychopathological research examining basic disturbances of imagination in the schizophrenia spectrum, obsessive symptoms, and related phenomena in other mental disorders, including the suggested DSM-6 category of maladaptive daydreaming. We highlight methodological considerations in clinical work and suggest that an in-depth examination of anomalous imagination is of significant differential diagnostic and perhaps also therapeutic value.

resumo.texto: Imagination is part of ordinary psychic life, but, in somewhat distorted forms, also an aspect of different key psychopathological concepts and hence of immediate clinical importance. In this review, we present principal findings from clinical psychopathological research examining basic disturbances of imagination in the schizophrenia spectrum, obsessive symptoms, and related phenomena in other mental disorders, including the suggested DSM-6 category of maladaptive daydreaming. We highlight methodological considerations in clinical work and suggest that an in-depth examination of anomalous imagination is of significant differential diagnostic and perhaps also therapeutic value.

artigos.titulo: Consciousness and Its Disorders
artigos.autores: de Freitas GR, Fontenelle LF
artigos.destaque: Standardized behavioral assessment was developed for various scenarios, such as coma and delirium, and is superior to traditional assessment. The discovery that complementary tests can reveal the presence of consciousness in unresponsive patients opens a new avenue in the management of these patients.

resumo.texto: Disorders of consciousness are commonly encountered by neurologists and psychiatrists in clinical practice. It is important that these professionals are familiar with the various nomenclatures and different perspectives among the specialties. The bedside assessment of these patients can provide useful diagnostic and prognostic information. Standardized behavioral assessment was developed for various scenarios, such as coma and delirium, and is superior to traditional assessment. The discovery that complementary tests can reveal the presence of consciousness in unresponsive patients opens a new avenue in the management of these patients.

artigos.titulo: Construction and deformation mechanism of water-responsive starch-based shape memory emulsion gels
artigos.autores: Li R, Fu S, Han Y et al.
artigos.destaque: Macroscopic rheology, microscopic structure, and molecular spectroscopy results showed that the gel undergoes reversible structural evolution of "modulus increase-modulus decrease" and "dense-loose" during deformation, with hydrogen bonds acting as a key "molecular switch" driving the entire water-responsive shape memory cycle. This study provides a fundamental theoretical basis for designing food-derived hydrogels with shape memory properties.

resumo.texto: This study developed a water-responsive, starch-based shape memory emulsion gel (SMEG), systematically evaluated its moldability and shape memory performance, and thoroughly analyzed its structural mechanism. By comparing gels prepared from corn starch (CS), potato starch (PS), and tapioca starch (TS), it was found that PS-based shape memory emulsion gel containing 25% (m/v) PS (PS-SMEG (25)) exhibited moderate hardness, good flexibility, and a uniform, dense 3D network, enabling sharp folding without creases and demonstrating excellent mechanical properties. Under 50 °C, PS-SMEG (25) achieved shape fixity and recovery ratios of approximately 100% and stably completed 10 shape memory cycles. Mechanistic studies indicated that the water-regulated dynamic hydrogen-bonded network acts as the reversible phase, fixing the shape through dehydration-induced hydrogen bond strengthening and network densification, and triggering shape recovery via hydration-induced bond dissociation and network relaxation. Macroscopic rheology, microscopic structure, and molecular spectroscopy results showed that the gel undergoes reversible structural evolution of "modulus increase-modulus decrease" and "dense-loose" during deformation, with hydrogen bonds acting as a key "molecular switch" driving the entire water-responsive shape memory cycle. This study provides a fundamental theoretical basis for designing food-derived hydrogels with shape memory properties.

artigos.titulo: Moving Research Meetings from Data Updates to Cognitive Windows in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
artigos.autores: Prunuske AJ, Adams-Phillips LC
artigos.destaque: A case study illustrates how AI-generated analyses, combined with routine meeting dynamics, can obscure these dimensions when a trainee's reasoning is not made explicit. Intentionally structuring research meetings to surface these processes can help mentors more effectively assess trainee understanding and support the development of independent scientific judgment.

resumo.texto: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping how scientific work is conducted, enabling trainees to produce summaries, analyses, and interpretations with unprecedented speed and often plausible outputs. While these tools can enhance productivity, they may also obscure the reasoning processes that underlie scientific judgment. Research meetings have long been valuable spaces for discussing progress, troubleshooting experiments, and developing ideas, but in the era of generative AI they may serve an even more important role as critical touchpoints for assessing understanding. We propose that research meetings serve as critical "cognitive windows" into trainee understanding. Structured discussion can reveal three complementary dimensions of scientific reasoning: metacognitive calibration, conceptual explanation, and collaborative sensemaking. A case study illustrates how AI-generated analyses, combined with routine meeting dynamics, can obscure these dimensions when a trainee's reasoning is not made explicit. Intentionally structuring research meetings to surface these processes can help mentors more effectively assess trainee understanding and support the development of independent scientific judgment.

artigos.titulo: Selective Cognitive and Affective Benefits of 3D-Printed Bacteriophage T4 Models in High School Molecular Biology Instruction: A Quasi-Experimental Study
artigos.autores: Xu L, Li Y, Wang L et al.
artigos.destaque: Affective outcomes significantly favored the model condition, including lesson enjoyment (p = 0.038), model construction interest (p = 0.028), perceived knowledge mastery (p = 0.033), perceived instructional utility (p = 0.028), and modeling skill need (p = 0.049). These findings suggest that curriculum-aligned 3D model-based instruction selectively enhances representational competence for spatially complex concepts and improves situational affective engagement.

resumo.texto: Teaching abstract molecular concepts poses persistent challenges in high school biology education. This study evaluated a custom-developed three-dimensional (3D) bacteriophage T4 model for teaching the Hershey-Chase experiment in a Grade 11 classroom. Using a quasi-experimental design, 92 students were assigned to either model-based instruction (n = 46) incorporating hands-on assembly of a disassemblable 3D-printed phage model, or conventional instruction (n = 46). Pre- and post-intervention questionnaires assessed conceptual understanding and affective outcomes. ANCOVA revealed no significant overall cognitive difference between groups, F(1, 89) = 1.42, p = 0.237. However, item-level analysis showed the model group significantly outperformed on structural component identification (52.2% vs 26.1%, p = 0.018, ϕ = 0.27). Affective outcomes significantly favored the model condition, including lesson enjoyment (p = 0.038), model construction interest (p = 0.028), perceived knowledge mastery (p = 0.033), perceived instructional utility (p = 0.028), and modeling skill need (p = 0.049). These findings suggest that curriculum-aligned 3D model-based instruction selectively enhances representational competence for spatially complex concepts and improves situational affective engagement.

artigos.titulo: Oral Protein Fibril Microgels with Gastric Stability and Intestinal Targeting Enhance Capsaicin Bioavailability for Effective Obesity Prevention
artigos.autores: Zhang H, Cui Y, Wu K et al.
artigos.destaque: Both microgels modulated gut microbiota homeostasis, with FPIFM/Cap uniquely enriching Akkermansia, potentially due to its high arginine content and its stable fibrillar structure. This work provides a proof of concept for upcycling agricultural processing byproduct proteins into high-performance biomaterials for mitigating metabolic diseases.

resumo.texto: To address the susceptibility of protein fibrils to pepsin degradation, this study proposed a fibril-to-microgel hierarchical assembly strategy, where flexible whey protein isolate fibrils (WPIF) and rigid flaxseed protein isolate fibrils (FPIF) were in situ self-cross-linked into microgels via a W/O emulsion template, followed by capsaicin (Cap) loading. Both microgels exhibited high gastric stability and intestinal response release properties. Compared with WPIF-based microgels (WPIFM), FPIF-based microgels (FPIFM) exhibited a more sustained intestinal digestion profile, leading to a higher Cap bioavailability. In high-fat-diet-induced obese mice, Cap-loaded microgels (WPIFM/Cap and FPIFM/Cap) effectively prevented metabolic disorders, as evidenced by reduced lipid accumulation, hepatic steatosis, and pro-inflammatory cytokines, with FPIFM/Cap demonstrating the highest protective efficacy. Both microgels modulated gut microbiota homeostasis, with FPIFM/Cap uniquely enriching Akkermansia, potentially due to its high arginine content and its stable fibrillar structure. This work provides a proof of concept for upcycling agricultural processing byproduct proteins into high-performance biomaterials for mitigating metabolic diseases.

artigos.titulo: Resistance Exercise for Body Composition in Children Who Are Overweight or Obese
artigos.autores: Rech A, Radaelli R, Turella DJP et al.
artigos.destaque: Resistance exercise improves body composition in children and adolescents who are overweight or obese.

resumo.texto: Childhood obesity is a major public health issue linked to long-term metabolic disorders. Although aerobic exercise is often emphasized, evidence suggests that resistance exercise may also improve body composition in youth who are overweight or obese. This study aims to examine the effects of resistance-based exercise programs on fat mass, lean mass, body fat percentage, body weight, and body mass index in children and adolescents who are overweight or obese and to identify potential moderators of these effects.

Eight electronic databases and 3 gray literature databases were searched from inception to May 2025. Randomized controlled trials involving resistance-based exercise programs in children and adolescents classified as overweight or obese were included. Data were extracted independently in duplicate, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed.

Twenty-four trials (n = 846 participants) were included. Resistance exercise significantly reduced fat mass (-2.06 kg), body fat percentage (-2.1%), and body weight (-1.3 kg), and increased lean mass (+0.8 kg), with small-to-moderate effect sizes (standardized mean difference = -0.35 to 0.33; P < .05). No significant moderating effects of age, sex, duration, volume, or intensity were identified.
Resistance exercise improves body composition in children and adolescents who are overweight or obese.

artigos.titulo: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Reproductive Health: Implications for Contraception, Fertility, and Pregnancy
artigos.autores: Porterfield F, Mulligan J, Salim K et al.
artigos.destaque: Most GLP-1 RAs do not significantly affect oral contraceptive pharmacokinetics, although tirzepatide may require temporary backup contraception. Evidence regarding fertility outcomes and pregnancy safety remains limited.

resumo.texto: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have rapidly expanded in use for the treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes, including among women of reproductive age. Emerging evidence suggests that GLP-1 signaling may influence reproductive physiology through central effects on the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and indirect metabolic pathways. In women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), GLP-1 RAs improve insulin resistance and androgen profiles and may improve menstrual regularity. Most GLP-1 RAs do not significantly affect oral contraceptive pharmacokinetics, although tirzepatide may require temporary backup contraception. Evidence regarding fertility outcomes and pregnancy safety remains limited.

artigos.titulo: Visual behaviour in acute stress during simulated and on-road driving
artigos.autores: Bakhchina A, Arutyunova K, Burashnikov E et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings support gaze-derived measures as candidate indicators of changes in visual behaviour related to acute stress during driving, while highlighting the importance of considering acute stress as a phased process. They also indicate that multimodal context-aware validation is needed for translation into real-time driver state monitoring and safety-relevant assistance applications.

resumo.texto: Driving frequently exposes individuals to conditions triggering acute stress, but its effects on drivers' visual behaviour remain insufficiently understood. We used the heart rate dynamics to label acute stress episodes in recordings from 881 participants who performed simulated and on-road driving. Considering acute stress as a phased process, we analysed eye gaze metrics during stress activation and stress resistance periods. In simulation, stress activation was accompanied by more frequent and shorter fixations, greater fixation area, higher stationary gaze entropy, and lower gaze transition entropy. In on-road driving, significant effects were more selective, with the most consistent changes observed for the horizontal diameter of fixation area and entropy-based gaze measures. During stress resistance, many measures partially returned toward non-stress levels, suggesting a transition from initial reactivity toward stabilisation. These findings support gaze-derived measures as candidate indicators of changes in visual behaviour related to acute stress during driving, while highlighting the importance of considering acute stress as a phased process. They also indicate that multimodal context-aware validation is needed for translation into real-time driver state monitoring and safety-relevant assistance applications.

artigos.titulo: Filial Caregiving Burnout in the Chinese Cultural Context: Conceptualization, Scale Development, and Longitudinal Validation
artigos.autores: Zhou B, Li Y, Wang W et al.
artigos.destaque: Longitudinally, higher baseline FCB significantly predicted lower subsequent family and job performance and higher subsequent family undermining and counterproductive work behavior. Moving beyond generic burden metrics, the FCB Scale captures relational and value-laden aspects of filial caregiving burnout and provides a multidimensional tool for assessing burnout experiences among adult-child caregivers.

resumo.texto: In China, the Confucian norm of filial piety has historically framed eldercare as an important responsibility of adult children. Amid rapid population aging, caregivers frequently experience profound exhaustion. While traditional assessments capture caregiver burden, they may be less sensitive to role- and culture-embedded experiences such as emotional detachment, relational strain, and value dissonance arising when caregiving realities conflict with internalized obligations. Although the phenomenon of Filial Caregiving Burnout (FCB) has been recently identified, it lacks a formal theoretical definition and measurement tool. To address this limitation, we conceptualize FCB and develop a culturally grounded, multidimensional scale. Using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, qualitative interviews first generated the initial item pool. Subsequent quantitative evaluations across three independent caregiver samples (N = 1653) refined and validated the structure via exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, alongside measurement invariance testing. Finally, a two-wave longitudinal design assessed predictive validity. The finalized 17-item FCB Scale features a robust three-factor structure: physical and mental exhaustion, relational detachment, and dysregulation of filial piety value. It demonstrated excellent internal consistency (α = 0.948), acceptable model fit, and measurement invariance across gender and Hukou type. Longitudinally, higher baseline FCB significantly predicted lower subsequent family and job performance and higher subsequent family undermining and counterproductive work behavior. Moving beyond generic burden metrics, the FCB Scale captures relational and value-laden aspects of filial caregiving burnout and provides a multidimensional tool for assessing burnout experiences among adult-child caregivers.

artigos.titulo: Pathways, consequences, and community-proposed responses to school discontinuation in rural eastern Uganda: a qualitative study
artigos.autores: Lee YJ, Edwards MD, Carrier AC et al.
artigos.destaque: School discontinuation in rural eastern Uganda is experienced as a cumulative process with cascading social, psychological, and economic consequences rather than a single educational event. Community members identified multi-domain responses addressing emotional recovery, livelihoods, and social reintegration together. These findings highlight the value of centering community perspectives when designing integrated interventions for young people affected by school discontinuation.

resumo.texto: Education is a social determinant of health, and incomplete schooling is associated with poorer sexual and reproductive health, psychosocial distress, and reduced economic opportunity. In Africa, many young people leave school before completing their educational cycle, yet qualitative evidence on the social and health consequences of discontinuation and on what affected communities view as appropriate responses remains limited.
To explore perspectives on the pathways, consequences, and proposed responses to school discontinuation in rural eastern Uganda.

This qualitative descriptive study drew on 59 in-depth interviews with young adults who had discontinued school (n = 15), family members (n = 14), teachers (n = 15), and community leaders (n = 15), purposively sampled with community assistance in Buyende and Kamuli districts in eastern Uganda. Data were analyzed using framework analysis.

Three themes emerged. First, participants described discontinuation as driven by intersecting household poverty, school-level barriers, and gendered pressures including early marriage, teenage pregnancy, and sexual exploitation. Second, discontinuation was followed by psychological distress, social stigma, economic marginalization, and heightened vulnerability, particularly for young women. Third, participants proposed complementary supports spanning counseling and mentorship, vocational training and economic empowerment, and interpersonal and community-based engagement.

School discontinuation in rural eastern Uganda is experienced as a cumulative process with cascading social, psychological, and economic consequences rather than a single educational event. Community members identified multi-domain responses addressing emotional recovery, livelihoods, and social reintegration together. These findings highlight the value of centering community perspectives when designing integrated interventions for young people affected by school discontinuation.

artigos.titulo: Germany's Verschickungskinder: parent-child separation and mental health
artigos.autores: Yim IS, Rivera PJ, von Majewski K et al.
artigos.destaque: Bivariate comparisons among the sent-away children indicated that younger age at separation was associated with more depressive symptoms, repeated separations with higher stress overload, and very negative memories with all three outcomes; no sex differences were observed. When entered simultaneously in regression models, emotional memory of the event was the only sent-away characteristic associated with depressive (p = .02) and anxiety symptoms (p = .009).Conclusions: Findings highlight the potential long-term mental health relevance of the sent-away experience, particularly among those with very negative memories of their experiences.

resumo.texto: Background: Parent-child separations have been associated with adverse health and well-being, with most research focusing on prolonged separations driven by war, famine or disease. Verschickungskinder ('sent-away children') - the eight to twelve million German children who, in the decades following World War II, were separated from their families for several weeks to stay in so-called children's health resorts - represent a largely overlooked case of short-term separation. Despite growing recognition of adverse experiences and abuse in these settings, little is known about the long-term mental health of this population or which characteristics of the sent-away experience are associated with these outcomes.Objective: To examine whether sent-away children show more depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and stress overload compared with peers, and to identify which characteristics of the sent-away experience are associated with these outcomes.Method: An anonymous online survey was conducted with 334 sent-away children and 77 participants in a convenience comparison group (M = 61.1 yrs.; 72.7% female). Linear regression models, adjusting for ACEs and sociodemographics, examined group differences and associations between characteristics of the sent-away experience (age at separation, sex, number of separations, emotional memory) and these outcomes.Results: Sent-away children reported more depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and stress overload than comparison participants (all p < .001). Bivariate comparisons among the sent-away children indicated that younger age at separation was associated with more depressive symptoms, repeated separations with higher stress overload, and very negative memories with all three outcomes; no sex differences were observed. When entered simultaneously in regression models, emotional memory of the event was the only sent-away characteristic associated with depressive (p = .02) and anxiety symptoms (p = .009).Conclusions: Findings highlight the potential long-term mental health relevance of the sent-away experience, particularly among those with very negative memories of their experiences.

artigos.titulo: Vitamin D deficiency and oral health in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA): A public health perspective
artigos.autores: Alyafei N
artigos.destaque: Vitamin D deficiency should be considered a potentially modifiable component of oral health promotion rather than a standalone cause or treatment of oral diseases. Integrating nutritional strategies with established oral disease prevention programs may strengthen public health efforts throughout the MENA. Longitudinal studies and randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify causal relationships and guide evidence-based policy and clinical practice.

resumo.texto: To examine evidence regarding the relationship between vitamin D deficiency and oral health in Middle East and North Africa (MENA) populations, where vitamin D deficiency and oral diseases remain important public health challenges, emphasizing biological mechanisms, dental caries, periodontal diseases, other oral outcomes, and public health implications.

This narrative review synthesizes systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and regional public health reports identified in electronic databases and through reference screening, focusing on vitamin D deficiency, oral health outcomes, biological mechanisms, and preventive strategies relevant to MENA populations.

Evidence suggests that vitamin D contributes to oral health through tooth mineralization, calcium and phosphate homeostasis, immune regulation, antimicrobial defense, inflammation control, and alveolar bone maintenance. Low vitamin D status has been associated with dental caries, periodontal diseases, developmental enamel defects, alveolar bone loss, impaired wound healing, and oral mucosal conditions. Evidence regarding oral cancer remains insufficient to establish a relationship. Periodontal disease shares inflammatory and metabolic pathways with systemic conditions, particularly diabetes, and emerging evidence suggests a possible association with cognitive decline and dementia. However, evidence remains heterogeneous and predominantly observational; therefore, causality has not been established. The coexistence of vitamin D deficiency and a high oral disease burden in MENA supports integrated public health strategies based on shared risk factors and the Common Risk Factor Approach.

Vitamin D deficiency should be considered a potentially modifiable component of oral health promotion rather than a standalone cause or treatment of oral diseases. Integrating nutritional strategies with established oral disease prevention programs may strengthen public health efforts throughout the MENA. Longitudinal studies and randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify causal relationships and guide evidence-based policy and clinical practice.

artigos.titulo: TPPU, a soluble epoxide hydrolase inhibitor, mitigates Aβ-induced neurotoxicity via dual modulation of mitochondrial stabilization and JNK suppression
artigos.autores: Song J, He A, Li S et al.
artigos.destaque: Western blot analysis confirmed that TPPU pretreatment suppressed the phosphorylation of JNK, thereby contributing to its anti-apoptotic effects. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that TPPU attenuates Aβ-induced neurotoxicity via dual mechanisms-restoring mitochondrial function and suppressing JNK activation-highlighting its potential as a therapeutic agent for AD.

resumo.texto: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, primarily driven by β-amyloid (Aβ) aggregation and neuronal apoptosis. This study aims to investigate the neuroprotective effects of soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) inhibition against Aβ-induced cytotoxicity in PC-12 cells, focusing on cell viability, apoptosis, and the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) signaling pathway. Western blotting and fluorometric assays revealed elevated sEH expression and activity in Aβ1-42-treated PC-12 cells compared to untreated controls. Treatment with N-[1-(1-Oxopropyl)-4-piperidinyl]-N'-[4-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl]urea (TPPU), a potent sEH inhibitor, significantly attenuated Aβ-induced apoptosis in PC-12 cells and enhanced cell viability. These findings were corroborated by CCK-8 assays and flow cytometry analyses. Furthermore, TPPU reversed Aβ-induced cleaved Caspase-3 dysregulation and restored mitochondrial membrane potential. Notably, exogenous administration of epoxyeicosatrienoic acids partially mimicked the protective effects of TPPU, primarily by preserving mitochondrial function. Western blot analysis confirmed that TPPU pretreatment suppressed the phosphorylation of JNK, thereby contributing to its anti-apoptotic effects. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that TPPU attenuates Aβ-induced neurotoxicity via dual mechanisms-restoring mitochondrial function and suppressing JNK activation-highlighting its potential as a therapeutic agent for AD.

artigos.titulo: Association Between Plasma N-Terminal Tau, Cognitive Decline, and Neurodegeneration in the ADNI Cohort
artigos.autores: Rao Y, Liu L, Ostaszewski BL et al.
artigos.destaque: Higher NT1 levels were associated with higher levels of plasma biomarkers, including NULISA-based brain-derived (BD) plasma pTau (BD-pTau181, BD-pTau217, BD-pTau231: p's < 5.01 × 10-6) and Simoa-Based pTau181 (p < 4.51 × 10-15) and neurofilament light chain (p < 5.34 × 10-7). Plasma NT1 may be useful in assessing amyloid-dependent cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.

resumo.texto: Blood-based biomarkers offer a cost-effective, minimally invasive alternative to neuroimaging and CSF biomarkers. Newly developed fluid biomarkers, including the N-terminal tau fragment (NT1), show promise for identifying individuals at risk for Alzheimer disease (AD) and for monitoring disease progression. Here, we determine whether NT1 levels are associated with key clinical and biomarker measures in a large, well-characterized cohort.

Participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort with available plasma NT1, β-amyloid (Aβ)-PET, MRI, and clinical measures (Clinical Dementia Rating) were included in this observational study. NT1 was measured using the Quanterix Simoa HD-X platform. PET, MRI, clinical, and other plasma measures were obtained using established ADNI procedures. A subset also had NULISA-based plasma measures of amyloid and tau and tau-PET assessed. Linear regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to assess cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between NT1 and clinical or biomarker measures, adjusting for relevant covariates. Multivariable-adjusted Cox regression was performed to evaluate the association between baseline NT1 levels and risk of clinically diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD. Mediation analysis was conducted to examine whether hippocampal atrophy mediates the relationship between NT1 and memory decline. Spearman correlations were used to examine continuous relationships between plasma NT1 and continuous fluid and neuroimaging markers.

A total of 755 participants (mean age: 72.9 [7.0], female: 375 [50%]) were included in the study. Plasma NT1 levels were elevated in MCI/AD individuals (BMCI/AD [SE] = 0.09 [0.022], p = 1.98 × 10-4) and were cross-sectionally associated with worse memory performance (B [SE] = -0.25 [0.09], p = 0.005). Aβ moderated the association between elevated NT1 and greater cognitive decline across multiple domains (memory: B [SE] = -0.17 [0.074], p = 0.022; executive function: B [SE] = -0.24 [0.082], p = 0.004; language: B [SE] = -0.21 [0.075], p = 0.006). NT1 levels were negatively associated with hippocampal volume (B [SE] = -264.49 [125.99], p = 0.036) and predicted longitudinal atrophy (B [SE] = -42.00 [16.90], p = 0.013). Accelerated hippocampal atrophy largely mediated the association between higher baseline NT1 level and greater memory decline (B [95% CI]indirect effect = -0.082 [-0.135 to -0.03], p = 0.003, B [95% CI]proportion mediated = 70.1% [32.6%-155.3%], p = 0.004). Higher NT1 levels were associated with higher levels of plasma biomarkers, including NULISA-based brain-derived (BD) plasma pTau (BD-pTau181, BD-pTau217, BD-pTau231: p's < 5.01 × 10-6) and Simoa-Based pTau181 (p < 4.51 × 10-15) and neurofilament light chain (p < 5.34 × 10-7).
Plasma NT1 may be useful in assessing amyloid-dependent cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.
